'''Ahmad Kadar Brooks''' (born March 14, 1984) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at the [[Virginia Cavaliers football|University of Virginia]] and was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the third round of the 2006 [[NFL supplemental draft]]. Brooks also played for the [[San Francisco 49ers]] and [[Green Bay Packers]].

==Early life==
Brooks attended [[C. D. Hylton High School]] in [[Woodbridge, Virginia]], where he helped lead two [[VHSL]] state championships as a freshman and sophomore. Becoming recognized, Brooks' team was nationally ranked, going 40–0 before losing to [[Potomac High School (Virginia)|Potomac High School]] of [[Woodbridge, Virginia]], during his junior season in 2000. Brooks injured his ankle during his junior season, which sidelined him that year. His senior season in 2001 was very productive—Brooks had 202 tackles (144 solo), including 34 for loss, and rushed for 848 yards and 10 touchdowns while averaging 12.6 yards per carry. The semifinal loss to [[Thomas Dale High School]] of [[Chester, Virginia]], in 2001 was the only loss in which he played. Brooks was named the ''[[USA Today]]'' national high school defensive player of the year after the 2001 season. He also participated in the 2002 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] game.

Considered a five-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], Brooks was listed as the number-one middle linebacker in the nation in 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Brooks, 2002 Outside Linebacker, Virginia |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/ahmad-brooks-31613?view=pv |access-date=2025-03-29 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref>

==College career==
Following high school, Brooks spent a semester at [[Hargrave Military Academy]] in [[Chatham, Virginia]], a military [[postgraduate year|post-graduate]] school, before enrolling in the [[University of Virginia]] in the winter of 2003. He earned a starting position on the [[Virginia Cavaliers football]] team as a freshman and finished the year with a career-high and team-leading 117 [[Tackle (football move)|tackles]]. Brooks also had four [[Quarterback sack|sacks]], six [[Pass defensed|passes defensed]], 10 tackles for loss, and 15 quarterback pressures. He had a career-high 12 tackles against [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh]] in the [[Continental Tire Bowl]], including a key stop early in the contest to complete a goal-line stand.

During his sophomore year at the University of Virginia, Brooks was one of three [[Butkus Award]] finalists, awarded annually to the best college linebacker in the country. He played in 12 games, earning [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors after totaling a team-leading 90 tackles with eight sacks, two interceptions, 11 quarterback pressures, and 10 tackles for loss. Brooks earned [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] defensive lineman of the week honors for his performance against the [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland Terrapins]]. Following his sophomore campaign, Brooks underwent knee surgery.

Brooks missed the first half of his junior year while rehabilitating his knee. Brooks finished the year with 27 tackles (10 solo), a sack, four pass deflections, and five quarterback pressures in only six games. Brooks was dismissed from the Cavalier football team following the 2005 season due to issues off the field.

==Professional career==

===Cincinnati Bengals===

====2006 season====
Brooks entered the [[NFL supplemental draft]] following his junior season at Virginia and was selected by the Bengals in the third round on July 13, 2006.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2006 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2006/draft.htm |access-date=May 8, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Brooks made his NFL debut during a Week 3 28–20 road victory over the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], but recorded no statistics.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609240pit.htm |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers - September 24th, 2006 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 28, 2006}}</ref> In the next game against the [[New England Patriots]], Brooks recorded his first NFL tackle during the 38–13 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610010cin.htm |title=New England Patriots at Cincinnati Bengals - October 1st, 2006 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 5, 2006}}</ref> Following a Week 5 bye, the Bengals went on the road to face the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In that game, Brooks made his first NFL start and had 11 tackles and a pass deflection during the narrow 14–13 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610150tam.htm |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers - October 15th, 2006 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 20, 2006}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Brooks recorded five tackles, a pass deflection, and his first NFL sack as the Bengals won by a score of 17–14.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610220pit.htm |title=Carolina Panthers at Cincinnati Bengals - October 22nd, 2006 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 25, 2006}}</ref> The following week against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], he had six tackles in the narrow 29–27 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200610290cin.htm |title=Carolina Panthers at Cincinnati Bengals - October 29th, 2006 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 1, 2006}}</ref>

Brooks finished his rookie season with 31 tackles, two passes defended, and a sack in 11 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrooAh21/gamelog/2006 |title=Ahmad Brooks 2006 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 31, 2006}}</ref>

====2007 season====
During the season opening 27–20 victory over the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Brooks was the starting middle linebacker and recorded six tackles and a strip-sack.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200609100cin.htm |title=Baltimore Ravens at Cincinnati Bengals - September 10th, 2007 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 13, 2007}}</ref> However, in the first series of the next game against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Brooks tore his groin muscle, prematurely ending his season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sports.aol.com/nfl-players/ahmad-brooks/8006 |title=Ahmad Brooks profile |work=Sports.aol.com |access-date=November 28, 2008}}</ref> Brooks was placed on [[injured reserve]] on November 7, 2007.<ref name="m246">{{cite web | title=Bengals LB Brooks out for season, will need surgery | website=NFL.com | date=2007-11-07 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bengals-lb-brooks-out-for-season-will-need-surgery-09000d5d803fc185 | access-date=2024-12-21}}</ref>

On August 30, 2008, Brooks was waived by the Bengals during final roster cuts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://scout.com/nfl/packers/Article/Packers-Look-to-Ahmad-Brooks-to-Bolster-OLB-Corps-106562367 |title=Packers Look to Ahmad Brooks to Bolster OLB Corps |last=Huber |first=Bill |website=Packers Report |access-date=September 5, 2008}}</ref>

====2014 season====
During the season-opening 28–17 road victory over the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Brooks recorded a tackle and his first sack of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201409070dal.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys - September 7th, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 9, 2014}}</ref> During Week 6 against the Rams on ''Monday Night Football'', Brooks had five tackles and two sacks in the 31–17 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201410130ram.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at St. Louis Rams - October 13th, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 16, 2014}}</ref>

During a Week 10 27–24 overtime road victory over the Saints, Brooks recorded three tackles along with a strip-sack in overtime to help set up the game-winning field goal.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201211250nor.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at New Orleans Saints - November 9th, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 12, 2014}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Redskins, he had three tackles, a pass deflection, and a fumble recovery in the 17–13 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411230sfo.htm |title=Washington Redskins at San Francisco 49ers - November 23rd, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 25, 2014}}</ref> In the next game against the Seahawks on [[NFL on Thanksgiving Day|Thanksgiving]], Brooks recorded four tackles, a pass deflection, and a sack during the 19–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201411270sfo.htm |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers - November 27th, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 27, 2014}}</ref> Brooks made his final appearance of the season in Week 15 against the Seahawks. During that game, he had three tackles and a sack as the 49ers lost on the road by a score of 17–7.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201412140sea.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks - December 14th, 2014 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 19, 2014}}</ref>

Brooks finished the 2014 season with 30 tackles, six sacks, three pass deflections, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 13 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrooAh21/gamelog/2014 |title=Ahmad Brooks 2014 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=January 1, 2015}}</ref>

====2015 season====
During a Week 4 17–3 loss to the Packers, Brooks recorded five tackles and his first sack of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201401190sea.htm |title=Green Bay Packers at San Francisco 49ers - October 4th, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 9, 2015}}</ref> Three weeks later against the Seahawks, Brooks had five tackles and sacked [[Russell Wilson]] twice in the 20–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201510220sfo.htm |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers - October 22nd, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref>

During a Week 11 29–13 road loss to the Seahawks, Brooks recorded three tackles and a sack.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220sea.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks - November 22nd, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 25, 2015}}</ref> Three weeks later against the Browns, he had five tackles and recovered a fumble in the 24–10 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512130sea.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Cleveland Browns - December 13th, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 18, 2015}}</ref> In the next game against his former team, the Bengals, Brooks recorded five tackles and a sack during the 24–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512200sfo.htm |title=Cincinnati Bengals at San Francisco 49ers - December 20th, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 24, 2015}}</ref> The following week against the [[2015 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]], he had three tackles and 1.5 sacks in the 32–17 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201512270det.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Detroit Lions - December 27th, 2015 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 31, 2015}}</ref>

Brooks finished the 2015 season with 42 tackles, 6.5 sacks, a fumble recovery, and a pass deflection in 14 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrooAh21/gamelog/2015 |title=Ahmad Brooks 2015 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=January 8, 2016}}</ref>

====2016 season====
During the season-opening 28–0 shutout victory over the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Brooks recorded three tackles and his first sack of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609120sfo.htm |title=Los Angeles Rams at San Francisco 49ers - September 12th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 14, 2016}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Seahawks, he had four tackles, two pass deflections, and a sack in the 37–18 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609250sea.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks - September 25th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 28, 2016}}</ref>

During a Week 7 34–17 loss to the Buccaneers, Brooks recorded five tackles and 0.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610230sfo.htm |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at San Francisco 49ers - October 23rd, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=October 24, 2016}}</ref> During a Week 11 30–17 loss to the Patriots, he had two tackles and sacked [[Tom Brady]] once.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610230sfo.htm |title=New England Patriots at San Francisco 49ers - November 20th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 21, 2016}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Miami Dolphins]], Brooks recorded four tackles and 0.5 sacks during the 31–24 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201611270mia.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Miami Dolphins - November 27th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 2, 2016}}</ref> The following week against the [[Chicago Bears]], he had three tackles and a sack in the 26–6 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612040chi.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Chicago Bears - December 4th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 9, 2016}}</ref>

During a Week 15 41–13 road loss to the Falcons, Brooks had four tackles and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612180atl.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Atlanta Falcons - December 18th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 22, 2016}}</ref> In the next game against the Rams, he recorded five tackles, a pass deflection, and a sack during the narrow 22–21 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201612240ram.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams - December 24th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 28, 2016}}</ref>

Brooks finished the 2016 season with 53 tackles, six sacks, four pass deflections, and a forced fumble in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrooAh21/gamelog/2016 |title=Ahmad Brooks 2016 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=January 4, 2017}}</ref>

Brooks was released by the 49ers on August 25, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=49ers Release LB Ahmad Brooks|url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/49ers-Release-LB-Ahmad-Brooks/707117f6-b29e-4412-83f9-6e5a79d1d698?sf109264661=1|website=49ers.com|date=August 25, 2017}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On September 3, 2017, Brooks signed a one-year deal with the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign LB Brooks, claim LB Odom, place OL Barclay on IR|url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-lb-brooks-claim-lb-odom-place-ol-barclay-on-ir-19311378|website=Packers.com|date=September 3, 2017}}</ref>

Brooks made his Packers debut during the season-opening 17–9 victory over the Seahawks, recording one tackle.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100gnb.htm |title=Seattle Seahawks at Green Bay Packers - September 10th, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> Two weeks later against his former team, the Bengals, he had two tackles and his first sack of the season during the 27–24 overtime victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709240gnb.htm |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Green Bay Packers - September 24th, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=September 30, 2017}}</ref> During a Week 11 23–0 shutout loss to the Ravens, Brooks recorded three tackles and 0.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711190gnb.htm |title=Baltimore Ravens at Green Bay Packers - November 19th, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 21, 2017}}</ref>

Brooks finished the 2017 season with 19 tackles, 1.5 sacks, and two pass deflections in 12 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BrooAh21/gamelog/2017 |title=Ahmad Brooks 2017 Game Log |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=January 1, 2018}}</ref>

{{Short description|American football player (born 1986)}} {{for|the college football quarterback|Ahmad Bradshaw (quarterback)}} {{Use mdy dates|date=May 2026}} {{Infobox NFL biography | name = Ahmad Bradshaw | image = Ahmad bradshaw.jpg | caption = Bradshaw with the New York Giants after winning
[[Super Bowl XLVI]] in 2012 | current_team = | number = 44 | position = [[Running back]] | birth_date = {{birth date and age|1986|03|19}} | birth_place = [[Bluefield, Virginia]], U.S. | height_ft = 5 | height_in = 10 | weight_lbs = 217 | high_school = [[Graham High School (Bluefield, Virginia)|Graham]] (Bluefield) | college = [[Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall]] (2004–2006) | draftyear = 2007 | draftround = 7 | draftpick = 250 | pastteams = * [[New York Giants]] ({{NFL Year|2007}}–{{NFL Year|2012}}) * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|2013}}–{{NFL Year|2015}}) | status = | highlights = * 2× [[Super Bowl champion]] ([[Super Bowl XLII|XLII]], [[Super Bowl XLVI|XLVI]]) * [[New York Giants#Top 100 greatest Giants of all-time|84th greatest New York Giant of all-time]] * 2× All-[[Conference USA]] (2005, 2006) | statlabel1 = [[Carry (American football)|Rushing attempts]] | statvalue1 = 1,083 | statlabel2 = [[Rushing yards]] | statvalue2 = 4,928 | statlabel3 = [[Touchdown|Rushing touchdowns]] | statvalue3 = 36 | statlabel4 = [[Reception (American football)|Receptions]] | statvalue4 = 187 | statlabel5 = [[Receiving yards]] | statvalue5 = 1,493 | statlabel6 = [[Touchdown|Receiving touchdowns]] | statvalue6 = 12 | pfr = BradAh00 }} '''Ahmad Bradshaw''' (born March 19, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Marshall Thundering Herd football|Marshall Thundering Herd]]. Bradshaw was selected in the seventh round of the [[2007 NFL draft]] by the [[New York Giants]]. He is a two-time [[Super Bowl]] champion, winning Super Bowls [[Super Bowl XLII|XLII]] and [[Super Bowl XLVI|XLVI]] as a member of the Giants, defeating the [[New England Patriots]] each time. He was the leading rusher in each game, becoming one of eight running backs in NFL history to be the leading rusher in two Super Bowls. ==Early life== Ahmad Bradshaw was born in [[Bluefield, Virginia]] to Diana Davis and James Bradshaw, and played [[high school football]], basketball and ran track at [[Graham High School (Bluefield, Virginia)|Graham High School]]. He was ranked as the #7 player in Virginia and the #28 [[cornerback]] prospect in the country by [[Rivals.com]]. He rushed for 2,282 yards and 27 touchdowns as a [[Eleventh grade|junior]] and 2,557 rushing yards and 31 touchdowns as a [[Twelfth grade|senior]], totaling 5,265 yards and 92 touchdowns while averaging nearly ten yards a carry for his high school career. He earned All-Virginia honors and was named VHSL AA Player of the Year. Bradshaw was also on the Graham High [[track & field]] team, where he competed as a sprinter and jumper. In sprints, he recorded times of 6.75 seconds in the [[55 metres]] and 11.34 seconds in the [[100 meters]]. In jumping events, he got a personal-best leap of 1.80 meters in the [[high jump]].{{Cite web |url=https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/ahmad-bradshaw-387/ |title=Ahmad Bradshaw | Army QB |access-date=October 20, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304023503/https://www.trackingfootball.com/players/ahmad-bradshaw-387/ |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |url-status=dead }} Bradshaw originally signed a letter of intent to [[University of Virginia|Virginia]] and arrived in [[Charlottesville, Virginia|Charlottesville]] for football practice, but was kicked off the team by [[Al Groh]] before his first season started, after being arrested for [[underage drinking]] and running from police.{{Cite web |url=http://www.cavalierdaily.com/CVArticle.asp?ID=26533&pid=1423 |title=The Cavalier Daily |access-date=November 30, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060619002813/http://cavalierdaily.com/CVarticle.asp?ID=26533&pid=1423 |archive-date=June 19, 2006 |url-status=dead }} He then enrolled at [[Marshall University]], where his college career would result in his induction into the Marshall Athletic Hall of Fame.{{cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw (2017) - Marshall Athletics Hall of Fame |url=https://herdzone.com/honors/marshall-athletics-hall-of-fame/ahmad-bradshaw/1 |website=Marshall University Athletics |access-date=November 23, 2024 |language=en}} ==College career== ===Freshman season (2004)=== With the [[Marshall Thundering Herd|Thundering Herd]], Bradshaw only had 462 yards and three touchdowns in his freshman season in 2004,[http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=DM&p_theme=dm&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=10DF9618EDFA9588&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM dallasnews.com | Archives] but also totaled 187 yards receiving on 14 receptions for two touchdowns. He missed two games that season, the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia]] and Miami games, due to an ankle sprain sustained during a stellar fourth quarter performance at Ohio State. He also recorded nine punt returns for 108 yards and 15 kick returns for 322 yards as a freshman. Bradshaw rushed for a then career-high 145 yards, including a 77-yard touchdown run, in just eight first half carries against [[Western Michigan University|Western Michigan]]. His other signature performance of the season came against [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State University]], when he took a screen pass 75-yards for a score. ===Sophomore season (2005)=== Bradshaw rushed for 997 yards{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/stats/_/id/10693/ahmad-bradshaw|title=Ahmad Bradshaw Stats|website=Espn.com|access-date=November 10, 2021}} and totaled 1,382 all-purpose yards en route to becoming a second-team All-[[Conference USA]] selection as a sophomore in 2005. He was the team's leading rusher and receiver as well. In the season-opener against [[William & Mary Tribe football|William & Mary]], Bradshaw rushed for 72 yards and a touchdown with 73 yards and a score receiving. He rushed for 99 yards and a touchdown in the loss to #3 [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]]. He followed it up with a then career-high 133 yards against the [[UTEP Miners football|University of Texas at El Paso]] and eclipsed the mark the following week in the Herd's overtime loss to [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss]] with 150 yards and a score. Bradshaw's best performance came against [[East Carolina Pirates football|East Carolina]], when he rushed for a season and career-high 187 yards with two touchdowns along with 51 yards on eight receptions. He added a season-long 56-yard run against ECU as well. ===Junior season (2006)=== Bradshaw's best season of his college career came as a junior in 2006, when he totaled 1,523 yards rushing, for 19 touchdowns, and 129 receiving yards for two scores.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2006 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ahmad-bradshaw-1/gamelog/2006 |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} He was eighth in the nation in rushing yardage and tied for third in rushing touchdowns. In the Herd's second game of the season against [[Hofstra Pride football|Hofstra]], Bradshaw ran for 152 yards and four touchdowns. Against the [[UCF Knights football|University of Central Florida]], he ran for 181 yards and a score. Bradshaw's first out of two 200-yard games of the season came two weeks later against the [[UAB Blazers football|University of Alabama-Birmingham]], when he rushed for 242 yards and two touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Marshall at UAB Box Score, October 21, 2006 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2006-10-21-alabama-birmingham.html |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} Against UTEP, he rushed for career-highs of 261 yards and five touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=UTEP at Marshall Box Score, November 18, 2006 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2006-11-18-marshall.html |access-date=April 28, 2026 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}} ==Professional career== {{NFL predraft | height ft = 5 | height in = 9 1/2 | weight = 198 | dash = 4.66 | ten split = 1.66 | twenty split = 2.75 | shuttle = 4.09 | cone drill = 6.70 | vertical = 34 | broad ft = 9 | broad in = 4 | wonderlic = | arm span = 31 1/2 | hand span = 8 1/2 | note = All values from [[NFL Combine]]{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Scout Ahmad Bradshaw College Football Profile |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=33797&DraftYear=2007 |access-date=November 11, 2023 |website=DraftScout.com}} }} ===New York Giants=== ====2007==== Bradshaw was selected by the [[New York Giants]] in the seventh round with the 250th overall pick of the [[2007 NFL draft]].{{Cite web |title=2007 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2007/draft.htm |access-date=May 11, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} In his first two games, Bradshaw fumbled twice on [[Kickoff (American football)|kickoff]] returns. He was fourth in the National Football Conference with a 26.0-yard kickoff return average when the Giants replaced him with veteran [[Reuben Droughns]]. Bradshaw returned to returning kickoffs for the November 18 game against the [[Detroit Lions]]. Injuries to teammates [[Brandon Jacobs]] and [[Derrick Ward]], and the disappointing play of Droughns, gave Bradshaw his first regular season carries against the [[Minnesota Vikings]]. He gained 29 yards on four carries in the game. On December 23, 2007, he scored his first NFL touchdown on an 88-yard run in the fourth quarter against the [[Buffalo Bills]]. It was the third longest run in Giants history and the longest run of the [[2007 NFL season|2007 season]].{{cite web | title=Ahmad Bradshaw, Brandon Jacobs carry the torch from Tiki Barber | website=New York Daily News | date=December 23, 2007 | url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2007/12/23/ahmad-bradshaw-brandon-jacobs-carry-the-torch-from-tiki-barber/ | access-date=May 1, 2026}} He finished the game with a 151 yards on 17 carries.{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Buffalo Bills - December 23rd, 2007 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200712230buf.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2007 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2007/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Bradshaw was used more frequently as a change of pace back to Jacobs during the Giants 2007 playoff run. He had a great performance in the [[NFC Championship Game]] in Green Bay, including a 52-yard would-be touchdown run in the fourth quarter that was negated by a holding penalty.{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship - New York Giants at Green Bay Packers - January 20th, 2008 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200801200gnb.htm |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} He contributed greatly to his team's success in [[Super Bowl XLII]] against the [[New England Patriots]], gaining 45 yards (the most of all running backs) and even recovering a fumble by quarterback [[Eli Manning]]. The Giants went on to win the Super Bowl, defeating the previously undefeated [[New England Patriots]] 17−14, and ending their opponent's bid for a perfect 19–0 season.{{cite web |last=Battista |first=Judy |author-link=Judy Battista |date=February 4, 2008 |title=Giants Stun Patriots in Super Bowl XLII |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/02/04/sports/football/04game.html#:~:text=But%20with%20their%20defense%20battering,undefeated%20Patriots%2C%2017-14. |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=The New York Times}} ====2008==== Bradshaw averaged 6.7 yards per carry as the third running back for the Giants in 2008. He had 67 carries for 355 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown and added a receiving touchdown.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2008 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2008/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} He was reduced to third string [[running back]] due to a strong performance by Derrick Ward, who finished the season with more than 1,000 rushing yards.{{Cite web |title=2008 New York Giants Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nyg/2008.htm |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2009==== In 2009, Bradshaw was second string running back behind [[Brandon Jacobs]] with [[Derrick Ward]]'s departure to the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. In Week 5, against the Oakland Raiders, he had 165 scrimmage yards and two rushing touchdowns in the 44–7 win.{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at New York Giants - October 11th, 2009 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/200910110nyg.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He rushed for a then career-high 778 yards and seven touchdowns on the season.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2009 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2009/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Bradshaw also had a career receiving long play of 55 yards. ====2010==== Bradshaw was promoted to first-string running back ahead of Brandon Jacobs in 2010, due to Jacobs's disappointing 2009 season. In Week 4, he had 23 carries for 129 yards and one touchdown in a 17–3 win over the Bears.{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at New York Giants - October 3rd, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010030nyg.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In Week 6, he had 19 carries for 133 yards in a 28–20 win over the Detroit Lions.{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at New York Giants - October 17th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010170nyg.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In Week 7, he had 24 carries for 126 yards in a 41–35 win over the Cowboys.{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Dallas Cowboys - October 25th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201010250dal.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} After a two turnover game against the Eagles in Week 9, Bradshaw was demoted to make room for Brandon Jacobs's return.{{cite web | last=Rosenthal | first=Gregg | title=Ahmad Bradshaw to bench; Brandon Jacobs defends him | website=NBC Sports | date=November 25, 2010 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/ahmad-bradshaw-to-bench-jacobs-defends-him | access-date=May 3, 2026}} Despite these obstacles, Bradshaw finished the season with career highs in rushing yards (1,235) and rushing touchdowns (8).{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2010 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2010/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} ====2011==== In 2011, Bradshaw signed a four-year deal worth $18 million and $9 million guaranteed with a $5 million bonus. In Week 3, against the Eagles, he had 139 scrimmage yards and a receiving touchdown in the 29–16 win.{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Philadelphia Eagles - September 25th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201109250phi.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} In Week 6 against the [[Buffalo Bills]], Bradshaw recorded three touchdowns with 104 rushing yards in a 27−24 Giants win.{{Cite web |title=Buffalo Bills at New York Giants - October 16th, 2011 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201110160nyg.htm |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} He was benched for the first half of a game against the Dallas Cowboys in Week 14 due to an alleged curfew violation.{{cite web | last=Schwartz | first=Paul | title=Ahmad benched by Giants for first half | website=New York Post | date=December 12, 2011 | url=https://nypost.com/2011/12/12/ahmad-benched-by-giants-for-first-half/ | access-date=December 20, 2024}} Bradshaw rushed for nine touchdowns during the season, a career-high mark.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} Bradshaw scored the go-ahead and eventual game-winning touchdown with a 6-yard run with 57 seconds remaining in [[Super Bowl XLVI]] against the [[New England Patriots]]. The touchdown was unusual in that the Patriots permitted Bradshaw to score unopposed, to prevent the Giants from [[running out the clock|running out most of the remaining time]] before winning the game with a [[field goal (American football)|field goal]]. Bradshaw, aware of the Patriots' strategy, attempted to stop himself from crossing the [[goal line (American football)|goal line]] but fell backward into the [[end zone]]. The Patriots failed to score, however, and the Giants thus won 21−17.{{cite magazine | url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/joe_posnanski/02/06/super.bowl.xlvi/?xid=cnnbin | title=Bradshaw's Reluctant Touchdown puts to rest an unusual Super Bowl | magazine=Sports Illustrated | date=February 6, 2012 | access-date=February 6, 2012 | author=Posnanski, Joe | archive-date=February 9, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209042357/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/joe_posnanski/02/06/super.bowl.xlvi/?xid=cnnbin | url-status=dead }} ====2012==== [[File:Ahmad bradshaw 2012.jpg|thumb|200px|Bradshaw with the Giants in [[2012 New York Giants season|2012]]]] Although Bradshaw mostly played along rookie [[David Wilson (running back)|David Wilson]] for the starting role, he had a fairly decent season. Bradshaw missed only two games due to injuries to his knee and foot. Despite having his minutes declining because of Wilson, He played in 14 games, had 221 rushing attempts, 1,015 rushing yards, and six touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} It was the second time in his career that Bradshaw had 1,000+ rushing yards (the first being in 2010). On October 7, during a Week 5 game against the [[Cleveland Browns]], Bradshaw carried the ball 30 times for 200 yards, with 1 touchdown, a 4-yard run; he also had 4 receptions for 29 yards, giving him 229 yards of total offense. The Giants would win against the Browns 41−27.{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201210070nyg.htm |title=Cleveland Browns at New York Giants - October 7th, 2012 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=December 7, 2017}} In Week 17, he had 148 scrimmage yards and one rushing touchdown in a 42–7 win over the Eagles.{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at New York Giants - December 30th, 2012 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201212300nyg.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} Bradshaw was released by the Giants on February 6, 2013, to clear cap space and after the emergence of the rookie David Wilson.{{Cite web |date=February 6, 2013|agency=Associated Press |title=Giants Release Running Back Ahmad Bradshaw, Defensive Lineman Chris Canty |url=http://newyork.cbslocal.com/2013/02/06/reports-giants-release-ahmad-bradshaw-chris-canty/ |access-date=February 6, 2013 |website=CBS News - New York}} ===Indianapolis Colts=== [[File:AhmadBradshaw camp2015.jpg|thumb|150px|right|Bradshaw in 2015 at training camp]] On June 11, 2013, Bradshaw signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].{{cite web|title=Ahmad Bradshaw, Indianapolis Colts strike contract|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ahmad-bradshaw-indianapolis-colts-strike-contract-0ap1000000210970|date=June 11, 2013|access-date= June 11, 2013|author= Wesseling, Chris|website=[[NFL.com]] }} After an injury sustained in Week 3, Bradshaw was put on [[injured reserve]] due to needing neck surgery.{{cite news|work=NBCSports.com|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2013/10/08/ahmad-bradshaw-to-have-season-ending-neck-surgery/|title=Ahmad Bradshaw to have season-ending neck surgery|first=Mike|last=Wilkening|date=October 8, 2013|access-date=June 22, 2014}} He had two rushing touchdowns on the 2013 season in three games.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} On March 11, 2014, Bradshaw reached a one-year agreement to re-sign with the Colts. Prior to his injury in Week 6, Bradshaw had a career-high six touchdown receptions, leading all NFL running backs, and was on pace to break [[Marshall Faulk]]'s record of 9.{{cite web|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/indianapolis-colts/post/_/id/5660/colts-offseason-wrap-up|title=Colts offseason wrap-up|date=May 23, 2014|first=Mike|last=Wells|access-date=June 22, 2014}}{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/ahmad-bradshaw-returns-to-indianapolis-colts-0ap2000000333126|title=Ahmad Bradshaw returns to Indianapolis Colts|first=Gregg|last=Rosenthal|date=March 11, 2014|access-date=June 22, 2014}}{{cite web|work=indystar.com|url=http://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nfl/colts/2014/10/16/ahmad-bradshaw-looking-pretty-good-as-a-last-resort/17373281|title=Colts offense's ace in the hole|first=Zak|last=Keefer|date=October 18, 2014|access-date=October 14, 2015}} In the 2014 season, he finished with 90 carries for 425 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns to go with 38 receptions for 300 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}} On October 14, 2015, Bradshaw agreed to terms on a one-year deal with the Colts. On November 30, he was placed on season-ending injured reserve with a wrist injury.{{cite web |date=November 30, 2015 |title=Indianapolis Colts make roster moves |url=http://blogs.colts.com/2015/11/30/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-122/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151204050942/http://blogs.colts.com/2015/11/30/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-122/ |archive-date=December 4, 2015 |access-date=November 30, 2015 |work=Colts.com}} He had two receiving touchdowns in Week 11 against the Atlanta Falcons in a 24–21 victory.{{Cite web |title=Indianapolis Colts at Atlanta Falcons - November 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220atl.htm |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He finished the 2015 season with 31 carries for 85 rushing yards and ten receptions for 64 receiving yards and three receiving touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Ahmad Bradshaw 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BradAh00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=May 3, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} Bradshaw participated in [[The Spring League]] in April 2017.{{cite news|first1=Natalie |last1=Weiner |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2707260-in-the-shadow-of-dak-prescott-welcome-to-the-nfls-league-of-last-chances |title=In the Shadow of Dak Prescott: Welcome to the NFL's League of Last Chances |publisher=Bleacher Report |date=May 10, 2017 |access-date=August 29, 2017}} ==Career statistics== ===NFL=== {| class="wikitable mw-collapsible mw-collapsed" |- ! '''Ahmard Rashad Hall''' (born November 13, 1979) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] for the [[Tennessee Titans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]] and was originally signed by the Titans as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2006.<ref name=TNtitans/> He is also a [[United States Marine]].

== Early life and military service ==
Ahmard Rashad Hall was born on November 13, 1979, in [[Galveston, Texas]].<ref name=TNtitans/> He attended Angleton High School in Angleton, Texas. In high school, in addition to playing football, he was a member of the track team and the baseball team.  He was team captain of the football team and was an all-district player.<ref name=TNtitans/>

He served for four years (1998–2002) in the [[United States Marine Corps]] in the [[2nd Battalion, 8th Marines]] as a field radio operator reaching the rank of sergeant.<ref name=TNtitans/><ref name=Marines.com>

</ref>  He served tours of duty in Kosovo and Afghanistan. He attended the [[University of Texas]] (UT) on the [[G.I. Bill]].<ref name=TNtitans/> He was a walk-on to the football program at UT.<ref name=Marines.com/>

== College career ==
Hall played fullback at the [[University of Texas at Austin]] for the [[Texas Longhorn Athletics|Longhorns]], including their [[2005 Texas Longhorns football team|2005 national championship team]].<ref name="LL PDF">{{cite news|url=http://www.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/doc_lib/2005_ULL_notes.pdf |title=Texas Game Notes – Louisiana Lafayette |access-date=2007-03-14 |publisher=MackBrownTexasFootball |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060216174842/http://mackbrown-texasfootball.com/doc_lib/2005_ULL_notes.pdf |archive-date=2006-02-16 }}</ref>

== Professional career ==

Hall played in 14 games his rookie season, rushing seven times for a total of 21 yards. He caught 15 balls, for 138 yards. Ahmard also played on special teams, making five tackles. He went on to play 85 games for the Titans until 2011.

'''Akeem Raphael Jordan''' (born August 17, 1985) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He was signed by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2007. He also played for the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[Washington Redskins]], and [[Toronto Argonauts]]. He played [[college football]] at [[James Madison Dukes football|James Madison University]].

==Early life==
Jordan attended [[Harrisonburg High School (Virginia)|Harrisonburg High School]] in Virginia. While there, he played [[high school football]]. In 2001, he was named the Virginia Group AA Player of the Year after leading his team to a state title. He earned first-team all-state honors in 2002 as a senior defensive back, and second-team honors as a [[running back]].

==College career==
Jordan played college football at [[James Madison University]], where he was a member of the 2004 National Championship team which defeated [[The University of Montana]] to win the title. He was named the Colonial Athletic Association Football Conference Defensive Player of the Year in 2006 after posting 140 tackles including 17 tackles for a loss, 5.5 sacks, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite news|author=O'Sullivan, Tim |title=Tough conference inspires 'Cats confidence in playoffs |url=http://www.concordmonitor.com/article/tough-conference-inspires-cats-confidence-in-playoffs |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120724162608/http://www.concordmonitor.com/article/tough-conference-inspires-cats-confidence-in-playoffs |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 24, 2012 |work=Concord Monitor |date=November 22, 2006 |access-date=2011-06-20 }}</ref> He finished third in voting for the 2006 [[Dudley Award]], which is given annually to the best college football player in [[Virginia]], behind [[Vince Hall]] and [[Chris Long (American football)|Chris Long]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Hall wins Dudley Award |url=http://www.hokiesports.com/football/recaps/2006126aaa.html |work=Virginia Tech Hokies |date=December 6, 2006 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> Jordan was named to the [[American Football Coaches Association]] Division I-AA Coaches' All-America Team in 2006.<ref>{{cite news |title=Murphy named to AFCA Division I-AA Coaches' All-America Team |url=http://www.montanagrizzlies.com/news/db.aspx?n=5236&m=37 |work=Montana Grizzlies |date=December 12, 2006 |access-date=2011-06-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629175355/http://www.montanagrizzlies.com/news/db.aspx?n=5236&m=37 |archive-date=2011-06-29 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He finished second in voting for the [[Buck Buchanan Award]], which is given to the best defensive player in Division I FCS.<ref>{{cite news|title=Shotwell, Moore also nab awards |url=http://www.concordmonitor.com/article/shotwell-moore-also-nab-awards |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120723020232/http://www.concordmonitor.com/article/shotwell-moore-also-nab-awards |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 23, 2012 |work=Concord Monitor |date=December 15, 2006 |access-date=2011-06-20 }}</ref> He was named the Virginia Defensive Player of the Year following the season as well.<ref>{{cite news |title=Hall, Ore honored as tops in the state |url=http://www.hokiesports.com/football/recaps/20061221aaa.html |work=Virginia Tech Hokies |date=December 21, 2006 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> In his career as a Duke, he appeared in 50 games (26 starts) and made 299 tackles and 7.5 sacks. He graduated from James Madison in 2007.

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia Eagles===
[[File:Akeem Jordan.jpg|thumb|left|Jordan with the Philadelphia Eagles.]]
Signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] in 2007, Jordan played in all preseason games and led the team in tackles when the preseason was over. He made the final cuts when the Eagles had to come down to the 53-man roster, but was cut and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day when the Eagles picked up two free agents.<ref>{{cite news|title=Extra innings Sports in brief |url=http://www.timesleader.com/sports/20070903_03_sports_briefs_spt_ART.html |work=[[Times Leader]] |date=September 3, 2007 |access-date=2011-06-20 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On October 29, 2007, the Eagles cut linebacker [[Matt McCoy (American football)|Matt McCoy]] and called up Jordan from the practice squad.<ref>{{cite news |author=Maaddi, Rob |title=From now on, Eagles are in win-or-else mode |url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/football/2007-10-29-1317441990_x.htm |work=[[USA Today]] |date=October 29, 2007 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> He made his NFL debut later that week, playing special teams against the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. Jordan made his first NFL start in week 17 of the [[2007 NFL season|2007 season]] at weakside linebacker against the [[Buffalo Bills]] after [[Takeo Spikes]] was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Eagles' Spikes Done For Season |url=http://www.koco.com/r/14890699/detail.html |work=KOCO.com |date=December 19, 2007 |access-date=2011-06-20 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120319202256/http://www.koco.com/r/14890699/detail.html |archive-date=March 19, 2012 }}</ref> He recorded 14 tackles in the game. He played in nine games as a rookie and finished fourth in special teams productions.<ref>{{cite news |author=Robinson, Tom |title=From JMU to NFL, Jordan trying to prove he belongs |url=http://hamptonroads.com/2008/08/jmu-nfl-jordan-trying-prove-he-belongs |work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]] |date=August 22, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref>

Jordan began the [[2008 NFL season|2008 season]] as the backup weakside linebacker to [[Omar Gaither]], playing mostly on special teams.<ref>{{cite news |author=Fierro, Nick |title=Evolution of Eagles defense |url=http://www.nj.com/sports/times/index.ssf?/base/sports-1/1229774711242231.xml&coll=5 |work=nj.com |date=December 20, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20 |archive-date=October 16, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121016185702/http://www.nj.com/sports/times/index.ssf?/base/sports-1/1229774711242231.xml&coll=5 |url-status=dead }}</ref> In a week 12 game against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Jordan replaced Gaither at weakside linebacker.<ref>{{cite news|author=Schwartz, Andy |title=Schwartz: Eagles Notes: Shurmur Informs McNabb |url=http://www.necn.com/pages/landing_newengland?blockID=18595&tagID=1120 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907003552/http://www.necn.com/pages/landing_newengland?blockID=18595&tagID=1120 |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 7, 2012 |work=CSNPhilly.com |date=November 23, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20 }}</ref> Jordan led the team with nine tackles in the game.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bird's-eye view |url=http://readingeagle.com/article.aspx?id=115078 |work=[[Reading Eagle]] |date=November 24, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20 |archive-date=September 26, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926174722/http://readingeagle.com/article.aspx?id=115078 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He kept the starting weakside linebacker job for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite news|author=Grotz, Bob |title=Reid proves to team that no job is safe |url=http://www.pottstownmercury.com/articles/2008/11/25/sports/srv0000004129474.txt?viewmode=fullstory |work=[[The Mercury (Pennsylvania)|The Mercury]] |date=November 25, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20 }}{{dead link|date=June 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The next week against the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on Thanksgiving night, Jordan recovered his first career fumble.<ref>{{cite news |author=Nalbone, John |title=Postgame Notebook |url=http://www.nj.com/eagles/index.ssf/2008/11/postgame_notebook_4.html |work=nj.com |date=November 28, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> He recorded 10 tackles in a week 16 loss to the [[Washington Redskins]].<ref>{{cite news |title=JMU Alum Soars with the Philadelphia Eagles |url=http://www.breezejmu.org/article_e8890cbb-8b0c-5471-91d8-6d44fa57528b.html |work=The Breeze |date=December 25, 2008 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref>

Jordan beat out Gaither for the starting right outside [[linebacker]] job before the [[2009 NFL season|2009 season]]. Jordan made an interception in each of the first two weeks of the season.<ref>{{cite news |author=Grotz, Bob |title=The Eagles Clipboard |url=http://www.delcotimes.com/articles/2009/09/21/sports/doc4ab6fdf3d8ed8801190655.txt |work=delcotimes.com |date=September 21, 2009 |access-date=2011-06-20 |archive-date=August 25, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825233525/http://www.delcotimes.com/articles/2009/09/21/sports/doc4ab6fdf3d8ed8801190655.txt |url-status=dead }}</ref> He missed four straight games after suffering a hyperextended knee in a week 9 game against the [[Dallas Cowboys]]. He rotated with [[Jeremiah Trotter]] at middle linebacker upon his return.<ref>{{cite news |author=Fierro, Nick |title=Henry's death hits hard for Andrews |url=https://www.mcall.com/2009/12/18/henrys-death-hits-hard-for-andrews-3/ |work=The Morning Call |date=December 18, 2009 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> Jordan made two starts at middle linebacker.<ref>{{cite news |author=Jasner, Andy |title=Eagles' Vick a fan of Wade Phillips |url=http://www.dallasnews.com/sports/dallas-cowboys/headlines/20100106-Eagles-Vick-a-fan-of-6177.ece |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |date=January 7, 2010 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> Jordan finished the season with 82 tackles in ten starts.<ref>{{cite news |title=Jordan signs one-year tender offer |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/news/story?id=5018897 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 22, 2010 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref>

Jordan was re-signed to a one-year [[restricted free agent]] tender on March 22, 2010.<ref>{{cite web |author=McLane, Jeff |title=Jordan signs tender |url=http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/eagles/Jordan_and_Cole_sign_tenders.html |publisher=Philly.com |date=March 22, 2010 |access-date=2010-03-22| archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20100324200017/http://www.philly.com/philly/sports/eagles/Jordan_and_Cole_sign_tenders.html| archive-date= 24 March 2010 | url-status= live}}</ref> He beat out [[Moise Fokou]] for the starting strongside linebacker job in the preseason, but was replaced by Fokou after starting the first four games of the season.<ref>{{cite news |author=Fierro, Nick |title=Eagles preparing for 49ers' best shot |url=https://www.mcall.com/2010/10/09/eagles-preparing-for-49ers-best-shot/ |work=The Morning Call |date=October 9, 2010 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref>

Jordan was not offered a tender following the [[2010 NFL season|2010 season]].<ref>{{cite news |author=McLane, Jeff |title=Eagles move to hold Rocca and Harrison |url=http://articles.philly.com/2011-03-04/sports/28653536_1_stewart-bradley-akeem-jordan-omar-gaither |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120527141931/http://articles.philly.com/2011-03-04/sports/28653536_1_stewart-bradley-akeem-jordan-omar-gaither |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 27, 2012 |work=[[The Philadelphia Inquirer]] |date=March 4, 2011 |access-date=2011-06-20}}</ref> He was re-signed to a one-year contract on July 30, 2011. He was re-signed again to a two-year contract on September 6.

===Kansas City Chiefs===
Jordan agreed to terms on a one-year deal with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] on April 13, 2013, reuniting him with former head coach [[Andy Reid]].

===Washington Redskins===
Jordan signed with the [[Washington Redskins]] on March 19, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Akeem-Jordan-Pads-Linebacker-Corps/67c8dda7-6bdb-4990-904c-b5566b31882a |title=Akeem Jordan Pads Linebacker Corps |access-date=2014-03-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140320151513/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Akeem-Jordan-Pads-Linebacker-Corps/67c8dda7-6bdb-4990-904c-b5566b31882a |archive-date=2014-03-20 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was placed on the active roster on October 18, 2014.<ref>{{cite web | last=Keim | first=John | title=Redskins activate Stephen Bowen | website=ESPN.com | date=2014-10-18 | url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nflnation/post/_/id/145410/redskins-activate-stephen-bowen | access-date=2025-05-18}}</ref> On November 25, the Redskins waived him off their injured reserve.<ref>{{cite news|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/football-insider/wp/2014/11/25/redskins-waive-injured-linebacker-akeem-jordan/|title=Redskins waive injured linebacker Akeem Jordan|first=Mike|last=Jones|date=November 25, 2014|access-date=2014-12-12}}</ref>

===Toronto Argonauts===
On September 12, 2017, Jordan signed with the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/football/2017/09/12/argonauts-sign-former-nfl-linebacker-akeem-jordan-to-contract.html |title=Argonauts sign former NFL linebacker Akeem Jordan to contract |website=The Star|language=en |access-date=2019-05-30}}</ref> Jordan made his debut on October 7, 2017 against the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] and made 10 tackles. Jordan played in 4 games in 2017, and played in 15 games in 2018. After receiving an extension prior to free agency opening,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/2019/02/06/argos-extend-lb-akeem-jordan/|title = Argos extend LB Akeem Jordan|date = 6 February 2019}}</ref> Jordan was released following the 2019 preseason.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.argonauts.ca/2019/06/08/argos-announce-final-roster-moves-following-training-camp/|title = Argos announce final roster moves following training camp|date = 8 June 2019}}</ref> In 19 regular season games with the Argos, Jordan produced 41 tackles, 9 special teams tackles, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cfl.ca/players/akeem-jordan/133069/|title = Akeem Jordan}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jordan and two of his James Madison teammates were charged with [[assault]] and [[Battery (crime)|battery]] by a teammate in February 2006. The teammate dropped the charges on March 20, 2006, but gave no reason for doing so.<ref>{{cite news |title=Charges Dropped |url=http://www.whsv.com/news/headlines/2495206.html |work=WHSV.com |date=March 20, 2006 |access-date=2011-06-20 |archive-date=March 22, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120322015731/http://www.whsv.com/news/headlines/2495206.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Jordan was arrested and served with a citizen-obtained warrant for misdemeanor assault and battery in [[Harrisonburg, Virginia]], on June 19, 2011.<ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.dnronline.com/news_details.php?AID=58398&CHID=76 |title=NFL Linebacker, JMU Star Jordan Arrested |last=DeLea |first=Pete |date=June 20, 2011 |work=The Daily News Record |access-date=2011-06-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110623031834/http://www.dnronline.com/news_details.php?AID=58398&CHID=76 |archive-date=June 23, 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Ahtyba Rubin''' ({{IPAc-en|ɑː|ˈ|t|ɑː|b|ə}} {{Respell|ah|TAH|bə}};<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=48388&SPID=4653&DB_OEM_ID=10700&ATCLID=324886&Q_SEASON=2007 |title=Ahtyba Rubin |work=Iowa State Cyclones Website |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20081119081118/http://www.cyclones.com/ViewArticle.dbml?SPSID=48388&SPID=4653&DB_OEM_ID=10700&ATCLID=324886&Q_SEASON=2007 |archivedate=November 19, 2008 }}</ref> born July 25, 1986) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State Cyclones]] and was selected by the [[Cleveland Browns]] in the sixth round of the [[2008 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Fort Belvoir, Virginia]], Rubin graduated from [[Escambia High School]] in [[Pensacola, Florida]] in 2004, the same high school as former Cleveland Browns teammate [[Trent Richardson]], and NFL Hall of Famer [[Emmitt Smith]]. He then went on to attend [[Trinity Valley Community College]] in [[Athens, Texas]]. In his freshman year, he played defensive line, but was converted into an offense lineman for his sophomore year. Rubin made the adjustment with significant success and earned all-conference and honorable mention All-America honors in 2006.

==College career==
Regarded as a three-star recruit out of [[junior college]],<ref>{{Citation |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Ahtyba-Rubin-44674 |work=Rivals.com |title=Ahtyba Rubin Recruiting Profile }}</ref> Rubin was recruited by a number of schools, and eventually picked [[Iowa State University]] over [[Texas Christian University]]. He was switched back to defensive line in his junior year, and started the last nine games of the 2006 season. He finished the year with 34 tackles, four tackles for loss, and a sack.

As a senior, Rubin played in all of the [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Cyclones]]' games, registering 42 tackles (with four for loss) and recording 1.5 sacks.

==Professional career==

===2008 NFL draft===
Following his impressive senior season at Iowa State, Rubin was regarded as a "productive NFL starter" at nose tackle, and projected a mid-third round pick by ''[[Sports Illustrated]]''.<ref>{{Citation |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2008/draft/players/56271.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715051124/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/football/2008/draft/players/56271.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 15, 2012 |title=2008 NFL Draft Profile: Ahtyba Rubin |magazine=Sports Illustrated }}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
Rubin was selected in the sixth round (190th overall) by the Cleveland Browns, and was signed on July 22, 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2008 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2008/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-12 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.foxnews.com/wires/2008Jul22/0,4670,FBNBrownsSignings,00.html |title=Browns sign 5 draft picks to 4-year contracts |date=July 22, 2008 |work=FOXNews.com }}</ref>

He filled out a backup role for Browns nose tackle [[Shaun Rogers (American football)|Shaun Rogers]] in 2008 and 2009, until Rogers went down with a lower leg injury in week 12 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Citation |url=http://www.ohio.com/sports/78188502.html |title=Injuries plague Browns: Rogers needs surgery, Pool suffers concussion against Bengals |first=Marla |last=Ridenour |work=Beacon Journal |date=November 30, 2009 }}</ref> Rubin has since become the Browns starting nose tackle. In the 2010 offseason the Browns traded [[defensive end]] [[Corey Williams (American football)|Corey Williams]] to the [[Detroit Lions]], moved former starting nose Tackle Shaun Rogers to defensive end and promoted Rubin to starter due to his performance in 2009.  2010 was the best season of Rubin's young career, highlighted by his 87 tackles and an interception against Kansas City's Matt Cassel.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Kansas City Chiefs at Cleveland Browns - September 19th, 2010 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201009190cle.htm |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In his five years with the Browns, Rubin has played in 72 games, starting 50 of them. His career totals are 9.0 sacks, 227 total tackles, 4 passes defended, 1 interception, 3 forced fumbles, and 1 fumble recovery.

===Seattle Seahawks===
On March 19, 2015, Rubin signed a one-year deal with the [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/articles/article-1/Nose-tackle-Ahtyba-Rubin-signs-with-Seahawks/41ae6d58-a9d1-400d-8ce0-878b9cf1f53e|title=Nose tackle Ahtyba Rubin signs with Seahawks|last=Farnsworth|first=Clare|date=March 20, 2015|work=Seattle Seahawks|access-date=September 16, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150322144638/http://www.seahawks.com/news/articles/article-1/Nose-tackle-Ahtyba-Rubin-signs-with-Seahawks/41ae6d58-a9d1-400d-8ce0-878b9cf1f53e|archive-date=March 22, 2015|url-status=dead|language=en}}</ref> The Seahawks released incumbent starting defensive tackle [[Tony McDaniel]] during training camp, giving Rubin a great opportunity at a starting job. In Week 4 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Rubin got his first sack as a Seahawk. In Week 11 vs the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Rubin got an interception in a 39–30 victory.<ref name="q425">{{cite web | last=Mandel | first=Eric | title=Seahawks' Ahtyba Rubin makes crucial, unexpected pick of Steelers' Ben Roethlisberger | website=Seattle Sports | date=2015-11-30 | url=https://sports.mynorthwest.com/64480/seahawks-ahtyba-rubin-makes-crucial-unexpected-pick-of-steelers-ben-roethlisberger/ | access-date=2024-08-09}}</ref>

On March 7, 2016, he signed a three-year contract.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Condotta|first1=Bob|title=Seahawks reach agreement with DT Ahtyba Rubin to three-year deal|url=http://www.seattletimes.com/sports/seahawks/seahawks-reach-agreement-with-dt-ahtyba-rubin-to-three-year-deal|website=SeattleTimes.com|date=March 8, 2016|accessdate=March 9, 2016}}</ref>

On September 2, 2017, Rubin was released by the Seahawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Seahawks Make Three More Trades, Set 53-Man Roster|url=http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/09/02/seahawks-make-three-more-trades-set-53-man-roster|author=Drovetto, Tony|website=Seahawks.com|date=September 2, 2017|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20171009153425/http://www.seahawks.com/news/2017/09/02/seahawks-make-three-more-trades-set-53-man-roster|archivedate=October 9, 2017}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On September 15, 2017, Rubin signed with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos sign NT Ahtyba Rubin|url=http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-sign-NT-Ahtyba-Rubin/6fc1a9f7-7107-4961-829e-38f56c406dc4|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=September 15, 2017|access-date=September 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171007143750/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-sign-NT-Ahtyba-Rubin/6fc1a9f7-7107-4961-829e-38f56c406dc4|archive-date=October 7, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was released on October 17, 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title=Broncos release Ahtyba Rubin, place Billy Turner on IR|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-release-ahtyba-rubin-place-billy-turner-on-ir-19592335|author=DiLalla, Aric|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=October 17, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017234927/http://www.denverbroncos.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Broncos-release-Ahtyba-Rubin-place-Billy-Turner-on-IR/c8210314-8400-4071-a1a4-8f986eb0c70f|archive-date=October 17, 2017|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Atlanta Falcons===
On October 19, 2017, Rubin signed with the [[Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign defensive tackle Ahtyba Rubin waive defensive lineman Taniela Tupou|url=http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/transactions/article-1/Falcons-sign-defensive-tackle-Ahtyba-Rubin-waive-defensive-lineman-Taniela-Tupou-/5b3134b3-dfc0-4c65-8f89-be7b4f9a2694|author=Conway, Kelsey|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=October 19, 2017|access-date=October 19, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171020001254/http://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/transactions/article-1/Falcons-sign-defensive-tackle-Ahtyba-Rubin-waive-defensive-lineman-Taniela-Tupou-/5b3134b3-dfc0-4c65-8f89-be7b4f9a2694|archive-date=October 20, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Oakland Raiders===
On June 12, 2018, Rubin signed with the [[Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 12, 2018 |title=Raiders sign DT Ahtyba Rubin and DT Frostee Rucker |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-sign-dt-ahtyba-rubin-and-dt-frostee-rucker |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 15, 2018, after suffering a tear in his biceps.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 15, 2018 |title=Raiders Claim DT Gabe Wright; Place DT Ahtyba Rubin on IR |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-claim-dt-gabe-wright-place-dt-ahtyba-rubin-on-ir |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

'''Ainsley Thomas Battles''' (born November 6, 1978) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt Commodores]].

Battles attended [[Parkview High School (Georgia)|Parkview High School]] in [[Lilburn, Georgia]]. After finishing high school, he went on to play football at [[Vanderbilt University]]. After finishing school at Vanderbilt, he played professionally in the NFL. He played four seasons for the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] and the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]]. During a heated 2003 [[National Football League Training Camp|training camp]] battle for [[Starting lineup|starting]] strong safety with the [[Buffalo Bills]], Ainsley Battles left the team for an undisclosed reason. After his time as a football player was over, he went on to be a Social Studies teacher at Archer High School and at Central Gwinnett High School, both in Lawrenceville, Georgia. Later he taught English II at Atlantic Coast High School in Jacksonville, Florida, where he also served as a defensive backs football coach. Most recently, he resides in Las Vegas, Nevada.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kffl.com/player/926/nfl/news/ainsley-battles |title=Ainsley Battles latest news and rumors |website=www.kffl.com |access-date=January 12, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205012824/http://www.kffl.com/player/926/nfl/news/ainsley-battles |archive-date=December 5, 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Ahmad Black''' (born December 12, 1988)<ref>[https://twitter.com/ahmadblack35/status/940452855445704705 Ahmad Black Twitter Post]</ref> is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] for the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).  He played [[college football]] for the [[Florida Gators football|Florida Gators]], and was a member of a [[BCS National Championship]] team.  Black was selected by the Buccaneers in the fifth round of the [[2011 NFL draft]].  Black officially retired from the NFL on April 9, 2017.{{Cn|date=November 2024}}

==Early life==
Black was born in [[Lakeland, Florida]], and he attended [[Lawton Chiles Middle Academy]] and later [[Lakeland High School (Lakeland, Florida)|Lakeland High School]].  As a sophomore playing for the Florida Class 5A [[high school football]] powerhouse Lakeland Dreadnaughts, he recorded 71 [[tackle (football move)|tackles]] and 10 [[interception]]s, and 71 tackles with six interceptions as a junior.  As a Dreadnaught senior, Black recorded 82 tackles and four interceptions.

==College career==
Black accepted an athletic scholarship to attend the [[University of Florida]] in Gainesville, Florida, where he played for coach [[Urban Meyer]]'s Florida Gators football team from [[2007 Florida Gators football team|2007]] to [[2010 Florida Gators football team|2010]].<ref name=ufmediaguide>{{Cite web |url=http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2012/media_guide.pdf  |title=2012 Florida Football Media Guide |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20130527130648/http://web.gatorzone.com/football/media/2012/media_guide.pdf |archivedate=May 27, 2013 |work=University Athletic Association |location=Gainesville, Florida |pages=68, 78, 88, 89, 94, 95, 97, 100, 103, 106, 116, 138, 144, 158–159, 165, 170, 176 |year=2012 |accessdate=September 15, 2012}}</ref>

As a freshman, Black played in seven games as a [[cornerback]] for the Gators and recorded seven tackles.  As a sophomore in 2008, Black [[starting lineup|started]] all 14 games at [[strong safety]] and made 59 tackles and seven interceptions for 191 return yards and two [[touchdowns]], and was recognized as a second-team [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) selection.  Black caught his seventh interception in the Gators' 24–14 win over the [[2008 Oklahoma Sooners football team|Oklahoma Sooners]] in the [[2009 BCS National Championship Game]].

Following his senior season in 2010, he was a first-team All-SEC selection and received first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors from Rivals.com and second-team honors from the [[Associated Press]].  To end his college career, he had two interceptions, returning one 80 yards for a touchdown against Penn State in the Outback Bowl, earning Player of the Game honors.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.gainesville.com/article/20110101/ARTICLES/110109963 |title=Black caps stellar career with game-winner |date=January 1, 2011 |newspaper=[[Gainesville Sun]]}}</ref>

'''Akeem Christopher Ayers''' (born July 10, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA Bruins]], earning second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors in 2010.  Ayers was selected by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the second round of the [[2011 NFL draft]]. He has also played for the [[New England Patriots]], [[St. Louis Rams]], [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[New York Giants]]. He won [[Super Bowl XLIX]] with the Patriots.

==Early life==
Ayers attended [[Verbum Dei High School]] in Los Angeles, where he played for the Verbum Dei Eagles [[high school football]] team. He won a CIF championship during his senior season.

==College career==
Ayers played for [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] in college. Ayers is known for his athletic interceptions for touchdowns, one in the 2009 season against [[2009 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon]] and one against [[2009 Temple Owls football team|Temple]] in the [[2009 EagleBank Bowl]]. The latter was the game-winning score of the bowl game and helped him earn MVP honors.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaaf/ucla-bruins-temple-owls-200912290015/ |title=UCLA at Temple {{!}} 2009-12-29 {{!}} College Football {{!}} Yahoo! Sports |website=sports.yahoo.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140426165623/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaaf/ucla-bruins-temple-owls-200912290015/ |archive-date=2014-04-26}}</ref> In a post-game interview, he admitted that he slipped, and was just trying to rush the passer on his game-changing play.  As he got up, he saw the [[quarterback]] looking to pass, jumped up, and pulled in the pass for an interception and score.

On September 18, 2010, Ayers had a key interception against #23 [[2010 Houston Cougars football team|Houston]] in UCLA's first win against a ranked opponent since 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207896753|title=UCLA-Houston Game Notes|date=September 18, 2010|access-date=September 28, 2010 }}</ref> The following week on September 25, he played a key role in the Bruins' second upset against a ranked opponent in a victory over No. 7 ranked [[2010 Texas Longhorns football team|Texas Longhorns]] 34–12 in front of more 101,000 fans in [[Austin, Texas]]. Ayers had a key interception, seven tackles, a forced fumble, and a sack. He was named [[Lott Trophy|Lott]] IMPACT Player of the Week on September 27. At the end of the 2010 season, his junior year, he entered for the NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/combine/profiles/akeem-ayers?id=2495491|title = Akeem Ayers Stats, News and Video - LB|website = [[NFL.com]]}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
Ayers was selected 39th overall by the [[Tennessee Titans]] in the [[2011 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2011/draft.htm |title=2011 NFL Draft Listing |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en |access-date=2019-02-26}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ocregister.com/ucla/ayers-462384-strong-round.html Tennessee Titans select Akeem Ayers]</ref>

===New England Patriots===
On October 21, 2014, the Titans traded Ayers along with a seventh round draft pick in the [[2015 NFL draft]] to the [[New England Patriots]] for a sixth round draft choice.<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/titans-trade-linebacker-akeem-ayers-to-patriots-0ap3000000415026|title=Titans trade linebacker Akeem Ayers to Patriots|first=Kevin|last=Patra|date=October 21, 2014|access-date=October 21, 2014}}</ref> In each of his first two games with New England, Ayers recorded a sack.

Ayers won [[Super Bowl XLIX]] with the Patriots after they defeated the [[Seattle Seahawks]] 28-24.

===St. Louis Rams===
[[File:Akeem Ayers.jpg|175px|thumb|right|Ayers with the Rams in 2015.]]
On March 12, 2015, Ayers signed a two-year contract with the St. Louis Rams.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kyed | first=Doug | title=Former Patriot Akeem Ayers Signs Two-Year Contract With St. Louis Rams | website=NESN.com | date=2015-03-13 | url=https://nesn.com/2015/03/former-patriot-akeem-ayers-signs-two-year-contract-with-rams/ | access-date=2025-05-18}}</ref> On September 3, 2016, he was released by the Rams as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams Make 53-Man Roster Decisions|url=http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Make-53-Man-Roster-Decisions/d9eabd99-516f-482a-ba08-783512f449de|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170831132249/http://www.therams.com/news-and-events/article-1/Rams-Make-53-Man-Roster-Decisions/d9eabd99-516f-482a-ba08-783512f449de|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 31, 2017|website=TheRams.com|date=September 3, 2016}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
Ayers signed a two-year contract with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] on September 6, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Veteran Linebacker Akeem Ayers Joins Colts|url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Veteran-Linebacker-Akeem-Ayers-Joins-Colts/ea6a1c34-1019-4e15-bfa0-c3223a3d8a64|access-date=September 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160909094530/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Veteran-Linebacker-Akeem-Ayers-Joins-Colts/ea6a1c34-1019-4e15-bfa0-c3223a3d8a64|archive-date=September 9, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On September 2, 2017, Ayers was released during final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Final 2017 Roster Cuts|url=http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Announce-Final-2017-Roster-Cuts/5dc30820-9391-401e-8bdd-40852df5769e|author=Walker, Andrew|website=Colts.com|date=September 2, 2017|access-date=September 8, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170906155106/http://www.colts.com/news/article-1/Colts-Announce-Final-2017-Roster-Cuts/5dc30820-9391-401e-8bdd-40852df5769e|archive-date=September 6, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On November 14, 2017, Ayers signed with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Giants roster moves: Keenan Robinson placed on IR; Three players signed|url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-roster-moves-Keenan-Robinson-placed-on-IR-Three-players-signed/abe405fe-28f3-4975-b6d3-36dd3ca69c1f|author=Eisen, Michael|website=Giants.com|date=November 14, 2017|access-date=November 15, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171117230940/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-roster-moves-Keenan-Robinson-placed-on-IR-Three-players-signed/abe405fe-28f3-4975-b6d3-36dd3ca69c1f|archive-date=November 17, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>
