'''Ahmad Drushane Brooks''' (born March 13, 1980) is an American sports broadcaster and former professional [[American football|football]] player who is a broadcaster for [[ESPNU]], the [[Longhorn Network]] and [[KTXX-FM]].<ref name="espnmedia">{{cite web |url=http://espnmediazone.com/us/bios/ahmad-brooks/ |title=Ahmad Brooks |publisher=ESPN MediaZone |work=www.espnmediazone.com |accessdate=November 23, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171023013113/http://espnmediazone.com/us/bios/ahmad-brooks/ |archive-date=October 23, 2017 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He played as a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Brooks played [[college football]] for the [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas Longhorns]], serving as team [[captain (sports)|captain]] in 2001. He played in the NFL for three years before retiring from playing in 2005.

==Early life==
Ahmad excelled in both the classroom and on the field at an early age. By the age of five, he became a Grand Champion in karate where he was given the nickname "Tank" for his exceptional karate skills and abilities. Not only was Ahmad an upcoming karate champion, but he also was a standout in soccer, baseball, and football.<ref name="bio">[http://www.sportsradio1300.com/pages/ahmadbrooks.html Brooks  ' bio at Sportsradio130.com]{{Dead link|date=October 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

Prior to graduating from [[Abilene High School (Abilene, Texas)|Abilene High School]], he was a member of the U-16 US National Soccer Pool and led the Abilene Eagles football squad to their best record in decades. In addition, Ahmad became Abilene High’s first Division I football signee in 11 years and the school’s first player to earn a spot in the Texas HS Coaches Association All-Star Game since 1964.

He was voted class president of his high school all four years, while also serving as a four-year student council representative, a member of Youth City Council and a prep scholar and mentor.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gonzalez-Boyd |first=Frances  |date=November 1, 2009 |title=Proud Mary Has Something to Brag About These Days; Son Ahmad Plays Both Roles As Scholar and Athlete From Abilene High to University of Texas at Austin |url=http://westtexastribune.com/clients/westtexastribune/proud-mary-has-something-to-brag-about-these-days-son-ahmad-plays-both-rol-p867.htm?twindow=Default&smenu=1&mad=No |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120720052538/http://westtexastribune.com/clients/westtexastribune/proud-mary-has-something-to-brag-about-these-days-son-ahmad-plays-both-rol-p867.htm?twindow=Default&smenu=1&mad=No |archive-date=July 20, 2012 |access-date=November 23, 2016 |website=www.westtexastribune.com |publisher=West Texas Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.texnews.com/sports/ahsfb092196.html |title=Article at Texnews.com |access-date=May 25, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100131085158/http://www.texnews.com/sports/ahsfb092196.html |archive-date=January 31, 2010 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Career==

===College===
In 1998, Ahmad signed and became a valuable member of the [[University of Texas]] football team for [[Mack Brown|Coach Mack Brown]]’s inaugural recruiting class at UT. By the conclusion of his senior year, he and his teammates were deemed as the winningest class in UT history.<ref name="bio" /><ref>{{cite web |url=http://grfx.cstv.com/schools/tex/graphics/newsstand/HC_050107_draft.pdf |title=Longhorns trio has high hopes in NFL draft |author=Joseph Duarte |date=April 27, 2007 |publisher=Houston Chronicle |work=ww.grfx.com |accessdate=November 23, 2016 |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304110037/http://grfx.cstv.com/schools/tex/graphics/newsstand/HC_050107_draft.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[http://www.dallasnews.com/sharedcontent/dws/spt/colleges/redrivershootout/history/1999.html 1999 article at Dallasnews.com]</ref>

Brooks' personal accomplishments include receiving action in 51 games and starting 27 contests while recording 182 tackles, four sacks, four interceptions, 27 pass breakups, seven forced fumbles and three fumble recoveries in four years at UT. In addition, he secured a team-high 88 tackles for the #1 ranked defense in the country during 2001 season, including a career-high 22 stops in the [[Big 12 Football Championship Game|Big 12 Championship Game]] against Colorado. Brooks led the Longhorns with 16 pass breakups and two interceptions in 1999.<ref name="bio" />

Brooks served as Team Captain in 2001 to his teammates and school along with [[Major Applewhite]] and Deandre Lewis. The honors he received included an All-Big 12 mention as well as receiving the University of Texas Outstanding Senior Award for accomplishments on and off the football field.  He was a member of the Athletics Dean’s Honor Roll while also serving on the Student-Athlete Advisory Council as the Longhorn football team representative.<ref name="bio" /><ref>[http://old.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/pages/releases/2001_02/007/2001_Team_Awards.pdf UT Football 2001 Team Awards]{{Dead link|date=October 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===NFL===
Following his tenure at Texas, Brooks entered the [[National Football League]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] signed by the [[Buffalo Bills]] in 2002. He was released by the Bills at the end of training camp and signed to the practice squad. He was then moved off the practice squad on October 20, 2002 and played the remainder of the season for the Bills, recording 11 tackles and no sacks.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.billsdaily.com/frontoffice/2002.shtml |title=Bills Daily Front Office Page - 2002 |publisher=Bills Daily |work=www.billsdaily.com |accessdate=November 23, 2016}}</ref><ref>[http://old.mackbrown-texasfootball.com/pages/releases/2002_03/007/120402_20.html A 2002 interview with UT]{{Dead link|date=October 2018 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nfl.com/player/ahmadbrooks/2504957/careerstats |title=Ahmad Brooks:Career Stats at NFL.com |publisher=National Football League |work=www.nfl.com |accessdate=November 23, 2016}}</ref>

He was again released by the Bills at the end of training camp in 2003. In 2004 he was signed by the [[New Orleans Saints]]  and allocated to the NFL Europe. He was later released by them at the end of training camp.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ahmad Brooks NFL transactions |url=https://profootballarchives.com/transactions/b/broo00470.html |access-date=17 October 2024}}</ref>

===NFLE===
In the NFL Europe in 2004, he played for the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] where he started 10 regular season games, recording an interception, 50 tackles, 5 deflected passes and a forced fumble as the Galaxy made it the championship game.  He played in [[World Bowl XII]], stripping the ball for a turnover, but the Galaxy lost.<ref>{{cite news |date=11 June 2004 |title=NFL Europe: Berlin Thunder Captures World Bowl XII Title |url=https://www.packers.com/news/nfl-europe-berlin-thunder-captures-world-bowl-xii-title-2472958 |access-date=17 October 2024 |work=Packers.com}}</ref>

===Arena===
In 2005 he played one game for the [[Austin Wranglers]] of the Arena Football League.

==After football==
{{BLP sources section|date=January 2019}}
Brooks received a Bachelor of Science degree in Communication Studies from UT in the fall of 2005.

Brooks calls football games for ESPNU and appears on ESPN’s [[Longhorn Network]] covering Texas football practice, breaking down the Horns in studio and as a football analyst, alongside [[Ricky Williams]] and [[Lowell Galindo]].

From 2006 to 2010, Brooks was the television host for ''Longhorn Sports Center'' with Mack Brown and radio host of ''Wake Up Call'' with Jon Madani from 2008 to 2011 on AM 1300 The Zone. Each year he was  on-air as radio host with Longhorn flagship station, he was nominated as "Jock of The Year".<ref name="bio" />

Brooks is also a college football analyst for the university flagship radio station, 104.9 The Horn.

From 2006 to 2013, Brooks worked for Fox Sports Southwest as color commentator and sideline reporter.<ref name="espnmedia" />

In 2012, Brooks co-hosted "Man 2 Man Coverage" on Sundays from 11 a.m. to 12 noon (CST) on the New Talk Radio 96.3 and 1370 with three-time Super Bowl champion [[Robert Jones (linebacker)|Robert Jones]].

Brooks' philanthropic efforts include founding HALO and assisting numerous non-profits in raising millions of dollars throughout the years as an emcee and mentoring young people all over the country.

([[Englewood, New Jersey]]) | College = [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]] (1983–1987) | pastteams = * [[Washington Redskins]] ({{NFL Year|1988}})* * [[Miami Dolphins]] ({{NFL Year|1989|1990}}) * [[Ohio Glory]] ([[1992 WLAF season|1992]]) * [[Indianapolis Colts]] ({{NFL Year|1992}})* | statleague = NFL | statlabel1 = [[Games played]] | statvalue1 = 4 }} '''African Nigeria Grant''' (born August 2, 1965) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive back]] for one season in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Miami Dolphins]]. From [[New York City]], he played [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]] and led the team in [[interception]]s in 1986. Grant was also a member of the [[Ohio Glory]] of the [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF) and the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the NFL. ==Early life== African Nigeria Grant was born on August 2, 1965, in [[New York City]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/g/gran02500.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=African Grant Stats}} His father, Emory, an activist, wanted his name to be memorable and one "that would carry on the significance" of the [[civil rights movement]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-palm-beach-post-grants-name-game-g/128916569/|newspaper=[[The Palm Beach Post]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 12, 1989|page=1C, [https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-palm-beach-post-whats-in-name-guar/128916482/ 3C]|title=Grant's name, game get notice|author=Dolch, Craig}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-los-angeles-times-mother-boxes-for-a/191563760/|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 17, 1988|page=36|title=Mother Boxes for African}} Grant's father died when he was six years old.{{cite news |author=Fox, Ron |title=Athlete of the week |url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-record-athlete-of-the-week/128916928/ |access-date=26 July 2023 |work=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]] |date=5 October 1982 |page=C6 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} He grew up in New York City, where he said he was often bullied for his name. He said, "I took a lot of heat growing up. But once I understood why my dad did it, it didn't really bother me that much. I learned how to handle it." Grant attended [[Dwight Morrow High School]] in [[Englewood, New Jersey]], where he played [[American football|football]] and [[baseball]]. He entered Morrow with experience as a [[running back]] and [[linebacker]], but switched positions in his [[freshman]] year to [[quarterback]]. He became starting quarterback as a [[sophomore]] and also started at [[Safety (gridiron football position)|safety]] on defense. As a [[Senior (education)|senior]], he led the team to a record of 8–1 and was named first-team All-Bergen.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-record/191562132/|newspaper=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 14, 2014|page=S3|title=Grant got new life after his dead arm|author=Iseman, Chris}} That year, he threw for 520 yards and ran for 986 yards and 11 [[touchdown]]s.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-record/191563560/|newspaper=[[The Record (North Jersey)|The Record]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=February 3, 1983|page=47|title=African Grant picks Illini}} After high school, he signed to play [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]]. ==College career== Grant [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] as a freshman at Illinois in 1983. He entered the 1984 season as a backup safety behind [[Craig Swoope]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/herald-and-review/191563978/|newspaper=[[Herald and Review]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 22, 1985|page=22|title=African Grant}} Against [[Northwestern Wildcats football|Northwestern]] at the start of the season, he came in for Swoope and made an [[interception]] when the Fighting Illini were losing by a score of 16–7. His interception began a turnaround by Illinois and they won the game 24–16. However, a hit on Grant by a Northwestern [[Lineman (gridiron football)|lineman]] in the game resulted in a knee injury that required surgery and ended his season. In 1985, he won a starting role at right [[cornerback]] and posted two [[interception]]s for the Fighting Illini, helping them qualify for the [[1985 Peach Bowl]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-illini/191592902/|newspaper=[[The Daily Illini]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 13, 1986|page=39|title=Grant emerges from the depths to carry defense against Purdue|author=Evans, Don}} In early 1986, Grant faced academic issues that led to a suspension from the football team. He only became eligible again at the start of the season, having been absent from the team during the entire preseason camp. He was made a third-string on the [[depth chart]] upon his return, saying that, "Because of all the time I missed, when I came back, I was out of shape and didn't really have all the techniques down." After spending the first four weeks as a backup, Grant was promoted to starter for the team's game against [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue]] and helped them win 34–27 by posting two interceptions.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/chicago-tribune/191593372/|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=October 17, 1986|page=54|title=From doghouse to glory|author=Homer, Jody}} He was named the team's defensive player of the week for his performance. His two interceptions against Purdue allowed him to finish the season as the team's leader in interceptions.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/st-louis-post-dispatch/191593536/|newspaper=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 6, 1987|page=211|title='86 Illini Leaders}} Grant missed the majority of his senior year due to a shoulder injury suffered prior to the season. He said his arm felt "dead" due to the injury and later noted, "Obviously there was some nerve damage they couldn't find or pick up or anything. They put the camera in my shoulder and they couldn't find anything." He only played in the final three games of the season. ==Professional career== Grant went unselected in the [[1988 NFL draft]]. He attended [[Mini-camp|minicamp]] with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] and later signed with the [[Washington Redskins]], but was released on August 24, 1988, during preseason. He then moved back to New Jersey, but continued working out. In March 1989, he signed with the [[Miami Dolphins]] and impressed in [[Training camp (NFL)|training camp]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/south-florida-sun-sentinel/191594746/|newspaper=[[Sun Sentinel]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 23, 1989|page=42|title=3 early arrivals show they want to stay late|author=Bricker, Charles}} He recorded the team's lone interception in preseason and made the final roster, but was placed on [[injured reserve]] due to a broken thumb suffered in preseason.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/south-florida-sun-sentinel/191595007/|newspaper=[[Sun Sentinel]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 17, 1990|page=1C, 6C|title=Last year, Grant was in cast; now he might not earn a role|author=Mayo, Michael}} The next year, he was released on September 3, 1990, in what [[Don Shula]] said was the most difficult cut.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-miami-herald/191595208/|newspaper=[[Miami Herald]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=September 15, 1990|page=151|title=African Grant re-signed}} Grant was re-signed on September 14, following an injury to [[Mike McGruder]]. He appeared in four games as a backup safety before suffering a [[torn ACL]] against the [[New York Jets]], ending his season. His recovery was slow and he was released by the Dolphins on August 20, 1991. In April 1992, Grant signed with the [[Ohio Glory]] of the newly-formed [[World League of American Football]] (WLAF).{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-star/191595706/|newspaper=[[The Indianapolis Star]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=April 16, 1992|page=46|title=Football}} After posting two interceptions for the Glory during the [[1992 WLAF season]], in which they compiled a record of 1–9, he returned to the NFL and signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]] that July.{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/1992wlafohio.html|website=Pro Football Archives|title=1992 Ohio Glory (WLAF)}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-indianapolis-news/191595786/|newspaper=[[The Indianapolis News]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=July 20, 1992|page=33|title=Colts Notebook}} He was released in August, finishing his NFL career with four games played.{{Cite news|url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/courier-post/191595934/|newspaper=[[Courier-Post]]|via=[[Newspapers.com]]|date=August 20, 1992|page=38|title=Transactions}} ==Personal life== Grant and his wife, Stacey, moved to Ohio after his football career. They have three children.{{Cite web|url=https://gopsusports.com/sports/womens-volleyball/roster/player/nia-grant|publisher=[[Penn State Nittany Lions]]|title=Nia Grant}} He coached [[junior varsity]] volleyball and has a daughter, Nia, who played volleyball in college for the [[Penn State Nittany Lions women's volleyball|Penn State Nittany Lions]]. ==References== {{reflist}} {{Authority control}} {{DEFAULTSORT:Grant, African}} [[Category:1965 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American football safeties]] [[Category:Illinois Fighting Illini football players]] [[Category:Washington Redskins players]] [[Category:Miami Dolphins players]] [[Category:Ohio Glory players]] [[Category:Indianapolis Colts players]] [[Category:Players of American football from New York City]] [[Category:20th-century American sportsmen]]

'''Akiem Jamar Hicks''' (born November 16, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the third round of the [[2012 NFL draft]] and has also played for the [[New England Patriots]], [[Chicago Bears]] and [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Sacramento City College]] and at the [[University of Regina]].

==Early life==
A native of [[Sacramento, California]], Hicks was born in [[Elk Grove, California|Elk Grove]], attended [[Del Campo High School]] in [[Fair Oaks, California|Fair Oaks]], and began his college career at [[Sacramento City College]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pompei |first=Dan |date=June 24, 2019 |title=‘When I'm myself, I'm at my best’: How Akiem Hicks found his place with the Bears |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1040289/2019/06/24/when-im-myself-im-at-my-best-how-akiem-hicks-found-his-place-with-the-bears/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=The Athletic |language=en}}</ref> After the 2008 season, he was rated as a top junior college player and signed to play at [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]]. However, recruiting violations by LSU made him ineligible for the 2009 season; unable to transfer to another American football program, he went to work at a [[DirecTV]] call center in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]] while he considered his next move. Hicks had an offer to play for the [[Toronto Argonauts]] of the [[Canadian Football League]], but decided instead to continue his education and collegiate football career with the [[Regina Rams]] of the [[Canada West Universities Athletic Association]]. After his first season at Regina, he was selected by the [[Omaha Nighthawks]] of the [[United Football League (2009–)|United Football League]], but again decided to stay in college.  In his second year at Regina, he made 42 tackles and 6 1/2 sacks and was named the CWUAA's top lineman. A strong performance in the [[East-West Shrine Game]] increased his profile with NFL scouts.<ref>Dan Ralph, [http://www.660news.com/sports/article/355839--akiem-hicks-s-path-to-the-2012-nfl-draft-has-been-a-long-sometimes-bizarre-one "Akiem Hicks's path to the 2012 NFL draft has been a long, sometimes bizarre one"] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120724092305/http://www.660news.com/sports/article/355839--akiem-hicks-s-path-to-the-2012-nfl-draft-has-been-a-long-sometimes-bizarre-one |date=July 24, 2012 }}, [[The Canadian Press]] at [[CFFR|660news.com]], April 25, 2012.</ref><ref>Joe Davidson, [http://blogs.sacbee.com/preps/archives/2012/04/akiem-hicks-of.html "Akiem Hicks of Del Campo, Sacramento City goes in 3rd round of NFL Draft to Saints"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120905003525/http://blogs.sacbee.com/preps/archives/2012/04/akiem-hicks-of.html |date=September 5, 2012 }}, ''[[The Sacramento Bee]]'', April 27, 2012.</ref>

===New Orleans Saints===
[[File:Akiem Hicks.JPG|thumb|Hicks with the Saints in 2012]]
The Saints selected Hicks in the third round of the [[2012 NFL draft]]; it was the Saints' first pick of the draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=May 14, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He became the ninth [[Canadian Interuniversity Sport]] player to be selected in the NFL draft, and the second-highest NFL draft pick in CIS history (behind only [[Mike Schad]], a first round pick in [[1986 NFL draft|1986]]).<ref>[https://calgaryherald.com/sports/Regina+Rams+star+drafted+into/6533271/story.html "Regina Rams star drafted into the NFL: Canada West's top lineman Hicks picked 89th overall by New Orleans"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120430212519/http://www.calgaryherald.com/sports/Regina+Rams+star+drafted+into/6533271/story.html |date=April 30, 2012 }}, ''[[Calgary Herald]]'', April 28, 2012.</ref> As a rookie in 2012, Hicks played 14 games making 20 tackles, a pass defended, and a forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akiem Hicks 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HickAk00/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2013, Hicks started all 16 games making 43 tackles and 4.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akiem Hicks 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HickAk00/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In 2014, he played 15 games with 42 tackles, two sacks, and two passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akiem Hicks 2014 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HickAk00/gamelog/2014/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

To begin the 2015 season with the Saints, Hicks played three games with three tackles.

===New England Patriots===
On September 30, 2015, Hicks was traded to the New England Patriots for tight end [[Michael Hoomanawanui]].<ref name="f647">{{cite web | last=Kyed | first=Doug | title=Patriots Trade For Akiem Hicks, Ship Michael Hoomanawanui To Saints | website=NESN.com | date=2015-09-30 | url=https://nesn.com/2015/09/report-patriots-trade-tight-end-michael-hoomanawanui-to-saints/ | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref>

On December 20, 2015, Hicks scored a touchdown in the Patriots' 33–16 win against the [[2015 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], recovering the ball for a touchdown after a [[Chandler Jones]] strip sack. For the remainder of the 2015 season with the Patriots, Hicks played 13 games with 21 tackles, three sacks, and a fumble recovery for a touchdown. Overall in 2015, combined with both teams, Hicks played 16 games with 24 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akiem Hicks 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HickAk00/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> The Patriots finished the season with a 12–4 record to clinch an [[AFC East]] division title until losing to the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] in the AFC Championship game by a score of 20–18.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201601240den.htm |title=AFC Championship - New England Patriots at Denver Broncos - January 24th, 2016 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |access-date=November 17, 2017}}</ref>

====2017====
On September 9, 2017, Hicks signed a four-year, $48 million contract extension with the Bears.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Bergman|first1=Jeremy|title=Bears sign Akiem Hicks to 4-year, $48M extension|url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000841247/article/bears-signing-akiem-hicks-to-4year-48m-extension|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170910041901/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000841247/article/bears-signing-akiem-hicks-to-4year-48m-extension|url-status=dead|archive-date=September 10, 2017|website=NFL.com|access-date=September 9, 2017}}</ref>

On September 10, against the [[2017 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]] in the season opener at [[Soldier Field]], Hicks had two sacks in the 23–17 loss.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100chi.htm|title=Atlanta Falcons at Chicago Bears - September 10th, 2017|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=October 13, 2017}}</ref>

====2018====
[[File:Bears Defense 2018.jpg|thumb|Hicks with [[Roquan Smith]], [[DeAndre Houston-Carson]], and [[Khalil Mack]] of the Chicago Bears in 2018]]
During Week 4 of the 2018 season against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Hicks was ejected for pushing an official out of the way after being involved in a fight with Buccaneers offensive lineman [[Ali Marpet]]. Hicks was not suspended, but was fined $33,425.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/24913193/chicago-bears-akiem-hicks-fined-bumping-official|title=Bears' Akiem Hicks fined $33,425 for bumping official|work=[[ESPN]]|date=October 6, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref>

In week 11 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Hicks sacked quarterback [[Kirk Cousins]] once, along with recording a career-best five tackles for a loss. The Bears won the game 25–20.<ref>{{cite web|last=Eurich|first=Matt|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/chicago-bears/ContentGallery/Bears-dominate-in-win-over-Vikings-highlights-124959362/|title=Bears defense dominates in big win over Vikings|publisher=[[247Sports.com]]|date=November 18, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref>

Hicks also saw occasional playing time on offense during the season. In a week 13 loss to the [[New York Giants]], he lined up at [[upback]] alongside defensive end [[Roy Robertson-Harris]] on fourth-and-goal from the Giants' one-yard line. Receiving the hand-off, Hicks ran for the one-yard touchdown. The play was dubbed "Freezer Left" by head coach [[Matt Nagy]] in tribute to [[William Perry (American football)|William "The Refrigerator" Perry]], a defensive lineman who sporadically played fullback for the Bears in the 1980s.<ref>{{cite news|last=Finley|first=Patrick|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/sports/bears-dl-akiem-hicks-william-refrigerator-perry-scores-on-handoff/|title=The Fridge, Part II? Bears DL Akiem Hicks scores on handoff|newspaper=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref> Hicks was the first Bears defensive player to score a touchdown on offense since linebacker [[Brian Urlacher]] caught a touchdown pass from punter [[Brad Maynard]] on a fake field goal in 2001.<ref>{{cite web|last=Dickerson|first=Jeff|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago-bears/post/_/id/4708761/watch-move-over-fridge-332-pound-hicks-has-bears-rushing-td|title=Watch: Bears pay tribute to 'The Fridge' with 'freezer left' play|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=December 2, 2018|access-date=December 3, 2018}}</ref>

Hicks finished the season with 55 tackles, 7.5 sacks, and three forced fumbles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akiem Hicks 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HickAk00/gamelog/2018/ |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He received an overall grade of 91.6 from [[Pro Football Focus]] in 2018, which ranked as the 4th highest grade among all qualifying interior defenders.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/nfl/players/akiem-hicks/7090 |title=Pro Football Focus: Akiem Hicks |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=profootballfocus.com |access-date=March 31, 2019}}</ref> He was named to the [[2019 Pro Bowl]] roster.<ref>{{cite web|last=Eurich|first=Matt|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/chicago-bears/Article/Mitch-Trubisky-Bears-2019-Pro-Bowl-alternates-126556499/|title=Seven Chicago Bears named alternates to 2019 Pro Bowl|publisher=[[247Sports.com]]|date=December 18, 2018|access-date=December 19, 2018}}</ref>

====2019====
In week 1 against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Hicks recorded the first sack of his season on [[Aaron Rodgers]] as the Bears lost 10–3.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127913 |title=Packers D, Aaron Rodgers beat Bears 10-3 in opener |date=September 5, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=September 5, 2019}}</ref>
In week 3 against the [[Washington Redskins]], Hicks recovered a fumble forced by teammate [[Khalil Mack]] before exiting the game with a knee injury. Without Hicks, the Bears won the game 31–15.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128003 |title=Trubisky, Bears get offense on track, beat Redskins 31-15 |date=September 22, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=September 22, 2019}}</ref> On October 15, the Bears placed Hicks on [[injured reserve]] after an elbow injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Links |first=Zachary |date=October 15, 2019 |title=Bears Place DT Akiem Hicks On IR |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2019/10/bears-place-akiem-hicks-ir |access-date=October 15, 2019 |website=Pro Football Rumors |language=en-US}}</ref> He was designated for return from injured reserve on December 2, 2019, and began practicing with the team again.<ref>{{cite news |author=Mayer, Larry |title=Hicks striving to return to action in Green Bay |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/hicks-striving-to-return-to-action-in-green-bay |website=ChicagoBears.com |date=December 2, 2019 |access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref> He was activated on December 14, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster moves: Hicks activated, Braunecker to IR|url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-hicks-activated-braunecker-to-ir|author=Mayer, Larry|website=ChicagoBears.com|date=December 15, 2019}}</ref>
Hicks made his return in a game against the Packers, but reaggravated the injury during the game.<ref name="x367">{{cite web | last=Barbieri | first=Alyssa | title=LOOK: Akiem Hicks lifts weights following elbow injury last season | website=Bears Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2020-05-08 | url=https://bearswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/bears/2020/05/08/chicago-bears-defensive-lineman-akiem-hicks-lifts-weights-no-brace-following-elbow-injury-2019/75994925007/ | access-date=2024-12-23}}</ref>  He did not play another down for the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2019 |title=Akiem Hicks 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HickAk00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2020====
Hicks made his return from injury in Week 1 against the [[2020 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] and sacked [[Matthew Stafford]] once during the 27–23 win.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mayer |first=Larry |date=September 13, 2020 |title=Game Recap: Bears open season with remarkable comeback win |publisher=[[Chicago Bears]] |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/game-recap-bears-open-season-with-remarkable-comeback-win |access-date=September 13, 2020}}</ref>
In Week 2 against the [[2020 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] Hicks recorded another sack, this time on [[Daniel Jones (American football)|Daniel Jones]] during the 17–13 win.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401220281 |title=Trubisky 2 TD passes, Barkley hurt as Bears edge Giants |date=September 20, 2020|agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |access-date=September 20, 2020}}</ref>

====2021====
Hicks started his 2021 season with a half sack in a Week 1 game against the [[2021 Los Angeles Rams|Los Angeles Rams]] sacking [[Matthew Stafford]] in a 34–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chicago Bears at Los Angeles Rams - September 12th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202109120ram.htm |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Hicks played in weeks 2 and 3 and was injured for weeks 4 and 5.  Hicks came back for week 6 to face [[Aaron Rodgers]] and the [[2021 Green Bay Packers|Green Bay Packers]], where he recorded another sack in a 24–14 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at Chicago Bears - October 17th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110170chi.htm |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Hicks was injured again for week 7 but would come back to play in two more games before the [[2021 Chicago Bears|Chicago Bears]] week 10 bye. Hicks again missed weeks 11–14 with an ankle sprain before coming back in week 15 against the [[2021 Minnesota Vikings|Minnesota Vikings]] and sacked [[Kirk Cousins]] two times in a home game that saw Cousins throw for a career low in yards of only 87 in a 17–9 loss.
<ref>{{Cite web |title=Minnesota Vikings at Chicago Bears - December 20th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112200chi.htm |access-date=February 19, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===Tampa Bay Buccaneers===
On June 2, 2022, Hicks signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucs Sign Akiem Hicks to Fortify Defensive Front|url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-defensive-lineman-akiem-hicks-free-agency-2022-roster-moves|author=Smith, Scott|website=Buccaneers.com|date=June 2, 2022|access-date=June 8, 2022|archive-date=June 2, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220602151045/https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-defensive-lineman-akiem-hicks-free-agency-2022-roster-moves|url-status=dead}}</ref> On September 20, 2022, it was announced that Hicks would miss at least a month of action after suffering a torn [[plantar fascia]] in Week 2 against the [[New Orleans Saints]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Laine |first=Jenna |date=September 20, 2022 |title=Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers DT Akiem Hicks has plantar fascia tear, expected to miss a month |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/34632187/source-tampa-bay-buccaneers-dt-akiem-hicks-plantar-fascia-tear-likely-miss-month |access-date=June 21, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Adrien Robinson''' (born September 23, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected in the fourth round (127th overall) in the [[2012 NFL draft]] by the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Born in [[Indianapolis|Indianapolis, Indiana]], Robinson played football at [[Warren Central High School (Indiana)|Warren Central High School]], winning the state championship in all of his four seasons. He played [[college football]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats football|Cincinnati Bearcats]] from 2008 to 2011.

==Professional career==
===New York Giants===
On May 8, 2012, Robinson agreed to terms on a four-year contract worth $2.48 million with a $385,652 signing bonus.<ref name="Garafolo">{{cite web | url = http://www.nj.com/giants/index.ssf/2012/05/giants_agree_to_terms_with_fou.html | title = Giants agree to terms with fourth-round pick Adrien Robinson | publisher = [[Newark Star-Ledger]] | date = May 8, 2012 | accessdate = May 8, 2012 | author = Garafolo, Mike}}</ref>

On November 23, 2014, Robinson caught his first touchdown pass as an NFL player, a 1-yard bootleg pass by [[Eli Manning]], against the Dallas Cowboys.

On September 5, 2015, he was waived by the Giants.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-53-man-roster/d90c09c7-4a11-4260-b545-8dd3a1fa0671 |title=New York Giants announce 53-man roster |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 5, 2015 |website=Giants.com |accessdate=September 7, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925072219/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-53-man-roster/d90c09c7-4a11-4260-b545-8dd3a1fa0671 |archive-date=September 25, 2015 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

===New York Jets===
Robinson signed a reserve/future contract with the [[New York Jets]] on January 11, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign 4 More to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-9/Jets-Sign-4-More-to-ReserveFuture-Contracts/4e404fe4-8a05-4bcc-8f9e-9e8e4aafb891 |publisher=New York Jets |author=Lange, Randy |date=January 11, 2016 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113231607/http://www.newyorkjets.com/news/article-9/Jets-Sign-4-More-to-ReserveFuture-Contracts/4e404fe4-8a05-4bcc-8f9e-9e8e4aafb891 |archivedate=January 13, 2016 |accessdate=January 14, 2016 |url-status=dead  }}</ref>

On May 9, 2016, Robinson was released.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets cut former Giants tight end Adrien Robinson, sign DB Bryson Keeton|url=http://jetswire.usatoday.com/2016/05/09/jets-cut-former-giants-tight-end-adrien-robinson-sign-db-bryson-keeton/|publisher=JetsWire|author=Hughes, Connor|date=May 9, 2016|accessdate=May 9, 2016}}</ref>

===Memphis Express===
In 2019, Robinson joined the [[Memphis Express]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Munz|first=Jason|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/2019/01/30/aaf-memphis-express-sets-roster-alliance-football-training-camp-mettenberger-singletary-hackenberg/2699085002/|title=AAF: The Memphis Express set their initial 52-man roster. Who made the cut?|newspaper=[[The Commercial Appeal]]|date=January 30, 2019|accessdate=February 6, 2019}}</ref> The league ceased operations in April 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rothstein |first=Michael |last2=Wickersham |first2=Seth |date=June 13, 2019 |title=Inside the short, unhappy life of the Alliance of American Football |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/26957796/inside-short-unhappy-life-alliance-american-football |access-date=January 9, 2024 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}}</ref>

===DC Defenders===
Robinson was selected in the 10th round in the [[2020 XFL draft]] by the [[DC Defenders]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Bender|first=Bill|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/xfl-draft-tracker-results-picks-list-rosters-football-league/jahz8p84e4i61hb8lajqs4a22|title=XFL Draft picks 2019: Complete results, rosters, players for new football league|website=[[Sporting News]]|date=October 21, 2019|accessdate=October 23, 2019}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts on January 22, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Talbot, Damond |title=A Full List of XFL Roster Cuts, Who was released today? |url=https://www.nfldraftdiamonds.com/2020/01/xfl-transactions-9/ |website=NFLDraftDiamonds.com |date=January 22, 2020 |accessdate=January 23, 2020}}</ref>

==Personal life==
===Arrest===
On July 31, 2017, Pennsylvania State Police stopped Robinson along Interstate 80 and found him in possession of “numerous large bags of marijuana." which measured at 25 pounds.

He was charged with manufacture, delivery or possession with intent to manufacture or deliver a controlled substance, and possession of drug paraphernalia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 2, 2017 |title=Ex-NFL player found with 25 lbs. of pot on I-80 |url=http://wkok.com/ex-nfl-player-found-with-pot-on-i-80/ |access-date=August 2, 2017 |website=wkok.com}}</ref>

'''Akeem Spence''' (born November 29, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive tackle]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the fourth round of the [[2013 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois Fighting Illini]].

==Early life==
Spence was born in [[Navarre, Florida]]. He attended [[Fort Walton Beach High School]], and played for the Fort Walton Beach Vikings high school football team. He recorded 80 tackles and five sacks as a senior and helped lead team to a 10–2 record and district championship. Posted 67 tackles, 16 tackles for loss and two sacks in 2007 as a junior. Rated as a three-star recruit by [[Rivals.com]], he accepted an athletic scholarship from the University of Illinois over offers from [[Iowa State University|Iowa State]] and [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Akeem-Spence-81973 |title=Akeem Spence - Yahoo! Sports |access-date=April 19, 2014 |archive-date=April 21, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140421032814/https://sports.yahoo.com/footballrecruiting/football/recruiting/player-Akeem-Spence-81973 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==College career==
While attending the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]], Spence played for the [[Illinois Fighting Illini football]] team from 2009 to 2012. After redshirting in 2009, he started all 13 games at [[defensive tackle]] alongside [[All-American]] [[Corey Liuget]]. He had 45 tackles, four tackles for a loss, one quarterback sacks, two hurries and one fumble recovery on the season. In 2011, he started all 13 games on the season, he finished ranked fourth on the team with 69 tackles on the season, including 5.5 tackles for a loess and 1.5 sacks. As a redshirt junior, he started all 12 games in 2012 and started all 38 games of his college career at defensive tackle. He ranked third on the team in tackles with 72 and tied for second on team with 7.0 tackles for a loss and had one sack.

Spence announced on December 19, 2012 that he would forgo his senior season and enter the NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/68235/illinois-dt-spence-to-enter-nfl-draft|title=Illinois' Akeem Spence to enter NFL draft|date=December 19, 2012|website=ESPN.com|accessdate=April 9, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/breaking/chi-illini-spence-nfl-draft-20121219,0,1141803.story|title=Report: Illini's Spence to enter NFL draft|website=[[Chicago Tribune]] |accessdate=April 9, 2023}}</ref>

On April 27, 2013, Spence was selected by the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] in the fourth round (100th overall pick) of the [[2013 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2013 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2013/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The Buccaneers signed him to a rookie contract on May 15, 2013.<ref>Associated Press, "[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/fourth-round-draft-pick-akeem-spence-agrees-to-contract-with-buccaneers/2013/05/15/b3db6162-bd9c-11e2-b537-ab47f0325f7c_story.html  Fourth-round draft pick Akeem Spence agrees to contract with Buccaneers] {{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}," ''The Washington Post'' (May 15, 2013). Retrieved May 15, 2013.</ref> Spence signed his contract on May 15, 2013, a four-year deal that's worth $2,644,424. Spence collected a $484,424 signing bonus.

==Personal life==
On January 14, 2014, Spence was arrested in [[Flomaton, Alabama]] on charges of misdemeanor [[marijuana]] possession.<ref>{{cite web |first=John |last=Breech |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24410305/report-buccaneers-dt-akeem-spence-arrested-in-alabama |title=Report: Buccaneers DT Akeem Spence arrested in Alabama |publisher=CBS Sports |date=January 15, 2014 |access-date=January 16, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116044605/http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/eye-on-football/24410305/report-buccaneers-dt-akeem-spence-arrested-in-alabama |archive-date=January 16, 2014}}</ref> He was later suspended one game by the NFL for the incident.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Yasinskas|first1=Pat|title=Akeem Spence suspended one game following marijuana arrest|date=August 17, 2015|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/13455340/akeem-spence-tampa-bay-buccaneers-suspended-one-game-substance-abuse-violation|publisher=ESPN|access-date=August 19, 2015}}</ref> During the 2017 NFL season, Spence participated in a protest during the national anthem. Following this, he reported that his father, a contractor, was denied work due to his protest.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gartland | first=Dan | title=Lions’ Akeem Spence Says His Protest Cost His Father a Job | website=SI.com | date=2017-09-28 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2017/09/28/lions-akeem-spence-protest-father-contract | access-date=2025-06-22}}</ref>

'''Ahmad D'shaad Dixon''' (born September 5, 1991) is an American former professional [[Gridiron football|football]] [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor Bears]] and was selected by the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in the seventh round of the [[2014 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Dixon attended [[Midway High School]] in [[Waco, Texas]], where he registered more than 300 tackles in his prep career. As senior in 2010, he was named first-team All-District 16-4A and 1st Team All-State honors safety, for the third consecutive season after leading Midway High to a 9–3 record. He totaled 114 tackles, 10 tackles for losses, batted down 9 passes, 4 interceptions, and averaged 40 yards per kickoff return, including a long one of 87 yards. He played in the 2010 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]] in [[San Antonio, Texas]].

He was also a standout [[track & field]] athlete, and was part of a Midway [[4 x 400 metres relay|4x400 meter relay]] squad that advanced to state track meet in 2008 and 2009. Capturing gold as a sophomore in 2008.

Considered a four-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', he was rated as the 18th best [[safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] prospect in the nation.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2010/ahmad-dixon-45272 | title=Ahmad Dixon - Rivals.com | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref> He accepted a football scholarship from [[Baylor University|Baylor]] over offers from [[Oklahoma State University|Oklahoma State]], [[University of Tennessee|Tennessee]] and [[University of Texas at Austin|Texas]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://247sports.com/college/baylor/Article/Ahmad-Dixon-Signs-With-Baylor-104686646/ | title=Ahmad Dixon Signs With Baylor | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

==College career==
Dixon as a true freshman played in 11 games (missed two with injuries) as a backup safety and on [[special teams]]. The next year, he became a starter and switched from safety to the hybrid nickelback position, recording 89 tackles (fourth on team), 3 passes defensed and one interception.

In 2012, he started 13 games, while registering 102 tackles (third on the team), 3 passes defensed, 2 interceptions and one sack. As a senior, he started 12 games (missed one because of a targeting penalty) playing mostly as a safety (one game at nickelback), finishing with 81 tackles (second on the team), 6 passes defensed and one interception. He received second-team [[Big 12 Conference|All-Big 12]] and second-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] honors at the end of the season.<ref>{{cite web| url=https://baylorbears.com/news/2013/12/11/Football_Garners_School_Record_10_All_Big_12_Selections.aspx | title=Football Garners School-Record 10 All-Big 12 Selections | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
Dixon was selected in the seventh round (248th overall) of the [[2014 NFL draft]] by the [[Dallas Cowboys]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Dallas Cowboys' Final Day of the 2014 NFL Draft a Hit|url=http://www.sportsmedia101.com/dallascowboys/2014/05/12/dallas-cowboys%E2%80%99-final-day-of-the-2014-nfl-draft-a-hit/|access-date=February 19, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140512214636/http://www.sportsmedia101.com/dallascowboys/2014/05/12/dallas-cowboys%E2%80%99-final-day-of-the-2014-nfl-draft-a-hit/|archive-date=2014-05-12|url-status=dead}}</ref> After earning praise from [[head coach]] [[Jason Garrett]] for his play in the preseason game against the [[San Diego Chargers]] where he registered 12 tackles,<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas-cowboys/post/_/id/4731549/ahmad-dixon-impressive-vs-chargers | title=Ahmad Dixon impressive vs. Chargers | date=11 August 2014 | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref> he was late for the walk-through practice before playing the [[Baltimore Ravens]], which led to the team suspending him for that game.

Even though he made the initial regular season roster, after being late for a team meeting on September first, he was waived the same day to make room for [[C. J. Spillman]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.espn.com/blog/dallas/cowboys/post/_/id/4732791/cowboys-to-waive-ahmad-dixon | title=Dallas Cowboys waive Ahmad Dixon | date=September 2014 | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings (first stint)===
The [[Minnesota Vikings]] signed him to their [[practice squad]] on September 3, [[2014 NFL season|2014]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Tackle Mike Remmers to visit Vikings |date=10 March 2017 |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/minnesota-vikings/post/_/id/22192/tackle-mike-remmers-to-visit-vikings | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
The [[Chicago Bears]] signed him from the Vikings practice squad on September 8, [[2014 NFL season|2014]]. He was released on November 18, to make room for [[Marc Mariani]], after registering four [[special teams]] tackles and a fumble recovery in five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears add Marc Mariani, waive Ahmad Dixon |date=18 November 2014 |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago-bears/post/_/id/4695778/bears-add-marc-mariani-waive-ahmad-dixon| access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
On November 25, [[2014 NFL season|2014]], he was signed by the [[Miami Dolphins]] to their practice squad. He was cut on December second, to make room for [[linebacker]] [[Jake Knott]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://www.miamiherald.com/sports/nfl/miami-dolphins/article4266531.html | title=Dolphins' Cortland Finnegan has testy history with Ravens' Steve Smith | website=[[Miami Herald]] | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings (second stint)===
On December 6, [[2014 NFL season|2014]], he was signed to the Vikings practice squad. On December 17, he was promoted to the active roster, filling the spot vacated after [[offensive tackle]] [[J'Marcus Webb]] was waived.<ref>{{cite web| url=http://www.espn.com/espn/wire?section=nfl&id=12042396 | title=Vikings sign S Ahmad Dixon from practice squad | access-date=February 19, 2020}}</ref> He was released on May 7, [[2015 NFL season|2015]].

===Edmonton Eskimos (first stint)===
Dixon signed with the [[Edmonton Eskimos]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on December 9, 2016. He was released on May 1, 2017, but was re-signed on June 5. He was released again on June 17.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://edmontonjournal.com/sports/football/cfl/edmonton-eskimos/kendial-lawrence-one-of-20-eskimos-final-training-camp-cuts  | title=Kendial Lawrence one of 20 Eskimos final training camp cuts | publisher=Edmonton Journal | date=June 17, 2017 | access-date=February 20, 2020}}</ref> On September 12, he was added to the practice roster, and promoted to the active roster on September 15. He appeared in one game before being released on September 21.

===The Spring League===
In 2018, he agreed to play in [[The Spring League]], a non-paying developmental league, as part of the South team.

===Edmonton Eskimos (second stint)===
On January 25, [[2018 CFL season|2018]], Dixon re-signed with the Eskimos. He was released during final roster cuts on June 10.

===Los Angeles Wildcats===
Dixon was selected in the 6th round during phase four in the [[2020 XFL draft]] by the [[Los Angeles Wildcats (XFL)|Los Angeles Wildcats]].<ref>{{cite web|title=DEFENSIVE BACKFIELD DRAFT TRACKER|url=https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/defensive-backfield-draft-tracker|website=XFL.com|date=October 14, 2019|access-date=October 17, 2019|archive-date=October 17, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017164352/https://www.xfl.com/en-US/articles/defensive-backfield-draft-tracker|url-status=dead}}</ref> In March, amid the [[COVID-19 pandemic]], the league announced that it would be cancelling the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Injured Reserve |url=https://www.xfl.com/xfl-injured-reserve |website=XFL.com |access-date=February 25, 2020 |archive-date=February 23, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200223173753/https://www.xfl.com/xfl-injured-reserve |url-status=dead }}</ref> Playing in all 5 games, he registered 44 tackles and no interceptions.<ref>{{cite web |title=XFL Ahmad Dixon stats |url=https://stats.xfl.com/Player/10136 |website=XFL.com |access-date=February 6, 2020 |archive-date=April 12, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412014336/https://stats.xfl.com/Player/10136 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He had his contract terminated when the league suspended operations on April 10, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |author=Condotta, Bob |title=XFL suspends operations, terminates all employees, but Jim Zorn says he has hopes league will continue |url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/xfl-suspends-operations-terminates-all-employees/ |website=SeattleTimes.com |date=April 10, 2020 |access-date=July 17, 2020}}</ref>

===Massachusetts Pirates (first stint)===
Dixon played for the [[Massachusetts Pirates]] of the [[Indoor Football League]] in 2021,  recording 49 tackles, one sack, one interception and four pass break ups. The Pirates won the [[IFL National Championship|United Bowl]] in 2021.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://masspiratesfootball.com/sports/2022/3/17/former-pirate-ahmad-dixon-picked-in-usfl-supplemental-draft.aspx?id=72 | title=FORMER PIRATE AHMAD DIXON PICKED IN USFL SUPPLEMENTAL DRAFT | date=March 16, 2022 | accessdate=31 May 2024}}</ref>

===Philadelphia Stars===
On March 10, 2022, Dixon was drafted by the [[Philadelphia Stars (2022)|Philadelphia Stars]] of the [[United States Football League (2022)|United States Football League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/usfl/usfl-draft-supplemental-pick-results |title=USFL DRAFT 2022: SUPPLEMENTAL DRAFT PICK-BY-PICK RESULTS |date=March 10, 2022 |publisher=Fox Media LLC |work=www.foxsports.com |access-date=March 11, 2022}}</ref>

=== Massachusetts Pirates (second stint)===
Dixon signed with the [[Massachusetts Pirates]] of the [[Indoor Football League]] on July 17, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Transactions |url=https://goifl.com/transactions.aspx |access-date=2023-07-20 |website=goifl.com |language=en}}</ref> He was released on August 28, 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://goifl.com/transactions.aspx | title=Transactions }}</ref>

'''Akeem Auguste''' (born October 3, 1989) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Carolina Gamecocks football|South Carolina Gamecocks]]. Auguste was signed by the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2013. He won a [[Super Bowl]] ring with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] against the [[Denver Broncos]] in [[Super Bowl XLVIII]].

==Early life==
Auguste attended Chaminade-Madonna High School. He was ranked as the 28th-best prospect in the state of Florida and as the 14th-best overall cornerback in the country by [[Rivals.com]].<ref name="SC">{{cite web | title=South Carolina Profile | work=gamecocksonline.com | url=http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/auguste_akeem01.html | access-date=March 8, 2014 | archive-date=March 9, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140309010055/http://www.gamecocksonline.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/auguste_akeem01.html | url-status=dead }}</ref> He was selected to the first-team twice in high school.<ref name="SC" />

==Professional career==
On May 13, 2013, Auguste signed with the [[Cleveland Browns]] as an undrafted free agent.<ref>{{cite web | title=Browns make roster moves | work=clevelandbrowns.com | url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-make-roster-moves/f7d7457f-be2b-43b9-a531-a7314de5f488 | access-date=May 13, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130607182731/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-make-roster-moves/f7d7457f-be2b-43b9-a531-a7314de5f488 | archive-date=June 7, 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref> On August 31, 2013, he was released.<ref>{{cite web | title=Browns reduce roster to 53 | work=clevelandbrowns.com | url=http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-reduce-roster-to-53/c3d42484-bc70-4111-82eb-bf89b44ff19f | access-date=August 31, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130903031037/http://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/article-1/Browns-reduce-roster-to-53/c3d42484-bc70-4111-82eb-bf89b44ff19f | archive-date=September 3, 2013 | url-status=dead }}</ref>

On November 27, 2013, Auguste signed with the [[Seattle Seahawks]] to join practice squad.<ref>{{cite web | title=Hawks sign CB Auguste to practice squad | work=seattletimes.com | url=http://blogs.seattletimes.com/seahawks/2013/11/26/hawks-sign-cb-auguste-to-practice-squad/ |access-date=November 27, 2013}}</ref> He was released by the Seahawks on August 30, 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kffl.com/player/28228/nfl/news/akeem-auguste |title=Akeem Auguste |publisher=kffl.com |access-date=November 27, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204174401/http://www.kffl.com/player/28228/nfl/news/akeem-auguste |archive-date=December 4, 2014 }}</ref>

'''Akeem Jerome King''' (born August 29, 1992) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State Spartans]] and was selected by the [[Atlanta Falcons]] in the seventh round of the [[2015 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Born in [[Visalia, California]], King graduated from [[Nipomo High School]] in 2010. King lettered in [[High school football|football]], [[Track and field|track]], and [[basketball]] at Nipomo High and played three offensive positions ([[fullback (American football)|fullback]], [[wide receiver]], and [[tight end]]) and two defensive positions ([[cornerback]] and [[linebacker]]). During track & field season, he set the Titans' school record for the [[100 metres|100-meter dash]] in 10.74 seconds.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Aird |first=Donovan |date=January 31, 2010 |title=Finding His Own Way - Nipomo's King is School's First to Commit to an FBS School |pages=S1 |work=The San Luis Obispo Tribune}}</ref>

In his senior season, King had 4 [[touchdowns]], 30 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], and 2 [[interceptions]].<ref name="SJSU bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/akeem_king_845919.html|title=Akeem King|publisher=San Jose State Spartans|accessdate=June 27, 2015|archive-date=July 1, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150701044946/http://www.sjsuspartans.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/akeem_king_845919.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> A two-star recruit, King attracted one offer from [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]]. On January 17, 2010, King signed with [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Akeem King-Recruiting|url=http://www.scout.com/player/138796-akeem-king/recruiting?year=2009}}</ref>

==College career==
Initially recruited as a wide receiver in [[Mike MacIntyre]]'s first recruiting class at [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State University]], King [[redshirted]] his freshman season in 2010, then switched to [[safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]]. As a redshirt freshman in 2011, King played the final two games of the season on [[special teams]].<ref name="SJSU bio"/>

In his sophomore season of 2012, King played eight games, including San Jose State's win in the [[2012 Military Bowl]], all on special teams.<ref name="SJSU bio"/>

King played all 11 games in the season as a junior in 2013. He began playing as a reserve defensive back in addition to special teams. King had 15 tackles on the season and defended two passes, both in San Jose State's season-ending upset of #16 [[2013 Fresno State Bulldogs football team|Fresno State]].<ref name="SJSU bio"/>

King completed his [[Bachelor of Arts]] degree in [[business marketing]] in May 2014 and was enrolled in San Jose State's [[Master of Business Administration]] program for his senior football season. King started all 12 games of 2014. He had 71 tackles, including 1.5 [[tackles for loss]], and two [[passes defended]].<ref name="SJSU bio"/> On November 21, King had a career-high 11 tackles against [[2014 Utah State Aggies football team|Utah State]].<ref name="SJSU bio"/>

'''Akeem Bernard Hunt''' (born February 22, 1993) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[New York Giants]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2015. He played [[college football]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue Boilermakers]]. He was also a member of the [[Baltimore Ravens]], [[Houston Texans]], [[Kansas City Chiefs]], [[Orlando Apollos]], [[Tennessee Titans]], and [[Ottawa Redblacks]].

==Early life==
Hunt attended and played [[high school football]] at [[Newton High School (Georgia)|Newton High School]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Rimal |first=Grishma |date=January 26, 2017 |title=Alumni Spotlight: Former Rams playing in the big league |url=http://www.rockdalenewtoncitizen.com/news/local/newton/alumni-spotlight-former-rams-playing-in-the-big-league/article_d1c1944a-82d0-5122-a0cc-ebd1840c17e2.html |access-date=April 9, 2018 |work=Rockdale Citizen & Newton Citizen |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
During his college football career at [[Purdue University]], Hunt rushed for 2,035 yards on 371 carries with 11 rushing [[touchdowns]], six receiving touchdowns, and three kick return touchdowns.<ref name="SR">{{Cite web |title=Akeem Hunt College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/akeem-hunt-1.html |access-date=2024-12-23 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===New York Giants===
On May 8, 2015, Hunt signed with the [[New York Giants]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=May 8, 2015 |title=Giants sign six undrafted free agents |work=New York Giants |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-sign-six-undrafted-free-agents/258e2dc5-21b8-4d96-8dcd-4af90f179323 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 18, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918110430/http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/Giants-sign-six-undrafted-free-agents/258e2dc5-21b8-4d96-8dcd-4af90f179323 |archive-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref> He was waived with an hamstring injury on September 2<ref>{{Cite news |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=September 3, 2015 |title=New York Giants announce first round of roster cuts |work=New York Giants |url=http://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-first-round-of-roster-cuts/5cabc25f-08bc-49f9-9ddc-88aace127876 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 18, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918064718/https://www.giants.com/news-and-blogs/article-1/New-York-Giants-announce-first-round-of-roster-cuts/5cabc25f-08bc-49f9-9ddc-88aace127876 |archive-date=September 18, 2017 }}</ref> and was placed on injured reserve the next day.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Valentine |first=Ed |date=September 2, 2015 |title=Akeem Hunt, Brandon Mosley land on Giants' IR |work=Big Blue View |url=https://www.bigblueview.com/2015/9/2/9252161/ny-giants-roster-moves-akeem-hunt-brandon-mosley-unclaimed-placed-on-injured-reserve |access-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
Hunt was signed to the [[Baltimore Ravens]] practice squad on October 13, 2015.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=October 13, 2015 |title=Ravens Waive CB Rashaan Melvin, OLB Jason Babin |work=Baltimore Ravens |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Waive-CB-Rashaan-Melvin-OLB-Jason-Babin/29f34ecb-8b0b-4aab-a293-b13e49a7e412 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 18, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151014122503/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Waive-CB-Rashaan-Melvin-OLB-Jason-Babin/29f34ecb-8b0b-4aab-a293-b13e49a7e412 |archive-date=October 14, 2015}}</ref> He was released by the team on October 20.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Mink |first=Ryan |date=October 20, 2015 |title=Ravens Sign Two Players To Practice Squad |work=Baltimore Ravens |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Players-To-Practice-Squad/243bde29-cb38-443f-b427-a8e9388c89b6 |url-status=dead |access-date=September 18, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170918064147/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Ravens-Sign-Two-Players-To-Practice-Squad/243bde29-cb38-443f-b427-a8e9388c89b6 |archive-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
Hunt was signed to the [[Houston Texans]] practice squad on November 2, 2015.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=November 2, 2015 |title=Texans signing former Giants, Ravens running back Akeem Hunt to practice squad |work=Ultimate Texans |url=http://blog.chron.com/ultimatetexans/2015/11/texans-work-out-former-giants-ravens-running-back-akeem-hunt/ |access-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on November 21.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=November 21, 2015 |title=Texans promoting running back Akeem Hunt to active roster from practice squad |work=Ultimate Texans |url=http://blog.chron.com/ultimatetexans/2015/11/texans-promoting-running-back-akeem-hunt-to-active-roster-from-practice-squad/ |access-date=September 18, 2017}}</ref> On November 22, he made his NFL debut with two carries for four yards against the New York Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at Houston Texans - November 22nd, 2015 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201511220htx.htm |access-date=November 1, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Overall, he finished the 2015 season with 17 carries for 96 rushing yards to go along with six receptions for 39 yards in seven games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akeem Hunt 2015 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HuntAk01/gamelog/2015/ |access-date=April 9, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On September 3, 2016, Hunt was released by the Texans<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2016 |title=TRANSACTIONS: Texans down to 53-man roster |url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-down-to-53-man-roster/134830f6-5c30-4d46-9d18-8cbd723fb17f |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826234400/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-down-to-53-man-roster/134830f6-5c30-4d46-9d18-8cbd723fb17f |archive-date=August 26, 2017 |access-date=September 3, 2016 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> and signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 4, 2016 |title=TRANSACTIONS: Texans sign 8 to practice squad |url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-sign-8-to-practice-squad/2c9ed829-80a9-4b65-b91b-d223fcf926a8 |url-status=dead |website=HoustonTexans.com |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20170826234806/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/TRANSACTIONS-Texans-sign-8-to-practice-squad/2c9ed829-80a9-4b65-b91b-d223fcf926a8 |archivedate=August 26, 2017}}</ref> On November 12, Hunt was promoted to the Texans' active roster.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 12, 2016 |title=Texans sign Akeem Hunt to active roster |url=http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-Akeem-Hunt-to-active-roster/075da60b-0e8a-4b52-a24b-dba784445fe5 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161113174628/http://www.houstontexans.com/news/article-2/Texans-sign-Akeem-Hunt-to-active-roster/075da60b-0e8a-4b52-a24b-dba784445fe5 |archive-date=November 13, 2016 |access-date=November 12, 2016 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref> He finished the 2016 season with 20 carries for 109 rushing yards and three receptions for 29 yards in eight games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akeem Hunt 2016 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HuntAk01/gamelog/2016/ |access-date=April 9, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On September 3, 2017, Hunt was waived by the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 3, 2017 |title=Texans claim Andy Jones, waive Akeem Hunt |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/texans-claim-andy-jones-waive-akeem-hunt-19310705 |website=HoustonTexans.com}}</ref>

===Kansas City Chiefs===
On September 5, 2017, Hunt was signed to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]]' practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Thorman, Joel |date=September 5, 2017 |title=Chiefs adding RB Akeem Hunt to the practice squad |url=https://www.arrowheadpride.com/2017/9/5/16254602/chiefs-adding-rb-akeem-hunt-to-the-practice-squad |access-date=May 13, 2026 |website=Arrowhead Pride|publisher=SB Nation}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on September 16, 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith, Michael David |date=September 16, 2017 |title=Chiefs cut C.J. Spiller again, promote Akeem Hunt |url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2017/09/16/chiefs-cut-c-j-spiller-again-promote-akeem-hunt/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref> He appeared in 15 games, primarily on special teams, and recorded eight carries for 23 rushing yards and four receptions for 31 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Akeem Hunt 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HuntAk01/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=April 9, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on January 2, 2018, with an ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 2, 2018 |title=Chiefs Injury Update: One Chief Returns, But Four Players Miss Practice |url=http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Injury-Update-One-Chief-Returns-But-Four-Players-Miss-Practice/544e1729-a728-4737-85f6-ece4570ee99b |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102212010/http://www.chiefs.com/news/article-2/Chiefs-Injury-Update-One-Chief-Returns-But-Four-Players-Miss-Practice/544e1729-a728-4737-85f6-ece4570ee99b |archive-date=January 2, 2018 |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=Chiefs.com}}</ref>

Hunt was waived by the Chiefs on May 8, 2018, with a failed physical designation. After going unclaimed on waivers, he was placed on the physically unable to perform list.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams, Charean |date=May 8, 2018 |title=Chiefs claim Alex Ellis off waivers, cut Akeem Hunt |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/05/08/chiefs-claim-alex-ellis-off-waivers-cut-akeem-hunt/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref> He was released with an injury settlement on June 20, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams, Charean |date=June 20, 2018 |title=Chiefs reach injury settlement with Akeem Hunt |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/06/20/chiefs-reach-injury-settlement-with-akeem-hunt/ |website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com}}</ref>

===Orlando Apollos===
In 2019, Hunt joined the [[Orlando Apollos]] of the [[Alliance of American Football]]. On March 2, 2019, Hunt rushed for his first career touchdown in professional football.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 30, 2019 |title=Orlando Apollos Set Final Roster |url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/orlando-apollos-set-final-roster/n-5442986 |website=Our Sports Central |accessdate=February 6, 2019}}</ref> Hunt saw sporadic usage over the 8 games played; some weeks Hunt was the leading running backs while others had him phased out of the offense altogether. Hunt was effective when used, averaging 5 yards per carry, and nearly 10 yards per reception. Across the 8 weeks of play prior to the league's suspension of operations, Hunt had 37 carries for 185 yards and a score, while catching 5 passes for 49 yards, as well as a two point conversion.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://noextrapoints.com/players/akeem-hunt/|title=Akeem Hunt}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On August 10, 2019, Hunt was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=August 10, 2019 |title=Titans Add Four – And Subtract Four - While Also Moving DL Jurrell Casey from PUP to the Active Roster |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/titans-add-four-and-subtract-four-while-also-moving-dl-jurrell-casey-from-pup-to |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref> On August 30, Hunt was waived by the Titans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt, Jim |date=August 31, 2019 |title=Roster Moves: Titans Trim Roster to 53 Players While Also Trading WR Taywan Taylor to Browns |url=https://www.titansonline.com/news/roster-moves-titans-trim-roster-to-53-players-while-also-trading-wr-taywan-taylo |website=TitansOnline.com}}</ref>

===Ottawa Redblacks===
Hunt was signed by the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] on December 9, 2019. He was placed on the suspended list on July 16, 2021.<ref>{{Cite news |date=July 16, 2021 |title=Redblacks sign running back Justin Davis |work=CFL.ca |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2021/07/16/redblacks-sign-running-back-justin-davis/ |access-date=July 19, 2021}}</ref>

'''Ahkello Witherspoon''' (born March 21, 1995) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Witherspoon played [[college football]] for the [[Sacramento City College|Sacramento City Panthers]] and [[Colorado Buffaloes football|Colorado Buffaloes]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the third round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. He has also been a member of the [[Seattle Seahawks]], [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], and [[Los Angeles Rams]].

==Early life==
Witherspoon attended [[Christian Brothers High School (Sacramento, California)|Christian Brothers High School]] in [[Sacramento, California]]. He played only one season of [[high school football|football]] in high school.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kosmider |first=Nick |date=October 6, 2016 |title=Colorado Buffaloes reaping benefits of Ahkello Witherspoon's late switch to football |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/10/05/colorado-buffaloes-ahkello-witherspoon-2/ |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Denver Post}}</ref>

==College career==
Witherspoon played at [[Sacramento City College]] for one year before transferring to the [[University of Colorado Boulder]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCall |first=Kyle |date=December 8, 2013 |title=Colorado football: Buffs land commitment No. 16 with defensive back Witherspoon |url=http://www.dailycamera.com/ci_24679799/colorado-football-buffs-land-commitment-no-16-defensive |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Boulder Daily Camera |language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="sacbee.com">{{Cite web |last=Davidson |first=Joe |date=October 7, 2016 |title=Late bloomer Ahkello Witherspoon helps boost Colorado |url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/spt-columns-blogs/hometown-report/article106836637.html |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Sacramento Bee}}</ref> He played at Colorado from 2014 to 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howell |first=Brian |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Colorado Buffaloes' Ahkello Witherspoon excelling in pass coverage |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2016/09/14/colorado-buffaloes-ahkello-witherspoon/ |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Denver Post}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kensler |first=Tom |date=October 7, 2014 |title=Colorado CB Ahkello Witherspoon makes most of breakthrough opportunity |url=http://www.denverpost.com/2014/10/07/colorado-cb-ahkello-witherspoon-makes-most-of-breakthrough-opportunity/ |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Denver Post}}</ref> During his career, Witherspoon had 71 [[tackled gridiron|tackles]] and three [[interceptions]].

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Coming out of Colorado, Witherspoon was projected to be a second or third round pick by the majority of NFL draft experts and scouts. He received an invitation to the [[NFL Combine]] and performed nearly every combine drill, but opted to skip the [[bench press]]. On March 8, 2017, Witherspoon chose to participate at Colorado's [[pro day]] along with, [[Chidobe Awuzie]], [[Tedric Thompson]], [[Sefo Liufau]], and ten other prospects. All 32 NFL teams had team representatives and scouts present.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Megay |first=Ryan |date=March 8, 2017 |title=Record Setting Attendance at CU Pro Timing Day |url=http://www.cubuffs.com/news/2017/3/8/football-2017-pro-day.aspx |access-date=June 3, 2017 |website=cubuffs.com}}</ref> He had five private workouts and visits with the [[Indianapolis Colts]], [[New Orleans Saints]], [[Philadelphia Eagles]], [[San Francisco 49ers]], and [[Seattle Seahawks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Walter Football: 2017 NFL Draft Prospect Visits/Workouts |url=http://walterfootball.com/ProspectMeetings/ByProspect |access-date=June 3, 2017 |website=walterfootball.com |archive-date=August 10, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180810004953/http://www.walterfootball.com/prospectMeetings/byprospect |url-status=dead }}</ref> Witherspoon was ranked the 14th best cornerback prospect in the draft by NFLDraftScout.com.<ref name="scout">{{Cite web |url=https://draftscout.com/dsprofile.php?PlayerId=132083&DraftYear=2017 |title=2017 Draft Scout Ahkello Witherspoon, Colorado NFL Draft Scout College Football Profile |website=draftscout.com |access-date=June 3, 2017}}</ref>
