===San Francisco 49ers===
====2017====
[[File:Ahkello Witherspoon with 49ers.jpg|thumb|Witherspoon as a rookie with the [[San Francisco 49ers]], 2017]]
The 49ers selected Witherspoon in the third round (66th overall) of the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fann, Joe |date=April 28, 2017 |title=San Francisco 49ers Draft Colorado CB Ahkello Witherspoon |url=http://www.49ers.com/news/article-2/San-Francisco-49ers-Draft-Colorado-CB-Ahkello-Witherspoon/71d6c88c-d807-47c6-ba5c-970c4b12826d |website=49ers.com}}</ref> He was the 11th cornerback selected in the draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 

On May 12, 2017, the 49ers signed Witherspoon to a four-year, [[United States dollar|$]]3.88 million [[contract]] that included an initial [[signing bonus]] of $973,572.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Spotrac.com: Ahkello Witherspoon contract |url=http://www.spotrac.com/nfl/san-francisco-49ers/ahkello-witherspoon-21808/ |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

Throughout [[training camp]], Witherspoon competed against [[Dontae Johnson]], [[Rashard Robinson]], and [[Keith Reaser]] to earn a role as a starting cornerback following the departure of [[Jimmie Ward]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ourlads.com: San Francisco 49ers' depth chart: 08/01/2017 |url=http://www.ourlads.com/nfldepthcharts/archive/198/SF |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=ourlads.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Kyle Shanahan]] named Witherspoon a backup cornerback to begin the season and listed him as the fifth cornerback on the depth chart, behind Johnson, Robinson, [[K'Waun Williams]], and Reaser.<ref>{{cite web| title=49ers release unofficial Week 1 depth chart| url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-release-unofficial-week-1-depth-chart-19321383 |access-date=February 4, 2025| website=49ers.com| date=September 5, 2017}}</ref>

Witherspoon was inactive as a healthy scratch for the first four games (Weeks 1–4) of the season. On September 16, 2017, the 49ers released Reaser, but opted to sign [[Asa Jackson]] to the active roster with Witherspoon remaining inactive. Heading into Week 5, he had surpassed Asa Jackson on the depth chart and was promoted to the fourth cornerback on the depth chart. On October 8, 2017, Witherspoon made his professional regular season debut, but was limited to a solo tackle during a 26–23 overtime road loss to the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref name="a069">{{cite web | last=Fucillo | first=David | title=49ers-Colts inactives: Ahkello Witherspoon active for the first time | website=Niners Nation | date=2017-10-08 | url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2017/10/8/16443860/49ers-colts-inactives-ahkello-witherspoon-active-for-the-first-time | access-date=2024-12-20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Indianapolis Colts - October 8th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710080clt.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Entering Week 8, defensive coordinator [[Robert Saleh]] promoted Witherspoon to the starting cornerback after Rashard Robinson was benched following disappointing performances and repetitive penalties. Witherspoon earned his first career start in Week 8 against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], recording three solo tackles, a pass deflection, and his first career interception on a pass attempt thrown by [[Carson Wentz]] to wide receiver [[Mack Hollins]] during the 33–10 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Philadelphia Eagles - October 29th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201710290phi.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> [[Pro Football Focus]] graded Witherspoon the best player on the 49ers during the matchup against the Eagles and credited him with allowing three receptions on eight targets.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wagoner |first=Nick |date=November 1, 2017 |title=Penalties, belief in Ahkello Witherspoon led to Rashard Robinson trade |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/san-francisco-49ers/post/_/id/28511/penalties-49ers-belief-in-ahkello-witherspoon-led-to-rashard-robinson-trade |access-date=November 7, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> Two days later, the 49ers traded Robinson to the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{cite web |author=Lewis, Edward |date=October 31, 2017 |title=Niners trade Rashard Robinson to New York Jets |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/niners-trade-rashard-robinson-to-new-york-jets-0ap3000000870483 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> Head coach [[Kyle Shanahan]] stated that Witherspoon would be the starting cornerback, opposite Dontae Johnson, moving forward and his development was one of the key factors in their decision to trade Robinson. He surpassed [[Leon Hall]], [[Greg Mabin]], and K'Waun Williams on the depth chart. During Week 16 against the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], Witherspoon had three combined tackles (two solo), set a season-high with two pass deflections, and also intercepted a pass by [[Blake Bortles]] to wide receiver [[Keelan Cole]] in the 44–33 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at San Francisco 49ers - December 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240sfo.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="s024">{{cite web | last=Maniego | first=Florito | title=Ahkello Witherspoon: Why 49ers cornerback will have a breakout year in 2018 | website=Niner Noise | date=2018-02-01 | url=https://ninernoise.com/2018/01/31/ahkello-witherspoon-49ers-cornerback-breakout-year-2018/ | access-date=2024-12-20}}</ref> In the regular season finale against the [[2017 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]], Witherspoon collected a season-high tying four solo tackles and a pass deflection during the 34–13 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams - December 31st, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712310ram.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Witherspoon finished his rookie year with 32 combined tackles (28 solo), seven pass deflections, and two interceptions in 12 games and nine starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WithAh00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2018====
Throughout training camp, Witherspoon competed against K'Waun Williams, Jimmie Ward, [[D. J. Reed]], [[Emmanuel Moseley]], [[Tarvarius Moore]], and [[Tarvarus McFadden]] to be the No. 2 starting cornerback.<ref>{{cite web |title=2018 San Francisco 49ers starters, 53-man roster, schedule prediction |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/san-francisco-49ers/post/_/id/31930/san-francisco-49ers-53-man-roster-projection-final-cuts-2018 |access-date=February 4, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=Nick Wagoner| date=September 8, 2018}}</ref> Head coach Kyle Shanahan named Witherspoon and [[Richard Sherman (American football)|Richard Sherman]] the starting cornerbacks to begin the regular season.<ref>{{cite web| title=49ers depth chart updated to reflect Jimmy Garoppolo injury, new linebacker lineup| url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2018/9/27/17910558/49ers-depth-hart-week-4-vs-chargers-jimmy-garoppolo-injury-reuben-foster-malcolm-smith-fred-warner| access-date=April 18, 2025| website=ninersnation.com| date=September 27, 2018| author=David Fucillo}}</ref>

During a Week 3 38–27 road loss to the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Witherspoon collected a season-high five solo tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Kansas City Chiefs - September 23rd, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201809230kan.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During Week 15 against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], he had a solo tackle before leaving the eventual 26–23 overtime victory in the third quarter with a knee injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Seattle Seahawks at San Francisco 49ers - December 16th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201812160sfo.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Madson |first=Kyle |date=December 16, 2018 |title=Ahkello Witherspoon injures knee vs. Seahawks, OUT for game |url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/niners/2018/12/16/ahkello-witherspoon-injured-on-49ers-first-defensive-series/79912776007/ |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Niners Wire |language=en-US}}</ref> On December 18, 2018, Witherspoon was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 18, 2018 |title=49ers Place Ahkello Witherspoon on IR, Sign Tyvis Powell |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-place-ahkello-witherspoon-on-ir-sign-tyvis-powell |access-date=September 30, 2019 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

Witherspoon finished his sophomore professional season with 37 combined tackles (30 solo), four pass deflections, and a fumble recovery in 14 games and 12 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WithAh00.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2019====
Witherspoon entered training camp projected to be the No. 2 starting cornerback. He competed against [[Jason Verrett]], K'Waun Williams, and D. J. Reed.<ref>{{cite web| title=49ers 2019 roster battles: Who is a lock at cornerback?| url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2019/9/3/20848065/49ers-release-first-unofficial-depth-chart-of-the-regular-season| access-date=April 18, 2025| website=ninersnation.com| date=June 5, 2019| author=Rob Lowder}}</ref> Head coach Kyle Shanahan named Witherspoon a starting cornerback to begin the season and paired him with Richard Sherman.<ref>{{cite web| title=49ers release first unofficial depth chart of the regular season| url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2019/6/5/18651645/49ers-2019-roster-battles-cornerback-richard-sherman-ahkello-witherspoon-jason-verrett| access-date=April 18, 2025| website=ninersnation.com| date=September 8, 2019| author=Kyle Posey}}</ref>

During the season-opening 31–17 road victory over the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], Witherspoon had two solo tackles, a season-high with three pass deflections, and intercepted a pass thrown by [[Jameis Winston]] to running back [[Dare Ogunbowale]] and returned it 25 yards for his first career touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2019 |title=Sherman, 49ers upend Winston, Buccaneers 31-7 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128010 |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=[[ESPN]] |agency=Associated Press}}</ref> Witherspoon was inactive due to a foot injury for six consecutive games (Weeks 5–10). In the regular season finale against the Seahawks, he recorded a season-high five solo tackles and two pass deflections during the 26–21 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks - December 29th, 2019 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201912290sea.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Witherspoon finished the regular season with 28 combined tackles (24 solo), a career-high nine pass deflections, an interception, and a touchdown in 10 games and eight starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WithAh00.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The 49ers finished the season atop the [[NFC West]] with a 13–3 record and clinched the #1-seed in the playoffs. In the Divisional Round against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], Witherspoon was demoted to a backup role to [[Emmanuel Moseley]] after a poor performance. The 49ers went on to reach [[Super Bowl LIV]], but lost 31–20 to the Chiefs. Witherspoon finished the Super Bowl with one tackle.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LIV - San Francisco 49ers vs. Kansas City Chiefs - February 2nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202002020kan.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 

====2020====
During training camp, Witherspoon competed against [[Emmanuel Moseley]] to be the No. 2 starting cornerback. Head coach Kyle Shanahan named him a backup and listed Witherspoon as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind Richard Sherman, Moseley, and [[K'Waun Williams]].<ref>{{cite web| title=2020 Training Camp Preview: Cornerbacks| url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-cornerbacks-camp-sherman-moseley-witherspoon-verrett| access-date=April 18, 2020| website=49ers.com| date=July 22, 2020| author=Keiana Martin}}</ref>

Witherspoon was inactive for two games (Weeks 3–4) after injuring his hamstring.<ref>{{cite web| title=49ers inactive list vs. Giants: Ahkello Witherspoon officially out| url=https://ninerswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/niners/2020/09/27/49ers-inactive-list-vs-giants-ahkello-witherspoon-officially-out/79791496007/| access-date=April 18, 2025| website=ninerswire.usatoday.com| author=Kyle Madson| date=September 27, 2020}}</ref> After Week 8, Witherspoon was placed at the bottom of the depth chart as the eighth cornerback, behind Jason Verrett, Emmanuel Moseley, K'Waun Williams, [[Jamar Taylor]], Dontae Johnson, and [[Ken Webster (American football)|Ken Webster]].<ref>{{cite web| title=49ers inactives: Ahkello Witherspoon is a healthy scratch| url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2020/11/15/21566336/49ers-inactives-ahkello-witherspoon-is-a-healthy-scratch| access-date=April 18, 2025| website=ninersnation.com| author=Kyle Posey| date=November 15, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=49ers Inactives: Ahkello Witherspoon gets benched| url=https://www.knbr.com/2020/11/05/49ers-inactives-ahkello-witherspoon-gets-benched/| access-date=April 18, 2025| website=knbr.com| author=Jacob Hutchinson| date=November 5, 2020}}</ref> Witherspoon was inactive as a healthy scratch for three games (Weeks 9, 10, and 12). Entering Week 13, Witherspoon was promoted to being the fourth cornerback on the depth chart after both [[Emmanuel Moseley]] and [[K'Waun Williams]] suffered injuries.

During a Week 15 41–33 road loss to the [[2020 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], Witherspoon earned his second start of the season, appearing as a nickelback and recorded a solo tackle and a season-high two pass deflections.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys - December 20th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012200dal.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Arizona Cardinals]], Witherspoon set a season-high with seven solo tackles, made one pass deflection, and had his first career interception on a pass attempt thrown by [[Kyler Murray]] to wide receiver [[Christian Kirk]] late in the fourth quarter to help secure a 20–12 road victory for the 49ers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Arizona Cardinals – December 26th, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202012260crd.htm |access-date=December 26, 2020 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Witherspoon finished the 2020 season with 20 combined tackles (17 solo), four pass deflections, and an interception in 11 games and four starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WithAh00.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks===
On March 19, 2021, the [[Seattle Seahawks]] signed Witherspoon to a one-year, $4 million contract that was fully guaranteed and included an initial signing bonus of $2.5 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |date=March 19, 2021 |title=Seahawks Sign Cornerback Ahkello Witherspoon |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-sign-cornerback-ahkello-witherspoon |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> Defensive coordinator [[Ken Norton Jr.]] held an open competition between [[D. J. Reed]], [[Tre Brown]], [[Tre Flowers]], [[Damarious Randall]], and [[Pierre Desir]] in order to select their starting cornerbacks.<ref>{{cite web| title=Top 2021 Seahawks Training Camp Storylines: Who Wins The Starting Cornerback Jobs?| url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/top-2021-seahawks-training-camp-storylines-who-wins-the-starting-cornerback-jobs| access-date=April 18, 2025|website=Seahawks.com| author=John Boyle| date=July 14, 2021}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
====2021====
On September 3, 2021, the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] executed a trade and agreed to send their [[2023 NFL draft|2023]] fifth-round pick (151st overall) to the [[2021 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] in return for Witherspoon.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=September 3, 2021 |title=Steelers agree to trade for Witherspoon |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-agree-to-trade-for-witherspoon |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> Upon his initial arrival, head coach [[Mike Tomlin]] listed Witherspoon as the sixth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind [[Joe Haden]], [[Cameron Sutton]], [[James Pierre]], [[Arthur Maulet]], and [[Justin Layne]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Steelers release updated depth chart heading into Week 1| url=https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/2021/9/6/22659718/steelers-release-updated-depth-chart-heading-into-week-1-chuks-okorafor-dan-moore-kendrick-green-nfl| access-date= April 19, 2025| website=behindthesteelcurtain.com| date=September 6, 2021| author=Dave Schofield}}</ref>

Witherspoon was inactive for the season-opening 23–16 road victory over the [[2021 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. He remained inactive as a healthy scratch for the next seven games (Weeks 3–10). Going into Week 11, defensive coordinator [[Keith Butler (American football)|Keith Butler]] promoted Witherspoon and listed him as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart after Joe Haden injured his foot and remained inactive for four games. During Week 13, Witherspoon had a season-high five solo tackles and a pass deflection in a narrow 20–19 victory over the [[2021 Baltimore Ravens season|Baltimore Ravens]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Pittsburgh Steelers - December 5th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112050pit.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the Vikings on Thursday Night Football, he recorded four solo tackles, three pass deflections, and set a new career-high with two interceptions on pass attempts thrown by [[Kirk Cousins]] during the 36–28 road loss.<ref name="l204">{{cite web | last=Straley | first=Owen | title=Film Room: CB Ahkello Witherspoon Tape Evaluation | website=Steelers Depot | date=2021-12-17 | url=https://steelersdepot.com/2021/12/film-room-cb-ahkello-witherspoon-tape-evaluation/ | access-date=2024-12-20}}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[2021 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]] on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Witherspoon tied his season-high with three pass deflections and also set a new career-high with his third interception of the season on a pass by [[Baker Mayfield]] to wide receiver [[Donovan Peoples-Jones]] in the 26–14 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Pittsburgh Steelers - January 3rd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201030pit.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Witherspoon finished the 2021 season with 15 combined tackles (14 solo), nine pass deflections, and a career-high three interceptions in nine games and three starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WithAh00.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

====2022====
On March 25, 2022, the Steelers signed Witherspoon to a two-year, $8 million contract extension with an initial [[signing bonus]] of $2.96 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=March 25, 2022 |title=Witherspoon signed to two-year contract |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/witherspoon-signed-to-two-year-contract |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref> He entered training camp projected to be the No. 3 cornerback on the depth chart under the Steelers' new defensive coordinator [[Teryl Austin]]. Austin was hired to replace Keith Butler after he chose to retire. Head coach [[Mike Tomlin]] named Witherspoon the No. 1 starting cornerback to begin the season in lieu of [[Levi Wallace]] and paired him with [[Cameron Sutton]]. 

Witherspoon started during the season-opener at the [[2022 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] and had a season-high with eight combined tackles (six solo), a pass deflection, and his lone interception of the season on a pass by [[Joe Burrow]] to wide receiver [[Tyler Boyd (American football)|Tyler Boyd]] in the fourth quarter of the 23–20 overtime road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cincinnati Bengals - September 11th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209110cin.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the Browns on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', Witherspoon recorded five combined tackles (four solo) and a pass deflection before leaving the eventual 29–17 road loss with a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Pittsburgh Steelers at Cleveland Browns - September 22nd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209220cle.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Ahkello Witherspoon leaves game in 3rd quarter, ruled out|url=https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/2022/9/22/23367948/ahkello-witherspoon-leaves-game-in-3rd-quarter-ruled-out-pittsburgh-steelers-news-updates-cornerback| access-date=April 19, 2025| website=behindthesteelcurtain.com| date=September 22, 2022| author=Dave Schofield}}</ref> He was inactive for the next four games (Weeks 4–7) due to his injury.<ref>{{cite web| title=As expected, Ahkello Witherspoon inactive for the Steelers in Week 7 |url=https://www.behindthesteelcurtain.com/2022/10/23/23419563/as-expected-ahkello-witherspoon-inactive-for-the-steelers-in-week-7-sims-rudolph-green-robinson-news| access-date=April 19, 2025| website=behindthesteelcurtain.com| date=October 23, 2022| author=Dave Schofield}}</ref>

During a Week 8 35–13 road loss to the Eagles, Witherspoon returned from injury and made five solo tackles before head coach Mike Tomlin benched him for the second half after Witherspoon gave up two touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon’s lost 2022 could mean he isn’t back with Steelers in 2023 |url=https://triblive.com/sports/ahkello-witherspoons-lost-2022-could-mean-he-isnt-back-with-steelers-in-2023/ |access-date=April 19, 2025 |website=triblive.com |date=January 12, 2023 |author=Chris Adamski}}</ref> On December 3, 2022, the Steelers officially placed Witherspoon on injured reserve due to his hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Varley |first=Teresa |date=December 3, 2022 |title=Steelers make roster moves |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-roster-moves-x9732 |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Steelers.com |archive-date=December 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205060647/https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-roster-moves-x9732 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He finished the 2022 season with 20 combined tackles (17 solo), two pass deflections, and an interception in 13 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ahkello Witherspoon 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/W/WithAh00.htm |access-date=2026-02-15 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On May 17, 2023, Witherspoon was released.<ref name="v755">{{cite web | last=Podell | first=Garrett | title=Steelers release Ahkello Witherspoon: Veteran CB let go in final year of two-year, $8 million deal | website=CBSSports.com | date=2023-05-17 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/steelers-release-ahkello-witherspoon-veteran-cb-let-go-in-final-year-of-two-year-8-million-deal/#:~:text=The%20former%20San%20Francisco%2049er,two%20seasons%20with%20the%20Steelers&text=The%20Pittsburgh%20Steelers%20have%20done,year-old%20cornerback%20Ahkello%20Witherspoon. | access-date=2024-12-20}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Rams===
On June 29, 2023, the [[Los Angeles Rams]] signed Witherspoon to a one-year, $1.08 million contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams agree to terms with CB Ahkello Witherspoon|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-agree-to-terms-with-cb-ahkello-witherspoon|author=Jackson, Stu|website=TheRams.com|date=June 29, 2023}}</ref> He recorded his first interception as a Ram in a loss to the [[2023 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]] on September 25.

On September 11, 2024, Witherspoon was signed to the Rams' practice squad after going unsigned during the offseason.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rams place WR Puka Nacua, OL Steve Avila and OL Joe Noteboom on Injured Reserve; sign OL Dylan McMahon and OL Geron Christian to active roster and CB Ahkello Witherspoon to practice squad|url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-place-puka-nacua-steve-avila-joe-noteboom-on-injured-reserve-sign-dylan-mcmahon-geron-christian-ahkello-witherspoon|author=Jackson, Stu|website=TheRams.com|date=September 11, 2024}}</ref> On October 22, the Rams promoted Witherspoon to their active roster and signed him to a one-year, $1.12 million contract.<ref name="e306">{{cite web | last=Vierra | first=Brock | title=Rams sign CB Ahkello Witherspoon to active roster, make 2 other moves | website=Rams Wire |publisher=USA Today| date=2024-10-23 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/2024/10/23/rams-sign-cb-ahkello-witherspoon-to-active-roster-make-2-other-moves/ | access-date=2024-12-20}}</ref> Witherspoon dove to catch a game-winning interception against [[Kyler Murray]] and the [[2024 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]] on December 28. Witherspoon's play sealed a key win for the Rams, as it helped them clinch the NFC West division crown.<ref>{{cite web |last=Kownack |first=Bobby |date=December 29, 2024 |title=Rams CB Ahkello Witherspoon on last-minute interception: 'Friendly reminder that the game's never over' |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rams-cb-ahkello-witherspoon-on-last-minute-interception-friendly-reminder-that-the-game-s-never-over |access-date=May 25, 2026 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref name="q920">{{cite web | last=Jackson | first=Stu | title=Rams clinch 2024 NFC West title | website=TheRams.com | date=2024-12-30 | url=https://www.therams.com/news/rams-clinch-2024-nfc-west-title-wild-card-playoff-tickets-sofi-stadium | access-date=2025-03-02}}</ref>

On March 19, 2025, it was announced that Witherspoon agreed to a one-year contract to return for his third season with the Rams.<ref>{{cite web|title=CB Ahkello Witherspoon re-signs for a 3rd season with the Los Angeles Rams|url=https://apnews.com/article/rams-ahkello-witherspoon-9c969c818a0671721f908031217189d7|author=Associated Press|website=apnews.com|date=March 19, 2025}}</ref> He started at cornerback in the Rams' first two games, but suffered a [[scapular fracture|broken scapula]] in Week 2 and was placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite web | last=Simmons | first=Myles | title=Rams place CB Ahkello Witherspoon on IR|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/rams-place-cb-ahkello-witherspoon-on-ir|department=Pro Football Talk|website=NBCSports.com|date=September 15, 2025}}</ref> Witherspoon was activated on November 29.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vierra |first=Brock  |date=November 29, 2025 |title=Rams Announce Massive Update on Ahkello Witherspoon |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/rams/onsi/los-angeles-announce-massive-update-ahkello-witherspoon |access-date=December 9, 2025 |website=si.com |language=en}}</ref> However, he re-broke his scapula during the Wild Card Round against the Panthers and was placed on season-ending injured reserve on January 12, 2026.<ref>{{cite web | last=DaSilva | first=Cameron | title=Rams injuries: Ahkello Witherspoon put on IR after re-breaking scapula | website=Rams Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=January 12, 2026 | url=https://theramswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/rams/2026/01/12/rams-injuries-ahkello-witherspoon-scapula-shoulder/88143379007/ | access-date=May 15, 2026}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
On March 26, 2026, Witherspoon signed a one-year contract with the [[Washington Commanders]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Skinner |first=Caleb |date=March 26, 2026 |title=Ahkello Witherspoon Reunites With Adam Peters After Signing With Commanders |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/commanders/onsi/news/commanders-sign-cornerback-ahkello-witherspoon-free-agency |access-date=May 15, 2026 |website=SI.com}}</ref>

'''Ahmad Thomas''' (born December 15, 1994) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) and [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma Sooners]].

==Professional career==
[[File:Semper Fidelis All-American Bowl East team practice, Day 1 130104-M-CT639-803.jpg|thumb|left|175px|Thomas covering [[Ryan Switzer]] at Semper Fidelis All-American Bowl practice in 2012]]
===Oakland Raiders===
Thomas was signed by the [[Oakland Raiders]] as an undrafted free agent on May 5, 2017, but was waived three days later.<ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders officially announce 17 undrafted free agent signings|url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2017/5/5/15561096/raiders-officially-announce-17-undrafted-free-agent-signings|website=SilverAndBlackPride.com|date=May 5, 2017|accessdate=December 15, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Raiders waive three to make room for three tryout players|url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2017/5/8/15586304/raiders-waive-three-to-make-room-for-three-tryout-players|website=SilverAndBlackPride.com|date=May 8, 2017|accessdate=December 15, 2018}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
On November 29, 2017, Thomas was signed to the [[Green Bay Packers]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers sign LB Ahmad Thomas to practice squad|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/green-bay-packers/article/green-bay-packers-sign-lb-ahmad-thomas-to-practice-squad--111380990/|website=247Sports.com|date=November 29, 2017|access-date=December 15, 2018}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the team on January 4, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Green Bay Packers sign LB Ahmad Thomas|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/green-bay-packers/article/green-bay-packers-sign-lb-ahmad-thomas-113221679/|website=247Sports.com|date=January 4, 2018|access-date=December 15, 2018}}</ref>

On September 1, 2018, Thomas was waived by the Packers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Packers announce roster moves |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-1|website=Packers.com|date=September 1, 2018|accessdate=December 15, 2018}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On September 3, 2018, Thomas was signed to the [[Indianapolis Colts]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Sign Free Agent Tight End Ryan Hewitt; Place Tyquan Lewis On IR|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-free-agent-tight-end-ryan-hewitt-place-tyquan-lewis-on-ir|author=Walker, Andrew|website=Colts.com|date=September 3, 2018|accessdate=December 15, 2018}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 14, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Move: Colts Elevate LB Ahmad Thomas To Active Roster|url=https://www.colts.com/news/roster-move-colts-elevate-lb-ahmad-thomas-to-active-roster|website=Colts.com|date=December 14, 2018|accessdate=December 15, 2018}}</ref>

Thomas was waived/injured during final roster cuts on August 31, 2019,<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts Announce Final 2019 Roster Cuts|url=https://www.colts.com/news/initial-2019-roster-cuts|author=Walker, Andrew|website=Colts.com|date=August 31, 2019|accessdate=September 11, 2019}}</ref> and reverted to the team's [[injured reserve]] list the next day. He was waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on September 11.

===Atlanta Falcons===
On October 1, 2019, Thomas was signed to the [[Atlanta Falcons]] practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign offensive lineman, linebacker to practice squad|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-offensive-lineman-linebacker-to-practice-squad|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=October 1, 2019}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 10, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons place Calvin Ridley, Desmond Trufant on IR|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-place-calvin-ridley-desmond-trufant-on-ir|author=McFadden, Will|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=December 10, 2019|access-date=December 12, 2019|archive-date=December 11, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211231428/https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-place-calvin-ridley-desmond-trufant-on-ir|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On August 5, 2020, Thomas was waived by the Falcons.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons activate Tyeler Davison from reserve/COVID-19 list, waive Ahmad Thomas|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-activate-tyeler-davison-from-reserve-covid-19-list-waive-ahmad-thomas|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=August 5, 2020}}</ref>

===Montreal Alouettes===
Thomas signed with the [[Montreal Alouettes]] on January 21, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Alouettes ink former NFL first rounder Datone Jones |url=https://en.montrealalouettes.com/2021/01/21/alouettes-ink-former-nfl-first-rounder-datone-jones/ |website=MontrealAlouettes.com |date=January 21, 2021 |access-date=February 22, 2021}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/suspended list on May 15, 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/teams/cfl/montreal-alouettes/transactions/2022 | title=Montreal Alouettes Transactions | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=13 August 2024}}</ref>

'''Ahmad Gooden''' (born October 27, 1995) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive end]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Samford Bulldogs football|Samford Bulldogs]].

==College career==
Gooden was a member of the [[Samford Bulldogs football|Samford Bulldogs]] for four seasons. As a junior, Gooden made 101 tackles (15.5 for loss) with 5.5 sacks and was named first-team All-[[Southern Conference]] (SoCon) and the conference Defensive Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/samford/2018/08/samfords_gooden_named_to_bucha.html|title=Samford's Gooden named to Buchanan Award watch list|website=[[AL.com]]|date=August 2, 2018|access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref> Gooden was named first-team All-SoCon as a senior after recording 49 tackles, 15 tackles for loss and 5.5 sacks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.annistonstar.com/the_daily_home/nfl-draft-talladega-native-ahmad-gooden-goes-undrafted-signs-with/article_a7f75f3a-696d-11e9-8417-3b421ea91880.html|title=NFL Draft: Talladega native Ahmad Gooden goes undrafted, signs with Broncos|first=LaVonte|last=Young|work=[[The Anniston Star]]|publisher=[[The Daily Home]]|date=April 27, 2019|access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref> He finished his collegiate career with 273 tackles, 22 sacks, five pass breakups, two forced fumbles and five fumble recoveries in 46 games played.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/11/22/broncos-release-orson-charles-promote-ahmad-gooden/|title=Broncos release Orson Charles, promote Ahmad Gooden|first=Charean|last=Williams|website=[[Profootballtalk.com]]|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=November 22, 2019|access-date=December 4, 2019}}</ref>

==Professional career==

web|url=https://247sports.com/nfl/denver-broncos/Article/Denver-Broncos-sign-17-undrafted-rookie-free-agents--131604235/|title=Broncos sign 17 college free agents following the 2019 draft|first=Chad|last=Jensen|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=April 30, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> He was waived at the end of training camp during final roster cuts, but was re-signed to the team's practice squad on September 1, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://broncoswire.usatoday.com/2019/09/01/denver-broncos-practice-squad-tracking-all-10-signings/|title=Broncos practice squad tracker: 10 players have signed|first=Jon|last=Heath|website=Broncos Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=September 1, 2019|access-date=December 3, 2019}}</ref> The Broncos promoted Gooden to the active roster on November 22, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/broncos-promote-ahmad-gooden-beef-pass-rush-221642930--nfl.html|title=Broncos promote Ahmad Gooden to beef up pass next day against the [[Buffalo Bills]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.al.com/sports/2019/11/samford-football-enjoying-its-nfl-golden-age.html|title=Samford football enjoying its NFL golden DL Deyon Sizer to active roster|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-dl-kyle-peko-promote-dl-deyon-sizer-to-active-roster|website=DenverBroncos.com|date=December 14, 2019}}</ref> Gooden '''Akeem Brian Davis-Gaither''' (born September 21, 1997) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He has previously played in the NFL for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] and [[Arizona Cardinals]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Appalachian State Mountaineers football|Appalachian State Mountaineers]].

==Early life==
Davis-Gaither attended Thomasville High School in [[Thomasville, North Carolina]]. As a senior in 2015, he had 115 tackles with five sacks and also had eight rushing touchdowns as a [[running back]]. He committed to [[Appalachian State University]] to play [[college football]].<ref>https://247sports.com/recruitment/akeem-davis-gaither-45911/recruitinterests/</ref>

==College career==
Davis-Gaither played at Appalachian State from 2015 to 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joyce  |first=Ethan |date=2024-06-24 |title=Akeem Davis-Gaither wondered if App State would be the right place for him. Now his patience is paying off |url=https://journalnow.com/sports/college/asu/akeem-davis-gaither-wondered-if-app-state-would-be-the-right-place-for-him-now/article_3359fe45-5dcb-5c75-9470-a24a2ac9ca26.html |access-date=2024-07-25 |website=Winston-Salem Journal}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Behr | first=Steve | title=Davis-Gaither gives App State power and quickness at LB | website=Watauga Democrat | date=2023-09-11 | url=https://www.wataugademocrat.com/sports/asu_sports/davis-gaither-gives-app-state-power-and-quickness-at-lb/article_be1b6890-5321-58ac-93c6-f2a6fbe78513.html | access-date=2024-07-25}}</ref> As a senior in 2019, he was the [[Sun Belt Conference]] Defensive Player of the Year after recording 101 tackles, five sacks and an interception.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.the-dispatch.com/sports/20191205/davis-gaither-thrilled-over-award|title=Davis-Gaither thrilled over award|first=Mike|last=Duprez|website=The Dispatch|access-date=March 17, 2020|archive-date=May 3, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200503164637/https://www.the-dispatch.com/sports/20191205/davis-gaither-thrilled-over-award|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Joyce| first=Ethan| title=No. 21 App State's Darrynton Evans, Akeem Davis-Gaither win Sun Belt offensive and defensive player of the year awards | website=Winston-Salem Journal | date=December 4, 2019 | url=https://journalnow.com/sports/college/asu/no-21-app-states-darrynton-evans-akeem-davis-gaither-win-sun-belt-offensive-and-defensive/article_eb5a66b0-140e-5734-bc14-2d90efee3c09.html | access-date=2025-09-29}}</ref> For his career, Davis-Gaither had 201 tackles, 6.5 sacks and the interception.<ref>[https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/nfl/carolina-panthers/article240259166.html How Appalachian State’s Davis-Gaither went from afterthought to a top LB in NFL Draft]</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
Davis-Gaither was selected by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] in the fourth round with the 107th pick of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Marcum |first1=Jason |title=Bengals select Akeem Davis-Gaither in Round 4 of 2020 NFL Draft |url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2020/4/25/21236186/bengals-picks-2020-nfl-draft-akeem-davis-gaither-appy-state |accessdate=April 27, 2020 |work=Cincy Jungle |date=April 25, 2020}}</ref>
In Week 17 against the [[Baltimore Ravens]], Davis-Gaither recorded his first career interception off a pass thrown by [[Lamar Jackson]] during the 38–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at Cincinnati Bengals - January 3rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202101030cin.htm |access-date=2021-01-03 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On November 9, 2021, Davis-Gaither was placed on injured reserve after suffering a foot injury in Week 9.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Make Four Roster Moves Ahead Of The Bye|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-make-four-roster-moves-ahead-of-the-bye|website=Bengals.com|date=November 9, 2021}}</ref>  In 2022, Davis recorded a career high 46 tackles and his first fumble recovery.  He also intercepted a pass in the Bengals wildcard playoff win against the Ravens.

On March 13, 2024, Davis-Gaither signed a one-year contract extension with the Bengals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Re-Sign Akeem Davis-Gaither|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-roster-moves-akeem-davis-gaither-re-signed-one-year-2024-season|website=Bengals.com|date=March 13, 2024}}</ref>

===Arizona Cardinals===
On March 13, 2025, Davis-Gaither signed with the [[Arizona Cardinals]] on a two-year, $11 million contract.<ref>{{cite web | last1=Root | first1=Jess | title=Arizona Cardinals announce signing of LB Akeem Davis-Gaither | website=Yahoo! Sports | date=2025-03-13 | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/arizona-cardinals-announce-signing-lb-225810072.html | access-date=2025-09-29}}</ref> He played in all 17 games for Arizona (including 13 starts), finishing second on the team with a career-high 117 tackles.

On March 6, 2026, Davis-Gaither was released by the Cardinals.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Urban |first1=Darren |title=Cardinals Release Akeem Davis-Gaither, Bilal Nichols |url=https://www.azcardinals.com/news/arizona-cardinals-release-akeem-davis-gaither-bilal-nichols |website=AZCardinals.com |access-date=6 March 2026}}</ref>

=== Indianapolis Colts ===
On March 18, 2026, Davis-Gaither signed a one-year, $2.725 million contract with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Colts sign free agent LB Akeem Davis-Gaither |url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-free-agent-lb-akeem-davis-gaither-cincinnati-bengals-lou-anarumo-appalachian-state-arizona-cardinals |access-date=2026-03-18 |website=Colts.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Aidan Joseph Bernardi Hutchinson'''<ref>{{Cite web |last=Vessels |first=Chandler |date=April 28, 2022 |title=WATCH: Aidan Hutchinson explains custom message inside suit jacket made by mom at NFL Draft |url=https://www.on3.com/news/aidan-hutchinson-explains-custom-inscriptions-suit-jacket-made-mom-2022-nfl-draft-michigan-wolverines/#:~:text=Aidan%20Joseph%20Bernardi%20Hutchinson |access-date=September 30, 2023 |website=on3.com}}</ref> (born August 9, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was a [[unanimous All-American]] playing [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]], and the runner-up for the [[Heisman Trophy]] in 2021. Hutchinson was selected with the [[List of second overall NFL draft picks|second overall pick]] by the Lions in the first round of the [[2022 NFL draft]], and named to the [[PFWA All-Rookie Team#2022|All-Rookie Team]]. He was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] in 2023 and 2025, and made his first [[All-Pro]] with a second-team selection in 2025.

==Early life==
Hutchinson was born on August 9, 2000, in [[Plymouth, Michigan]]. He attended [[Divine Child High School]] in [[Dearborn, Michigan]], where he played [[defensive end]], [[tight end]], [[offensive line]], and [[long snapper]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Goricki |first=David |date=August 22, 2017 |title=Detroit News top players: Hutchinson stands tall for Divine Child |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/08/22/aiden-hutchinson-stands-tall-divine-childs-line/104861708/ |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=Detroit News |archive-date=March 22, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190322083737/https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/08/22/aiden-hutchinson-stands-tall-divine-childs-line/104861708/ |url-status=live }}</ref> He played in the 2018 [[U.S. Army All-American Game]] and had two sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |date=September 25, 2017 |title=Four-star Michigan commit Aidan Hutchinson receives Army All-American Bowl jersey |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2017/four-star-michigan-commit-aidan-hutchinson-receives-army-all-american-bowl-jersey |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=USA Today |archive-date=December 9, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201209053736/https://usatodayhss.com/2017/four-star-michigan-commit-aidan-hutchinson-receives-army-all-american-bowl-jersey |url-status=live }}</ref> Hutchinson committed to play [[college football]] at the [[University of Michigan]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Snyder |first=Mark |date=February 21, 2017 |title=Divine Child four-star DE Aidan Hutchinson commits to Michigan |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2017/02/21/michigan-football-recruiting/98228706/ |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=Detroit Free Press |archive-date=September 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920055533/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2017/02/21/michigan-football-recruiting/98228706/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Hutchinson was selected in the first round with the [[List of second overall NFL draft picks|second overall]] pick by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the 2022 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twentyman |first=Tim |date=April 28, 2022 |title=Lions draft defensive end Aidan Hutchinson |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-draft-defensive-end-aidan-hutchinson |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=DetroitLions.com |archive-date=April 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429004307/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-draft-defensive-end-aidan-hutchinson |url-status=live }}</ref> He signed his four-year contract, worth $35.7 million fully guaranteed, on May 9, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birkett |first=Dave |date=May 9, 2022 |title=Detroit Lions sign first-round pick Aidan Hutchinson to guaranteed $35.7 million deal |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2022/05/09/detroit-lions-sign-first-round-pick-aidan-hutchinson-4-year-deal/9701549002/ |access-date=May 9, 2022 |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |archive-date=May 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220509142117/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2022/05/09/detroit-lions-sign-first-round-pick-aidan-hutchinson-4-year-deal/9701549002/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===2024===
Hutchinson was named NFC Defensive Player of the Month for September.<ref>{{cite web | last=Alper | first=Josh | title=Aidan Hutchinson named NFC defensive player of the month | website=NBC Sports | date=October 3, 2024 | url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/aidan-hutchinson-named-nfc-defensive-player-of-the-month | access-date=May 24, 2026}}</ref> On October 13, 2024, against the Dallas Cowboys in week 6, Hutchinson suffered a severe leg injury in the third quarter, fracturing both his [[tibia]] and [[fibula]]. He underwent immediate surgery, with head coach [[Dan Campbell]] estimating a recovery timetable of "four to six months."<ref>{{cite news |last=Woodyard |first=Eric |title=Lions' Campbell won't count out Hutchinson returning this season |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41796483/lions-campbell-count-hutchinson-returning-season |access-date=October 14, 2024 |work=ESPN |date=October 13, 2024}}</ref> Prior to the injury, Hutchinson had recorded a league-leading 7.5 sacks and 19 total tackles in five games.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jacob|last=Camenker|title=How long is Aidan Hutchinson out? Updated injury timeline for Lions DE|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2024/10/14/aidan-hutchinson-injury-update-lions-timeline/75670536007/|website=USA Today|date=October 14, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2024}}</ref> He was ranked 55th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2025]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2025-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2025===
The Lions picked up the fifth-year option on Hutchinson's contract; Hutchinson was set to earn nearly $20 million for the 2025 season.<ref>{{cite news |last=Patra|first=Kevin |title=Lions agree to terms with DE Aidan Hutchinson on four-year, $180M extension
|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/lions-aidan-hutchinson-four-year-extension |access-date=October 29, 2025 |work=NFL News|date=October 29, 2025}}</ref> On October 29, 2025, the Lions and Hutchinson agreed to a four-year contract extension for $180 million over four years, with $141 million in total guaranteed money.<ref name="Woodyard 2025">{{cite news |last=Woodyard |first=Eric |title=Lions, Aidan Hutchinson reach 4-year, $180M extension, agent says |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46770353/lions-aidan-hutchinson-reach-4-year-180m-extension-agent-says |access-date=October 29, 2025 |work=ESPN |date=October 29, 2025}}</ref> The contract set a new record for highest guaranteed money among non-quarterback players.<ref name="Woodyard 2025"/> He finished the 2025 season with 14.5 sacks, 54 total tackles (36 solo), one interception, three passes defended, four forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aidan Hutchinson 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/H/HutcAi00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-05-24 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He earned Pro Bowl honors for the second time in his career.<ref>{{cite web | last=DeYoung | first=Abigail | title=Meet the 6 Lions participating at 2026 Pro Bowl Games | website=Detroit Lions | date=January 31, 2026 | url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/meet-the-6-lions-participating-at-2026-pro-bowl-games-campbell-gibbs-hutchinson | access-date=May 24, 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
His father, [[Chris Hutchinson (American football)|Chris Hutchinson]], also played college football at Michigan. His mother, Melissa Sinkevics, won the 1988 [[Miss Michigan Teen USA]] event while his older sister, Aria, won [[Miss Michigan USA]] 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chengelis |first=Angelique S. |date=September 26, 2018 |title=Freshman DL Aidan Hutchinson living up to family name at UM |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/09/26/freshman-lineman-aidan-hutchinson-living-up-family-name-michigan-wolverines/1430758002/ |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=Detroit News |archive-date=August 15, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200815104358/https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/2018/09/26/freshman-lineman-aidan-hutchinson-living-up-family-name-michigan-wolverines/1430758002/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sang |first=Orion |date=August 27, 2020 |title=Michigan football DE Aidan Hutchinson's NFL draft decision: Here the factors to consider |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/08/27/michigan-football-aidan-hutchinson-big-ten/5648323002/ |access-date=September 30, 2020 |website=[[Detroit Free Press]] |archive-date=September 20, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200920043334/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2020/08/27/michigan-football-aidan-hutchinson-big-ten/5648323002/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

Hutchinson's great-grandfather, Giuseppe "Joseph" Bernardi, came from the town of [[Medeglia]] in [[Switzerland]]. '''Ainias Smith''' (born May 31, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Carolina Panthers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M Aggies]].

==Early life==
Smith grew up in [[Missouri City, Texas]] and attended [[John Foster Dulles High School]] in [[Sugar Land, Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Underwood |first=Hannah |date=December 14, 2020 |title=3 reasons why Texas A&M could be better in 2021, including a triple threat at running back |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/texas-am-aggies/2020/12/14/3-reasons-texas-am-could-be-better-in-2021-including-a-triple-threat-at-running-back/ |access-date=September 28, 2021 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref> In his high school career, he was a starter at wide receiver, running back, [[cornerback]], and occasionally [[free safety]].<ref name="aggieswire22">{{cite news |last1=Ohnysty |first1=Cameron |title=Texas A&M Player Profile: Wide receiver, Ainias Smith |url=https://aggieswire.usatoday.com/2022/06/25/texas-am-player-profile-wide-receiver-ainias-smith/ |access-date=6 January 2025 |work=Aggies Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]] |date=25 June 2022}}</ref> As a senior, he rushed for 481 yards and 10 touchdowns and caught 55 passes for 717 yards and 10 touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/texas-am/Article/Texas-AM-National-Signing-Day-2019-Ainias-Smith-127197385/|title=A&M adds speed, versatility to 2019 class in ATH Ainias Smith|first=Damon|last=Sayles|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=February 6, 2019|access-date=September 28, 2021}}</ref> Smith committed to play college football at Texas A&M over [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zwerneman |first=Brent  |date=February 6, 2019 |title=Texas A&M adds versatile player to 2019 signing class |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/aggies/article/Texas-A-M-Ainias-Smith-2019-signing-class-13594315.php |access-date=September 28, 2021 |website=[[Houston Chronicle]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://theeagle.com/aggie_sports/football/aggie-freshman-wide-receiver-ainias-smith-chose-texas-a-m-as-much-for-academics-as/article_0b62aeaa-d42e-5998-8810-eaf582bad693.html|title=Aggie freshman wide receiver Ainias Smith chose Texas A&M as much for academics as for football|first=Travis L.|last=Brown|work=[[The Bryan-College Station Eagle]]|date=November 16, 2019|access-date=September 28, 2021}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Smith played mostly wide receiver and served as the team's primary return specialist and had 22 receptions for 248 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 1, 2020 |title=Ainias Smith Brings Versatile Skill Set to A&M Backfield |url=https://www.fox44news.com/sports/texas-a-m/ainias-smith-brings-versatile-skill-set-to-am-backfield/ |access-date=May 5, 2021 |website=Fox44News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zwerneman |first=Brent  |date=October 22, 2019 |title=Aggies counting on happy returns from Ainias Smith |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/aggies/article/Aggies-counting-on-happy-returns-from-Ainias-Smith-14554766.php |access-date=September 28, 2021 |website=[[Houston Chronicle]]}}</ref> He played running back in the [[2019 Texas Bowl]] and rushed for 54 yards on seven carries in a 24-21 win over Oklahoma State.<ref>{{Cite web |last=O'Gara |first=Connor |date=2020-11-05 |title=Why Ainias Smith is the unique X-factor who suddenly has Texas A&M looking worthy of Playoff talk |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/tamu-football/is-texas-am-playoff-contender-ainias-smith-reason-why-question-even-being-asked-2020/ |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=Saturday Down South |language=en-US}}</ref> Smith was moved to running back before the start of his sophomore season, while remaining a flex option at wide receiver.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/tamu/football/ainias-smith-to-switch-positions-in-2020|title=Ainias Smith To Switch Positions in 2020|first=Cole|last=Thompson|website=[[SI.com]]|date=February 5, 2020|access-date=September 21, 2021}}</ref><ref name="aggieswire22" /> He finished the season with 293 yards and four touchdowns on 49 carries and also caught 43 passes for a team-leading 564 receiving yards with six touchdown receptions.

Smith was named to the watchlist for the Hornung Award going into his junior season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kagstv.com/article/sports/aggie-playmaker-ainias-smith-named-to-hornung-award-watch-list/499-2bd5a831-54c6-4d41-a91d-50f8b155c523|title=Aggie playmaker Ainias Smith named to Hornung Award watch list|website=KAGSTV.com|date=July 29, 2021|access-date=August 25, 2021}}</ref> That season, he was selected as a team captain and returned to a primarily wide receiver role, leading the team in receptions. In a win over #1 ranked Alabama, he recorded six receptions for 85 yards and two touchdowns.<ref name="aggieswire22" />

He was briefly suspended by the team in July 2022 due to a [[driving while intoxicated|DWI]] arrest, but was reinstated after the charges were dropped due to a lack of evidence.<ref name="nodwi">{{cite news |last1=Wilson |first1=Dave |title=Aggies' Smith won't face DWI, weapons charges |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/34314182/texas-wr-ainias-smith-face-dwi-weapons-charges-suspension-lifted |access-date=6 January 2025 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=29 July 2022 |language=en}}</ref> After starting the first four games of his senior season, he suffered a leg injury that ended his season.<ref name="12thmanfoundation">{{cite web |last1=Stanford |first1=Kiri |title=Ainias Smith '22 |url=https://12thmanfoundation.com/donor-impact/stories/ainias-smith-22/index.html |website=12th Man Foundation |publisher=[[Texas A&M Athletics]] |access-date=6 January 2025}}</ref><ref name="ambio">{{cite web |title=Ainias Smith - Football |url=https://12thman.com/sports/football/roster/ainias-smith/11579 |website=[[Texas A&M Athletics]] |access-date=6 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> Smith was granted a fifth year of eligibility due to the injury, qualifying as a [[medical redshirt]].<ref name="sitexasbowl">{{cite news |last1=Thompson |first1=Cole |title=Texas A&M Aggies WR Ainias Smith Declares For 2024 NFL Draft, Will Coach In Bowl Game |url=https://www.si.com/college/tamu/football/tamu-aggies-ainias-smith-declares-2024-nfl-draft-coach-texas-bowl |access-date=6 January 2025 |work=Texas A&M Aggies On SI |publisher=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=8 December 2023}}</ref>

On September 20, 2023, he earned SEC Special Teams Player of the Week honors after returning a punt 82 yards for a touchdown and recording a career-high 202 all-purpose yards against Arkansas, the team he was injured against the year prior.<ref name="12thmanfoundation" /> He ended his fifth year leading the Aggies in all-purpose yards (1,204), receiving yards (795), and punt return yards (285), earning him [[2023 All-SEC football team|first team All-SEC]] honors.<ref name="ambio" />

===Philadelphia Eagles===
Smith was selected by the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] with the 152nd pick in the fifth round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gowton |first=Brandon Lee |date=2024-04-27 |title=NFL Draft Results: Eagles pick Ainias Smith at No. 152 |url=https://www.bleedinggreennation.com/2024/4/27/24142672/nfl-draft-results-eagles-pick-anias-smith-no-152-wide-receiver-texas-am-wr-philadelphia |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=Bleeding Green Nation |language=en}}</ref> He was placed on injured reserve on August 27, 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Get your first look at the Eagles' initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-53-man-roster-2024-season-jalen-hurts-saquon-barkley |access-date=2024-11-07 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref> Smith was activated on October 26.<ref name="t559">{{cite web | last=McMullen | first=John | title=Eagles Activate Rookie WR | website=SI.com| date=2024-10-26 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/eagles/news/eagles-activate-rookie-wr-01jb57aygpg0 | access-date=2024-11-07}}</ref> Smith made his debut against the [[2024 Jacksonville Jaguars season|Jacksonville Jaguars]]; he caught one pass for no gain and rushed once for two yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ainias Smith 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SmitAi00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=2024-12-20 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> On January 5, 2025, in a Week 18 matchup against the [[2025 New York Giants season|New York Giants]], Smith caught the first touchdown of his NFL career on a pass from quarterback [[Tanner McKee]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=McManus |first1=Tim |title=Eagles' rookie WR Ainias Smith scores first TD vs. Giants |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/43297024/eagles-ainias-smith-first-career-td-tanner-mckee-new-york-giants |access-date=6 January 2025 |work=[[ESPN.com]] |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=6 January 2025 |language=en}}</ref> He won a Super Bowl championship when the Eagles defeated the [[2024 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] 40–22 in [[Super Bowl LIX]].<ref name="a252">{{cite web | last=Maaddi | first=Rob | title=Eagles deny the Chiefs a Super Bowl three-peat with dominant defense in a 40-22 rout | website=AP News | date=2025-02-10 | url=https://apnews.com/article/super-bowl-2025-eagles-chiefs-score-e2ff209c074a00a6faff39750ff048f8 | access-date=2025-02-17}}</ref>

On August 26, 2025, Smith was waived by the Eagles as part of final roster cuts.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 26, 2025 |title=Eagles announce their initial 53-man roster |url=https://www.philadelphiaeagles.com/news/eagles-announce-initial-53-man-roster-2025-season |access-date=27 August 2025 |website=PhiladelphiaEagles.com}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On August 28, 2025, Smith was signed to the [[Carolina Panthers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |author=Gantt |first=Darin |date=August 28, 2025 |title=Panthers add two more to practice squad |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-add-two-more-to-practice-squad-hendon-hooker-ainias-smith |access-date=September 22, 2025 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Carolina on January 12, 2026.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign 15 to future deals|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-15-to-future-deals-demani-richardson-maz-mwansa-ipp-england|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=January 12, 2026}}</ref>

Smith is the younger brother of NFL defensive back [[Maurice Smith (cornerback)|Maurice Smith]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilson |first=Aaron |date=August 28, 2018 |title=Football is a family affair for Dolphins' Maurice Smith, brother Ainias Smith |url=https://www.chron.com/sports/texans/article/Football-family-affair-Dolphins-Maurice-Smith-13187565.php |access-date=September 28, 2021 |website=[[Houston Chronicle]]}}</ref> On July 20, 2022, Smith was arrested into Brazos County, Texas on three charges: unlawful carrying of a weapon, [[driving while intoxicated]], and possession of marijuana.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rittenberg |first=Adam |author-link=Adam Rittenberg |date=July 20, 2022 |title=Texas A&M Aggies football player Ainias Smith arrested on DWI, weapon, marijuana charges |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/34271401/texas-aggies-football-player-ainias-smith-arrested-dwi-weapons-marijuana-charges |access-date=2024-06-23 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He was released the same day after posting $8,000 bail, and the charges were dropped 9 days later by the Brazos [[county attorney]] due to a lack of evidence.<ref name="nodwi" />

'''Aidan James O'Connell''' (born September 1, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]]  [[quarterback]] for the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue Boilermakers]] and was selected by the Raiders in the fourth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
O'Connell was born on September 1, 1998, and grew up in [[Long Grove, Illinois]].<ref name=bio>{{cite web|title=Aidan O'Connell biography|publisher=Purdue University Athletics|work=purduesports.com|access-date=March 5, 2023|url=https://purduesports.com/sports/football/roster/aidan-o-connell/11413}}</ref> O'Connell is the middle child of five brothers: Sean, Patrick, Liam, and Seamus. He also has one sister, Grace.

O'Connell played high school football and basketball for [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson High School]] in [[Lincolnshire, Illinois]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McGraw |first=Patricia Babcock  |date=October 6, 2016 |title=Daily Herald: Stevenson's 'O' vs. Lake Zurich's 'D' |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2016/10/6/18496959/daily-herald-stevenson-8217-s-8216-o-8217-vs-lake-zurich-8217-s-8216-d-8217 |access-date=March 6, 2023 |website=Chicago Sun-Times}}</ref> He was not a highly recruited Illinois high school athlete, as his only scholarship offer came from [[Davenport Panthers football|Davenport University]], a [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] school.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Narang |first=Bobby  |date=December 14, 2016 |title=Recruiting notes: Stevenson's Aidan O'Connell opts for college football |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/lake-county-news-sun/sports/ct-lns-football-notes-st-1215-20161214-story.html |access-date=March 6, 2023 |website=Chicago Tribune}}</ref> In 2016, his only season as a starter, he threw for a school record 2,741 yards and 26 [[touchdowns]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Reaven |first=Steve |date=March 6, 2017 |title=Purdue-bound QB Aidan O'Connell wraps up Stevenson athletic career |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/buffalo-grove/sports/ct-lsr-stevenson-waukegan-aidan-oconnell-tl-0309-20170306-story.html |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=Chicago Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McGraw |first=Patricia Babcock |date=September 15, 2016 |title=Stevenson's O'Connell making the most of his chance |url=https://football.dailyherald.com/article/20160915/sports/160919166/ |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=Football Focus}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:Aidan O'Connell (cropped).jpg|thumb|170px|O'Connell with Purdue during a game against the Michigan Wolverines in 2022]]
On February 3, 2017, O'Connell committed to play [[college football]] for [[Wheaton College (Illinois)|Wheaton College]],<ref name="carmin">{{Cite web |last=Carmin |first=Mike |date=November 8, 2019 |title=Aidan O'Connell's journey; Wheaton College commitment to Purdue's starting quarterback |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2019/11/08/aidan-oconnells-journey-wheaton-college-commitment-to-purdues-starting-quarterback/2524279001/ |access-date=March 6, 2023 |website=Lafayette Journal & Courier}}</ref> but less than a month later, he accepted a preferred walk-on spot with [[Purdue Boilermakers football|Purdue]].<ref name="carmin" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Narang |first=Bob |date=December 9, 2021 |title=Aidan O'Connell had no Division I scholarship offers coming out of Stevenson. But in his first season starting for Purdue, he has become one of the nation's top QBs. Is the NFL next? |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/suburbs/lake-county-news-sun/sports/ct-lns-cfb-oconnell-st-1210-20211209-pf5xabixubgnbmk5joswbqnxpe-story.html |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=Chicago Tribune}}</ref>

After not playing in 2017 and 2018, he played in six games in 2019 and started three. He made his first career start against Northwestern, completing 34 of 50 passes for 271 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Carmin |first=Mike |date=November 9, 2019 |title=Purdue, Aidan O'Connell produce more fourth-quarter magic at Northwestern |url=https://www.jconline.com/story/sports/2019/11/09/purdue-football-aidan-oconnell-produce-more-fourth-quarter-magic-at-northwestern/2532581001/ |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=Journal and Courier}}</ref> Overall that season, he completed 103 of 164 passes for 1,101 yards with eight touchdowns and four interceptions. O'Connell entered 2020 as the starter before suffering a season-ending injury after three games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rittenberg |first=Adam |date=December 4, 2020 |title=Purdue's O'Connell to have surgery; season over |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/30445785/purdue-aidan-oconnell-season-ending-surgery-foot |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He completed 88 of 136 passes for 916 yards with seven touchdowns and two interceptions. O'Connell entered 2021 as the backup to [[Jack Plummer]], but eventually took over as the starter and completed 315 of 440 passes for 3,712 yards with 28 touchdowns and 11 interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aidan O'Connell 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aidan-oconnell-1/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He decided to enter the [[2023 NFL draft]] after the 2022 season.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Fezler |first=D. J. |date=December 13, 2021 |title=Quarterback Aidan O'Connell Announces Decision to Return to Purdue Next Season |url=https://www.si.com/college/purdue/football/quarterback-aidan-oconnell-announces-decision-to-return-to-purdue-next-season |access-date=October 7, 2023 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> In the 2022 season, he passed for 3,490 yards, 22 touchdowns, and 13 interceptions to go with a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aidan O'Connell 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/aidan-oconnell-1/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=December 20, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2023 season===
O'Connell was drafted by the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] in the fourth round with the 135th pick of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edwards |first=Levi |date=April 29, 2023 |title=Raiders trade up to No. 135 to select QB Aidan O'Connell |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/aidan-o-connell-qb-purdue-raiders-trade-up-to-no-135-patriots |access-date=April 29, 2023 |website=Raiders.com}}</ref>

On October 1, 2023, O'Connell made his first career NFL start, filling in for an injured [[Jimmy Garoppolo]]. Playing against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], he went 24-of-39 for 238 yards and had his first career rushing touchdown on a goal-line sneak. The Raiders lost 24–17 in his debut.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Edwards |first=Levi |date=October 1, 2023 |title=What did rookie Aidan O'Connell learn in his first NFL start? |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/what-did-rookie-aidan-o-connell-learn-in-his-first-nfl-start-vs-chargers-week-4 |access-date=October 2, 2023 |website=Las Vegas Raiders |language=en-US}}</ref> On November 1, 2023, O'Connell was named the starting quarterback for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=November 1, 2023 |title=Aidan O'Connell will replace Jimmy Garoppolo as Raiders starting QB |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/aidan-oconnell-will-replace-jimmy-garoppolo-as-raiders-starting-qb |access-date=November 2, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 15, O'Connell threw four touchdown passes in a dominant 63–21 victory over the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Edwards |first=Levi |title=Quick Snap: Raiders put up franchise record 63 points against Chargers |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/quick-snap-raiders-put-up-franchise-record-63-points-against-chargers |access-date=November 29, 2024 |work=Raiders.com |date=December 14, 2023}}</ref> During the Week 16 [[NFL on Christmas Day|Christmas Day]] game against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], where despite his team winning 20–14, O'Connell went 9 of 21 in pass attempts for 62 yards, never completing a pass after the first quarter.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Skretta |first=Dave |date=December 25, 2023 |title=Raiders stun sloppy Chiefs with 2 defensive TDs in 20–14 victory on Christmas Day |url=https://news.yahoo.com/raiders-stun-sloppy-chiefs-2-211914570.html |access-date=December 25, 2023 |website=Yahoo! News |language=en-US}}</ref> O'Connell went 5–5 as a starter. He finished with 2,218 passing yards, 12 passing touchdowns and 7 interceptions to go with a rushing touchdown.<ref>{{cite web | title=Aidan O'Connell 2023 Game Log | website=[[Pro Football Reference]]  | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OConAi00/gamelog/2023/ | access-date=July 27, 2024}}</ref>

===2024 season===
Following a preseason quarterback competition with new free agent signing [[Gardner Minshew]], O'Connell was named a backup to begin the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 18, 2024 |title=Raiders name Gardner Minshew starting QB over Aidan O'Connell |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nfl/raiders-name-gardner-minshew-starting-qb-over-aidan-oconnell |access-date=August 25, 2024 |website=Fox Sports}}</ref> After the Raiders began the season with a 2–3 record, O'Connell was named the starter on October 9.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gutierrez |first=Paul |date=October 9, 2024 |title=Raiders benching Gardner Minshew, name Aidan O'Connell QB1 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41702492/raiders-benching-gardner-minshew-name-aidan-oconnell-qb1 |access-date=October 9, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> In his first start of the season, O'Connell passed for 227 yards, one touchdown, and one interception as the Raiders lost to the [[2024 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] 32–13. Against the [[Los Angeles Rams]] on October 20, O'Connell suffered a fractured thumb and was later placed on injured reserve.<ref>{{cite news |last=Shook |first=Nick |title=Raiders QB Aidan O'Connell out 4–6 weeks with fractured thumb, headed to injured reserve |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-qb-aidan-oconnell-out-4-6-weeks-fractured-thumb-injured-reserve |access-date=October 21, 2024 |work=NFL.com |date=October 21, 2024}}</ref> After missing four games, the Raiders activated O'Connell to the 53-man roster on November 28, ahead of the team's Week 13 matchup against the Chiefs.<ref>{{cite news |title=Raiders activate QB Aidan O'Connell, place CB Jakorian Bennett and QB Gardner Minshew on Reserve/Injured list |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-activate-qb-aidan-o-connell-place-cb-jakorian-bennett-qb-gardner-minshew-on-the-reserve-injured-list |access-date=November 28, 2024 |work=Raiders.com |date=November 28, 2024}}</ref> In his return from injury, O'Connell produced the first 300-yard performance of his career, finishing with 340 yards, two touchdowns, and zero interceptions, but miscommunication in the final minute resulted in a lost fumble as the Raiders lost 19–17.<ref>{{cite news |last=Skretta |first=Dave |title=Chiefs recover botched snap by Raiders in closing seconds, clinch playoff berth with 19–17 victory |url=https://apnews.com/article/raiders-chiefs-score-3570f241fd589939e3bbb28744e6aa06 |access-date=November 29, 2024 |work=Associated Press |date=November 29, 2024}}</ref> He sustained another injury in the team's Week 14 matchup against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as he suffered a bone bruise to his knee,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |title=Raiders Rumors: Aidan O'Connell's Knee Injury Diagnosed as Bone Bruise; Status TBD |url=https://nodereport.bleacherreport.com/articles/10146383-raiders-aidan-oconnell-carted-off-with-knee-injury-replaced-by-desmond-ridder#:~:text=Las%20Vegas%20Raiders%20quarterback%20Aidan,Jordan%20Schultz%20of%20Fox%20Sports. |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250427124644/https://nodereport.bleacherreport.com/articles/10146383-raiders-aidan-oconnell-carted-off-with-knee-injury-replaced-by-desmond-ridder#:~:text=Las%20Vegas%20Raiders%20quarterback%20Aidan,Jordan%20Schultz%20of%20Fox%20Sports. |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 27, 2025 |access-date=2025-01-14 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> before returning in Week 16 to end off the season with a record of 2–5.

===2025 season===
O'Connell suffered a fractured wrist in the Raiders' preseason finale against the [[2025 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]], and was placed on [[injured reserve list|injured reserve]] to begin the season as a result.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Raiders QB Aidan O'Connell suffered fractured wrist in  preseason finale, expected to be out 6-8 weeks|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/raiders-qb-aidan-o-connell-suffered-fractured-wrist-in-preseason-finale-expected-to-be-out-6-8-weeks|access-date=October 26, 2025|website=NFL.com|language=en}}</ref> He was activated on November 19, ahead of the team's Week 12 matchup against the [[2025 Cleveland Browns season|Cleveland Browns]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 19, 2025 |title=Raiders activate QB Aidan O'Connell from the Reserve/Injured list |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-activate-qb-aidan-o-connell-from-the-reserve-injured-list |access-date=November 19, 2025 |website=Raiders.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Serving as the team's third-string quarterback behind starter [[Geno Smith]] and backup [[Kenny Pickett]] throughout the year, O'Connell would make his sole 2025 season appearance during a Week 18 win against the Kansas City Chiefs, passing for 102 yards and marking the Raiders' first win against the Chiefs in [[Allegiant Stadium]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=4 January 2026 |title=Daniel Carlson hits 60-yard field goal to lift Raiders over Chiefs, 14-12 |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nfl/recap?gameId=401772957 |access-date=5 March 2026 |website=ESPN}}</ref>
