'''Akayleb Evans''' (born June 22, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Carolina Panthers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]] before transferring to the [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri Tigers]].

==Early life==
Evans grew up in [[McKinney, Texas]] and attended [[McKinney High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Emig |first=Guerin |date=January 26, 2019 |title='The bold one' -- TU cornerback Akayleb Evans has a voice. Now is the time we must hear it. |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sports/college/tu/guerin-emig-the-bold-one----tu-cornerback-akayleb-evans-has-a-voice/article_2a097da0-c862-52d9-981b-ee72746c232a.html |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Tulsa World]]}}</ref> As a senior, he recorded 48 tackles, five pass breakups, and one fumble recovery and was named second-team all-District 10-6A.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 31, 2017 |title=TU recruit gallery -- Akayleb Evans |url=https://tulsaworld.com/archive/tu-recruit-gallery----akayleb-evans/image_6d3e3cf9-9436-5167-99c7-d0cfae3051b0.html |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Tulsa World]]}}</ref> Evans initially committed to play [[college football]] at [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]], but later flipped his commitment to [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florek |first=Michael |date=July 21, 2016 |title=McKinney defensive back Akayleb Evans flips commitment from Kansas to Tulsa |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/2016/07/21/mckinney-defensive-back-akayleb-evans-flips-commitment-from-kansas-to-tulsa/ |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[The Dallas Morning News]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Evans began his collegiate career with the [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa Golden Hurricane]]. As a freshman, he played in nine games with five starts and had 26 tackles and two passes broken up.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hines |first=Kelly |date=August 26, 2018 |title=Maturity benefiting TU cornerback Akayleb Evans |url=https://tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/tusportsextra/maturity-benefiting-tu-cornerback-akayleb-evans/article_c4aa3784-ce99-5148-94e1-2a05c4bbe006.html |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Tulsa World]]}}</ref> Evans suffered a shoulder injury in the third game of his junior season and used a medical [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirt]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gabriel |first=Parker |date=May 15, 2021 |title=A graduate transfer pops onto the radar for Huskers at defensive back |url=https://journalstar.com/sports/huskers/recruiting/a-graduate-transfer-pops-onto-the-radar-for-huskers-at-defensive-back/article_c99f555c-7993-558d-9f6a-fecf426a142d.html |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Lincoln Journal Star]]}}</ref> He played in all nine of Tulsa's games during their COVID-19-shortened [[2020 NCAA Division I FBS football season|2020 season]] and finished the year with 30 tackles (27 solo tackles), one sack, three passes broken up, and one forced fumble.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Engel |first=Patrick |date=May 17, 2021 |title=Grad Transfer Corner Comes Onto Notre Dame's Radar, Picks Up Offer |url=https://notredame.rivals.com/news/grad-transfer-corner-comes-onto-notre-dame-s-radar-picks-up-offer |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref> After his redshirt junior season, Evans entered the transfer portal.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sampson |first=Pete |date=May 24, 2021 |title=Akayleb Evans has some Kyle Hamilton traits, but can Notre Dame beat out Texas, Missouri and more for him? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/2609308/2021/05/24/akayleb-evans-has-some-kyle-hamilton-traits-but-can-notre-dame-beat-out-texas-missouri-and-more-for-him/ |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[The Athletic]]}}</ref>

Evans transferred to [[Missouri Tigers football|Missouri]] as a graduate transfer.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Matter |first=Dave |date=June 12, 2021 |title=Mizzou bolsters secondary with Tulsa transfer Akayleb Evans |url=https://www.stltoday.com/sports/college/mizzou/mizzou-bolsters-secondary-with-tulsa-transfer-akayleb-evans/article_5b546971-12e2-540a-9f30-e92dc7a80161.html |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]}}</ref> He had considered offers from [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish football|Notre Dame]], [[Texas Longhorns football|Texas]], [[Texas Tech Red Raiders football|Texas Tech]], and [[Jackson State Tigers football|Jackson State]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Blum |first=Eric |date=August 13, 2021 |title=Tulsa defensive back transfers Akayleb Evans, Allie Green ===Minnesota Vikings===
Evans was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] with the 118th pick of the fourth round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Eric |date=April 30, 2022 |title=New Vikings CB Akayleb Evans Ready to Learn From Patrick Peterson |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/akayleb-evans-nfl-draft-cornerback-cornerback |access-date=April 30, 2022 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>  Evans entered his rookie season as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart behind [[Patrick Peterson]], [[Cameron Dantzler]], and [[Chandon Sullivan]]. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on December 7, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2022 |title=Vikings Place CB Akayleb Evans and TE Ben Ellefson on IR |url=https://www.vikings.com/news/akayleb-evans-ben-ellefson-ir-injured-reserve |access-date=April 7, 2023 |website=Vikings.com}}</ref>

On November 23, 2024, Evans was waived by the Vikings.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Florio |first=Mike |author-link=Mike Florio |date=November 23, 2024 |title=Vikings will waive CB Akayleb Evans |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/vikings-will-waive-cb-akayleb-evans |access-date=November 23, 2024 |website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On November 25, 2024, Evans was claimed off waivers by the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gantt |first=Darin |date=November 25, 2024 |title=Panthers claim cornerback off waivers |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-claim-cornerback-off-waivers-akayleb-evans |access-date=December 23, 2024 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref>

On March 11, 2026, Evans re-signed with the Panthers on a one-year contract.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gantt |first1=Darin |title=Panthers re-sign cornerback Akayleb Evans |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-re-sign-cornerback-akayleb-evans-free-agency-negotiating-period |website=panthers.com |access-date=12 March 2026}}</ref>

'''Aireontae Lamont Ersery''' ({{Respell|AIR|ee|on|tay ER|ser|ee}}; born February 19, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]] and was selected by the Texans in the second round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

== Early life ==
Ersery was born on February 19, 2002,{{cn|date=September 2025}} in [[Kansas City, Missouri]].<ref name="TheBeast">{{Cite web |last=Brugler |first=Dane |title=The Beast: 2025 NFL Draft Guide |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/the-beast/2025/player/aireontae_ersery-offensive_tackle-y6ZxZYPIj5fXletT/ |url-access=subscription |access-date=April 24, 2025 |website=[[The Athletic]] |publisher=[[The New York Times]] }}</ref> He grew up in the [[Ruskin Heights]] neighborhood of Kansas City.{{cn|date=September 2025}} He was raised by his mother, Takita Charles, alongside his five other siblings (Danny, Dean, Cherish, Journey, and Rain).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aireontae Ersery - Football |url=https://gophersports.com/sports/football/roster/aireontae-ersery/22044 |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=University of Minnesota Athletics |language=en}}</ref> During his childhood, Ersery’s family faced severe financial hardship, his mother worked 3 jobs to support Aireontae and his siblings, often facing threats of eviction. As a child, Ersery was resourceful, and often helped provide his family with [[water]] among other necessities.<ref>{{cite web  | title=A special story: Aireontae Ersery's journey to the Houston Texans | website= Houston Texans | date=2025-04-26 | url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/aireontae-ersery-journey-to-houston-texans | access-date=2025-07-21}}</ref> Ersery later attended [[Ruskin High School (Kansas City, Missouri)|Ruskin High School]].<ref name=TheBeast/> Originally, Ersery had his sights set on playing [[basketball]], but was drawn into [[American football|football]] through Ruskin High School football coach William Perkins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krammer |first=Andrew |date=2025-04-22 |title=Immense Gophers tackle Aireontae Ersery draws sizable NFL draft attention |url=https://www.startribune.com/aireontae-ersery-minnesota-gophers-football-offensive-tackle-nfl-draft/601336117 |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=StarTribune.com |language=en}}</ref> Ersery also participated in [[track and field]] and [[wrestling]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aireontae Ersery's Ruskin High School Bio |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/mo/kansas-city/ruskin-golden-eagles/athletes/aireontae-ersery/?careerid=jmcb41bbc1e00 |access-date=2025-06-16 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}}</ref> He was rated as a three-star [[College recruiting|recruit]] and committed to play [[college football]] for the [[Minnesota Golden Gophers football|Minnesota Golden Gophers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Engle |first1=Todd |title=A late-comer to football, no one's missing Ruskin High's future Golden Gopher anymore |url=https://www.kansascity.com/sports/high-school/article234259637.html |website=Kansas City Star |date=22 August 2019 |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ruane |first1=Blake |title=Minnesota Football Recruiting: Missouri OL Aireontae Ersery commits to the Gophers |url=https://www.thedailygopher.com/2019/6/16/18681000/minnesota-football-recruiting-2020-aireontae-ersery-offensive-tackle-missouri |website=The Daily Gopher |date=16 June 2019 |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref>

== College career ==
In Ersery's first two collegiate football seasons in 2020 and 2021, he played in two games, while making one start for Minnesota.<ref>{{cite web |title=Aireontae Ersery |url=https://gophersports.com/sports/football/roster/aireontae-ersery/22044 |website=Minnesota University Athletics |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref> In 2022, he started all 13 games for the Gophers, earning honorable mention all-[[Big Ten Conference]] recognition.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Randy |date=August 24, 2023 |title=Aireontae Ersery brings big personality, big talent to Gophers offensive line |url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-football-aireontae-ersery-nfl-draft-daniel-faalele-blaise-andrews/600299535/ |access-date=14 June 2024 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Randy |date=December 6, 2023 |title=Gophers tackle Aireontae Ersery announces he's returning for 2024 season |url=https://www.startribune.com/gophers-tackle-aireontae-ersery-announces-hes-returning-for-2024-season/600324689/ |access-date=14 June 2024 |website=Star Tribune}}</ref> In 2023, Ersery started all 13 games at left tackle for the Gophers and earned second-team all-Big 10 honors.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greder |first1=Andy |title=Gophers lineman Aireontae Ersery, a role model, with wit |url=https://www.twincities.com/2023/12/25/gophers-lineman-aireontae-ersery-is-a-role-model-with-a-wit/ |website=Pioneer Press |date=25 December 2023 |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Nelson |first1=Joe |title=Starting left tackle Aireontae Ersery returning to Gophers in 2024 |url=https://www.si.com/college/minnesota/football/starting-left-tackle-aireontae-ersery-returning-to-gophers-in-2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=5 December 2023 |access-date=14 June 2024}}</ref>

'''Aeneas Peebles''' (born September 3, 2001) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils football|Duke Blue Devils]] and [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech Hokies]]. Peebles was selected by the Ravens in the sixth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Peebles attended [[Knightdale High School]] in [[Knightdale, North Carolina]]. Over his junior and senior year in high school, he had a combined 195 tackles and 27 tackles. As a senior in 2019, he was the Northern Athletic 4A Defensive Player of the Year. Peebles committed to [[Duke University]] to play college football.

==College career==

access-date=2025-06-11}}</ref> During the four years he played in 47 games and had 87 tackles and 8.5 sacks.<ref>{{cite web | title=Peebles great addition from transfer portal – News Journal | website=Radford News Journal | date=2024-10-15 | url=https://radfordnewsjournal.com/peebles-great-addition-from-transfer-portal/ | access-date=2025-06-11}}</ref> After the 2023 season, he entered the [[transfer portal]] and transferred to [[Virginia Tech]] to play his final college season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Teel |first=David |date=2025-06-09 |title=Teel: All-ACC Duke transfer Aeneas Peebles a '''Ahmed Hassanein''' (born July 9, 2002) is an [[Egyptian Americans|Egyptian-American]] professional [[American football|football]] [[defensive end]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]] and was selected by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the sixth round of the [[2025 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Hassanein was born in the United States and moved to [[Egypt]] at age six to live with his father in [[Cairo]], where he participated in [[CrossFit]], wrestling, boxing, and swimming.<ref name="SI">{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/group-five/mountain-west/boise-state-football-ahmed-hassanein-embracing-both-egyptian-heritage-cowboy-toughness|title=Boise State Football: Ahmed Hassanein Embracing Both Egyptian Heritage & Cowboy Toughness|magazine=Sports Illustrated|first=Emily|last=Van Buskirk|date=November 7, 2024|access-date=November 30, 2024}}</ref><ref name="OCR">{{cite web |last1=Albano |first1=Dan |title=Football Signing Day: Loara's Ahmed Hassanein completes swift recruiting journey to sign with Boise State |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2020/12/16/loaras-ahmed-hassanein-completes-switft-recruiting-journey-to-sign-with-boise-state/ |website=Orange County Register |date=December 16, 2020 |access-date=November 30, 2024}}</ref> In 2018, he moved to [[Anaheim, California]], to live with his brother, a football coach who convinced him to try the sport.<ref name=SI/><ref name=OCR/> "My brother saved me,” Hassanein later said. "I was in Egypt acting one way and my life and personality changed. I’ve been grinding and working. I’m blessed."<ref name=OCR/>

Hassanein attended [[Loara High School]] in Anaheim, where he was rated a three-star [[College recruiting|recruit]]. On December 16, 2020, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play [[college football]] for the [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State Broncos]].<ref name=OCR/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Amundson |first1=Lynsey |title=Boise State football's recruit Ahmed Hassanein's journey from Egypt to Boise, "I didn't know anything about football" |url=https://www.kivitv.com/sports/boise-state-footballs-recruit-ahmed-hassaneins-journey-from-egypt-to-boise-i-didnt-know-anything-about-football |website=KITTV.com |date=December 18, 2020 |access-date=30 November 2024}}</ref>

==College career==
In his first two collegiate seasons in 2021 and 2022, Hassanein appeared in 21 games and notched 18 tackles with two being for a loss, two sacks, and a forced fumble.<ref name="college-sports-reference">{{cite web |title=Ahmed Hassanein |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ahmed-hassanein-1.html |website=Sports Reference |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title=A native of Egypt, this Boise State pass rusher rallied to put together 'special season' |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article282527508.html |website=Idaho Statesman |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Roberts |first1=Rachel |title='I'm the kid who came from Egypt.' Boise State defensive lineman finding his groove |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article278070952.html |website=Idaho Statesman |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref> He had a breakout season in 2023, notching 53 tackles with 17 being for a loss, 12.5 sacks, and two forced fumbles for the Broncos.<ref name=SI/><ref>{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title=Boise State's Hassanein wants to improve on gaudy sack numbers |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/latest-news/article290807019.html |website=Idaho Statesman |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref> Hassanein was named first-team [[2023 Mountain West Conference football season#All-conference teams|All-Mountain West Conference]] for 2023.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Counts |first1=Ron |title='I'm the same guy.' Boise State's standout pass rusher stays true to humble beginnings |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article290799664.html |website=Idaho Statesman |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref> Heading into the [[2024 Boise State Broncos football team|2024 season]], he was named one of the Broncos team captains.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wustrow |first1=John |title=With team-first mentality, Hassanein strives to deliver strong senior season to Boise State |url=https://www.idahopress.com/blueturfsports/football/with-team-first-mentality-hassanein-strives-to-deliver-strong-senior-season-to-boise-state/article_2059e9bc-4f86-11ef-97d1-cbe9c0958af4.html |website=Idaho Press |date=July 31, 2024 |access-date=November 30, 2024}}</ref> In week two of the 2024 season, Hassanein tallied a sack against [[2024 Oregon Ducks football team|Oregon]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Goodwin |first1=Shaun |title='My brothers are eating': Boise State's Hassanein puts teammate achievements above his own |url=https://www.idahostatesman.com/sports/college/mountain-west/boise-state-university/boise-state-football/article295886879.html |website=Idaho Statesman |access-date=November 29, 2024}}</ref> In his final collegiate game, the [[2024 Fiesta Bowl (December)|2024 Fiesta Bowl]] in the quarterfinals of the [[College Football Playoffs]], Hassanein made a sack and six tackles (three for loss). He finished the year with 48 total tackles, 16 tackles for loss, and 9.5 sacks, and was named first-team [[2024 Mountain West Conference football season#All-conference teams|All-Mountain West Conference]] again for his senior season.<ref name="college-sports-reference" /><ref>{{cite web |last=Lundeberg |first=Bob |website=Sports Illustrated |title=Boise State's Ahmed Hassanein accepts East-West Shrine Bowl invitation |date=December 27, 2024 |url=https://www.si.com/college/boise-state/football/boise-state-s-ahmed-hassanein-accepts-east-west-shrine-bowl-invitation-01jg586xdy6q |access-date=February 1, 2025}}</ref> On January 6, 2025, Hassanein declared for the [[2025 NFL draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Emplit |first=Kole |website=KMVT.com |title=Boise State's Ahmed Hassanein declares for NFL Draft |date=January 6, 2025 |url=https://www.kmvt.com/2025/01/06/boise-states-ahmed-hassanein-declares-nfl-draft/ |access-date=February 1, 2025}}</ref>

'''Aiden Williams''' (born August 31, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[Guard (gridiron football)|guard]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[University of Minnesota Duluth|UMD Bulldogs]].

==Early life==
At [[Bettye Davis East Anchorage High School|East Anchorage High School]], he started for two seasons in multiple roles, including tight end, defensive end, and long snapper, playing for head coach Jeff Trotter. In 2018, he repeated as a recipient of statewide and regional football honors from the Alaska Football Coaches Association, KTUU-TV, USA Today's Alaska list, and the Cook Inlet Conference. He also played four years on the varsity basketball team, contributing as a center and power forward. A National Honor Society student, he became the first athlete from Alaska to join the [[University of Minnesota Duluth|Bulldog]] football team.<ref name="h473">{{cite web | title=Aiden Williams | website=UMD Athletics | url=https://umdbulldogs.com/sports/football/roster/aiden-williams/7697 | access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
Williams [[redshirted]] in 2019. He did not play in 2020 due to the season being canceled by the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. In 2021, he appeared in five games. During the 2022 season, he played in 10 games and contributed to an offense that ranked in the national top 20 in time of possession, rushing offense, passing efficiency, and third down percentage. He was named to the All-NSIC Second Team Offense. In 2023, he again earned All-[[Northern Sun Intercollegiate Conference|NSIC]] Second Team Offense honors and was part of a rushing offense that led the NSIC and ranked seventh nationally, averaging 243.8 yards per game. He started every game through the 2024 season, during which, he received an invite to the [[East-West Shrine Bowl]].<ref name="h473" /><ref name="n378">{{cite web | last=Athletics | first=UMD | title=UMD Football's Aiden Williams Invited to 2025 East-West Shrine Bowl | website=UMD Athletics | date=October 30, 2024 | url=https://umdbulldogs.com/news/2024/10/30/umd-footballs-aiden-williams-invited-to-2025-east-west-shrine-bowl.aspx | access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
In the [[2025 NFL draft]], Williams went undrafted and was signed by the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]].<ref name="c946">{{cite web | last=Markowski | first=Jack | title=Steelers Sign Minnesota Duluth OL | website=Pittsburgh Steelers On SI | date=April 27, 2025 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/steelers/news/pittsburgh-steelers-sign-minnesota-duluth-aiden-williams | access-date=August 3, 2025}}</ref> He was waived on August 25.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make additional roster moves|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-additional-roster-moves-x1485|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=August 25, 2025}}</ref> Williams was re-signed to the practice squad on August 28 but waived on September 3.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Ward |first1=Chris |title=Steelers Part Ways with Promising Rookie Offensive Lineman |url=https://steelersnow.com/steelers-part-ways-with-promising-rookie-offensive-lineman/ |website=Steeler Now |access-date=4 September 2025}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On October 1, 2025, Williams signed with the [[Carolina Panthers]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rizzutti |first1=Anthony |title=Panthers announce roster moves involving 9 players on Wednesday |url=https://pantherswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/panthers/2025/10/01/panthers-roster-moves-week-5/86458798007/ |website=Panthers Wire |access-date=2 October 2025}}</ref> He was released on October 7.

===Pittsburgh Steelers (second stint)===
On January 14, 2026, Williams signed a reserve/futures contract with the Pittsburgh Steelers.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varley |first1=Teresa |title=Steelers sign 13 to Reserve/Future contracts |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-sign-13-to-reserve-future-contracts-x5578 |website=Steelers.com |access-date=15 January 2026}}</ref> He was released on June 11.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Varley |first1=Teresa |date=June 11, 2026 |title=Steelers make several roster moves |url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-several-roster-moves |access-date=12 June 2026 |website=Steelers.com}}</ref>

'''Ajani Carter''' (born August 17, 2000) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Houston Texans]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Houston Cougars football|Houston Cougars]] and [[Utah State Aggies football|Utah State Aggies]].

== Early life ==
Carter attended [[North Shore Senior High School (Texas)|North Shore Senior High School]] in [[Houston|Houston, Texas]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Straka |first=Dean |date=April 17, 2023 |title=Utah State football CB Ajani Carter, converted WR, enters NCAA transfer portal |url=https://247sports.com/article/utah-state-football-cb-ajani-carter-converted-wr-enters-ncaa-transfer-portal-208529826/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=247Sports |language=en}}</ref> In December 2018, he caught the [[Hail Mary pass]] that sent North Shore past [[Duncanville High School|Duncanville]] to win the Class 6A Division I state championship. Carter was a three-star recruit and received offers from [[Indiana Hoosiers football|Indiana]], Utah State, [[Southern Miss Golden Eagles football|Southern Miss]], and others. He chose to commit to Utah State.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Ajani Carter, Utah State Aggies, Cornerback |url=https://247sports.com/player/ajani-carter-46053392/ |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

== College career ==

=== Utah State ===
Carter played at Utah State from 2019 to 2022. For the first two years, he played as a [[wide receiver]] before converting to a defensive back. In the span of four years, he totaled 108 tackles, two sacks, four interceptions, three forced fumbles, and one fumble recovery.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Ajani Carter College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ajani-carter-1.html |access-date=November 21, 2025 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> At the end of the season, Carter entered the transfer portal.<ref name=":0" />

=== Houston ===
Carter initially committed to [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]] but flipped to Houston.<ref name=":1" /> In the 2024 season, Carter played 11 games and totaled 22 tackles, 0.5 sacks, and three pass breakups.<ref name=":2" />

==Professional career==
===Kansas City Chiefs===
Carter went unselected in the [[2025 NFL draft]]. On August 1, 2025, Carter signed with the [[Kansas City Chiefs]] as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chiefs signed two DBs, one WR before training camp practice on Friday|url=https://chiefswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/chiefs/2025/08/01/chiefs-sign-ajani-carter-azizi-hearn-keyshawn-smith-training-camp/85476084007/|access-date=November 19, 2025|website=chiefswire.usatoday.com|language=en}}</ref> He was waived by Kansas City as part of the team's final roster cuts on August 26.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chiefs Announce Roster Moves Heading Into 2025 NFL Season|url=https://www.chiefs.com/news/chiefs-announce-roster-moves-heading-into-2025-nfl-season|access-date=November 19, 2025|website=Chiefs.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Houston Texans===
On September 17, 2025, the [[Houston Texans]] signed Carter to their [[practice squad]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Former Chiefs CB Signs to Texans' Practice Squad|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/texans/onsi/news/former-kansas-city-chiefs-cb-ajani-carter-signs-houston-texans|access-date=November 19, 2025|website=si.com|language=en}}</ref> On November 15, the Texans added Carter to their roster as a standard gameday practice squad elevation.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (11-15-2025)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-11-15-2025|access-date=November 19, 2025|website=HoustonTexans.com|language=en}}</ref> He made his NFL debut the next day against the [[2025 Tennessee Titans season|Tennessee Titans]], playing 20 snaps on special teams.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ajani Carter (DB): Bio, News, Stats & more |url=https://www.houstontexans.com/team/players-roster/ajani-carter/ |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=HoustonTexans.com |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Ajani Carter - Houston Texans Cornerback |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4429379/ajani-carter |access-date=2025-11-16 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> Carter was signed to Houston's active roster on November 20.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Texans waive RB Dameon Pierce|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/texans-waive-rb-dameon-pierce|access-date=November 20, 2025|website=nbcsports.com|language=en}}</ref> He would make one more appearance for the Texans, logging 16 special teams snaps against the [[2025 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]] in Week 12. On November 29, Carter was placed on [[injured reserve list|injured reserve]] due to a hamstring injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Koch |first=Jared  |date=November 29, 2025 |title=Texans Announce Rookie CB Placed on Injured Reserve |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/texans/onsi/news/houston-texans-announce-rookie-cb-ajani-carter-injured-reserve |access-date=December 7, 2025 |website=si.com |language=en}}</ref>

On May 21, 2026, Carter was waived by the Texans with an injury designation.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 21, 2026 |title=Ajani Carter: Waived with injury tag |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/ajani-carter-waived-with-injury-tag/ |access-date=22 May 2026 |website=CBSSports.com}}</ref>
